| Container | Status, ports, start time, image pull policy, restarts, image, container id, environment variables, volume mounts (read-only or read-write), command, arguments, liveness, readiness, and startup probes, resource requests and limits |
| Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet | Available and total pods, ready and total replicas, selector, container images from the pod template, update strategy (StatefulSet) |
| DaemonSet | Selector, images, update strategy. Replica counts may be blank. |
| Service | Service type, cluster IP, external IP, selector, load balancer ingress addresses, the remaining spec as an expandable tree |
| Ingress | Rule hosts, the rules as an expandable tree, load balancer addresses |
| PersistentVolume | Capacity, claim, claim namespace, access modes, storage class |
| PersistentVolumeClaim | Requested size, storage class, access modes |
| Namespace | Phase and finalizers |
| Secret, ConfigMap | Secret type. Secret values are not rendered. |
| Event and all other kinds | The fields under All kinds only |

Container environment variables show their plain values. Values drawn from another source appear as `source(apiVersion: fieldPath)`.

### Labels and annotations

Labels render as `key=value` chips in the Details view. Selecting a chip toggles that label in the open view's `labels` filter and the chip turns green. The filter matches resources carrying any selected label, and the view autosaves. Annotations are listed without actions.

### Deep links

A resource that references a Node, Namespace, or ServiceAccount shows a link for each. Selecting one replaces the view's `kinds` filter with that kind and sets the name search to the value, keeping other filters. Use it to walk from a failing pod to the node it landed on.

## Node capacity gauges

For a Node, three gauges show how much of the node's capacity Kubernetes holds back from Pods.

| Gauge title | Resource |
|---|---|
| `System Reserved Cpu` | CPU |
| `Memory Usage` | Memory |
| `Disk Usage` | Ephemeral storage |

Each value is `(capacity - allocatable) / capacity` as a percentage, rounded to two decimals, using the node's reported `capacity` and `allocatable`. The gauge color follows the value:

| Value | Color |
|---|---|
| 0 to 30 percent | Teal-green |
| Over 30 to 60 percent | Amber |
| Over 60 to 90 percent | Orange |
| Over 90 percent | Red |

{{< alert type="note" title="Reserved capacity, not utilization" >}}
Despite the titles <code>Memory Usage</code> and <code>Disk Usage</code>, these gauges show reserved capacity, the share of the node unavailable to Pods. They do not show what Pods request or consume. Operator mode shows no live CPU or memory utilization, no per-pod metrics, and no time series. Use your metrics stack for those. Memory and storage parsing assumes the node reports values in `Ki` units.
{{< /alert >}}

## Actions

The panel header carries these actions. The same actions are in the canvas right-click menu, except **Open Source Design** and **Download**.

| Action | Offered on | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `Initiate Terminal Session` | Pod, Container | Opens shells. See [Open an Interactive Terminal]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/operating/interactive-terminal/index.md" >}}). |
| `Initiate Log Session` | Pod, Container | Streams logs. See [Stream Container Logs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/operating/log-streaming/index.md" >}}). |
| `Initiate Performance Test` | Service, Ingress | Opens the load test form. See [Run a Performance Test]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/operating/performance-testing/index.md" >}}). |
| `Open In Design` | Resources deployed from a design | Opens the source design in Designer with this component focused. |
| `Open Source Design` | Resources deployed from a design | Opens the source design. |
| `Download` | All kinds | Saves the resource record as indented JSON. The file name is the resource name with no `.json` extension. |

A resource counts as deployed from a design when it carries the design identity label that Meshery adds at deploy time. Resources created outside Meshery have no such label and do not offer the design actions. The header also shows **Expand** and **Collapse** buttons for every kind; they currently render without an icon.

## Events

Kubernetes `Event` objects appear on the canvas when you enable **Events** under **Monitoring** in the Layers panel. It is a plain kind toggle, grouped with the autoscalers. Selecting an event shows the generic fields only. Because events are short-lived and numerous, filter to a namespace first.

## Secrets

The panel does not render Secret values. The stored values still reach your browser: Meshery keeps the Secret and ConfigMap data MeshSync discovers and returns it with the resource, and **Download** writes it to the JSON file. Treat downloaded files as sensitive, and restrict who can use Operator mode against clusters whose Secrets matter.

## Related

- [Operator Views]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/views/index.md" >}}) save the filters you build with labels and deep links.
- [Kubernetes events and the Layers panel]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/layout-and-layers/index.md" >}}) describes the Layers panel in both modes.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Supported Import and Export Formats"
url: /kanvas/reference/supported-formats/index.md
description: Every file format Kanvas accepts on import and produces on export, with detection rules, limits, and what each format keeps.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This page lists exactly what Kanvas accepts and produces. For the steps, see [Import and Merge Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/import-designs/index.md" >}}) and [Export Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/export-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Import

Kanvas accepts the extensions `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.json`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.gz`, and `.zip`. Detection is by content and takes the first match in the order below.

| Order | Format | Extensions | Detected when | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Meshery design | `.yml` `.yaml` `.json` | The schema version is a supported design version | Lossless round trip of a design file export |
| 1 | Meshery design as OCI image | `.tar` `.tgz` `.tar.gz` `.zip` | The archive's layers contain a design file | Only the first design is taken. Other layer files are ignored. No design file means failure. |
| 2 | Kubernetes manifest | `.yml` `.yaml` | One or more valid Kubernetes documents | Multi-document files work. Unknown kinds are kept as generic objects. |
| 3 | Helm chart | `.tgz` `.tar.gz` `.gz` `.tar` `.zip` | A valid packaged chart | An uncompressed `.tar` is reported as needing gzip. No values overrides. |
| 4 | Docker Compose | `.yml` `.yaml` | Converts as a Compose file | The result is Kubernetes components. |
| 5 | Kustomize | `.yml` `.yaml` (kustomization), or an archive containing `kustomization.yaml` | The project builds | Archive must contain every referenced file. |

If nothing matches, the import fails and lists why each format was rejected. The interface shows only the generic failure message.

### Import sources

| Source | Supported | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| Local file in the import dialog | Yes | One file at a time. No size limit in the client. |
| Single-file http or https URL in the import dialog | Yes | 16 MiB body, 5 redirects, 10 second connect, 30 second request. Internal addresses are refused. |
| Drag or paste on the canvas | Yes | One design per file. Images and `.txt` files become canvas objects, limited to 500 KB on every plan. |
| Catalog clone or open | Yes | Public or published designs only. |
| Files and folders in a repository connected through the GitHub integration | Yes | One private design per valid file. |
| Git clone URL, Helm repository URL, `oci://` reference, directory, or pasted text | No | |
| RAR and 7Z archives | No | The drop check lets them through and the import fails. |

## Export

| Output | Keeps layout, annotations, metadata | Re-importable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design file (YAML) | Yes | Yes, lossless | Downloads as `<design name>.yml`. |
| Design (OCI image) | Yes | Yes | Archive of an OCI image. Push it with a registry tool. |
| Kubernetes manifest | No | Resources only | Plain Kubernetes YAML. |
| Helm chart | No | Resources only | `.tar.gz` chart archive. |
| Embeddable JavaScript module | Canvas snapshot | No | Static snapshot for web pages. See [Embed Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/embedding-designs/index.md" >}}). |
| View as JSON | Not applicable | No | Operator mode only. Downloads as `<view name>.json`. |

The canvas screenshot (a PNG picture, not a design file) is a separate action. See [Canvas Actions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-actions/index.md" >}}). Not available: Docker Compose export, SVG image export, export of an earlier version, and per-format export options. The catalog's light and dark snapshot images are produced by an automated workflow after publishing and are not user exports.

## Format by operation

| Format | Import | Export |
|---|---|---|
| Meshery design (YAML or JSON) | Yes | Yes (YAML) |
| Meshery design (OCI image) | Yes | Yes |
| Kubernetes manifest | Yes | Yes |
| Helm chart | Yes | Yes |
| Docker Compose | Yes | No |
| Kustomize | Yes | No |
| JavaScript embed | No | Yes |


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "URL Parameters"
url: /kanvas/reference/url-parameters/index.md
description: Every query parameter Kanvas reads from its address - which design or view to open, how to draw it, and which viewport to restore - with accepted values, defaults and how parameters combine.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kanvas reads its starting state from the query string of its address. A link can open a specific design, open Operator on a view, choose how much detail the canvas draws, and restore a zoom and pan position. The links produced by the Share dialog and by Copy Link are built from these parameters.

Append parameters to the Kanvas route of the Meshery you are using. On the hosted app that route is `https://kanvas.new/extension/meshmap`; on the Meshery Playground or a self-hosted Meshery it is `/extension/meshmap` on that host.

```
https://kanvas.new/extension/meshmap?mode=design&design=<design-id>&render=wireframe
```

## What to open

| Parameters | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mode=design&design=<design-id>` | Opens the design in Designer. This is the form the Share dialog produces. `name=<design-name>` is optional. |
| `mode=design&type=design&id=<design-id>&name=<design-name>` | Opens the design. An older form that Kanvas still accepts. |
| `mode=design&type=catalog&id=<catalog-id>&name=<name>` | Clones the catalog design into the opener's workspace and opens the copy. |
| `catalog-design=<catalog-id>` | Opens the catalog dialog focused on that design. |
| `mode=operator` | Opens Operator. |
| `mode=operator&type=view&id=<view-id>&name=<view-name>` | Opens Operator on a saved view. |
| `mode=operator&type=view&design_id=<design-id>&design_name=<design-name>` | Opens Operator on a view scoped to a design. |

A link to a private design opens only for people who can read the design. For anyone else the load fails with the message "Failed to render design", followed by the reason. Public designs open for anonymous visitors. See [Collaboration Model]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/collaboration/index.md" >}}) for who can read what.

## How to draw it

| Parameter | Values | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `full`, `medium`, `wireframe`, `view-only` | `full` | Sets the render mode when the canvas loads. |
| `adaptive` | `true` | off | Turns on Adaptive mode when the canvas loads. |

- **Spell the `render` value exactly.** The accepted value for the read-only mode is `view-only`, with a hyphen. Kanvas does not validate the value, and behavior with any other value is unsupported - for example, [auto-pan]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/autopan.md" >}}) stays off.
- **Full is the default.** A link with no `render` parameter opens in Full, which already draws TagSets, badges and animations. Add `render` to draw less, not to draw more.
- **`adaptive=true` always starts with a Full ceiling.** Adaptive mode may never exceed its ceiling, and a link cannot set it. Combine the two parameters and `render` sets the starting mode while the ceiling stays Full. Choose a different ceiling in the render mode switcher after the canvas loads.
- **Both parameters survive navigation inside Kanvas.** Kanvas keeps them in the address when it rewrites it, for example when it changes the mode or the open design.
- **Neither parameter is stored.** Render mode is session state. It is not saved in the design, not shared with collaborators, and not remembered the next time you open Kanvas without the parameter.

What each mode draws, and what Adaptive mode measures, is on [Performance Limits]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/performance.md" >}}). The reasoning behind the modes is in [Render Modes]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/render-modes/index.md" >}}).

## Where to restore the view

| Parameter | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewport` | An encoded zoom and pan position | Restores that zoom and pan on load. Copy Link adds it so the person who opens the link sees the same region you were looking at. |

The value is produced by Kanvas. Copy it from a link rather than writing it by hand.

## Common links

| Goal | Link |
| --- | --- |
| Open a large design without waiting for badges and overlays | `...?mode=design&design=<id>&render=wireframe` |
| Open a design for review and let Kanvas manage fidelity | `...?mode=design&design=<id>&adaptive=true` |
| Share a design that nobody should edit by accident | `...?mode=design&design=<id>&render=view-only` |
| Give a reader a catalog design as a starting point | `...?mode=design&type=catalog&id=<catalog-id>&name=<name>` |

{{< alert type="note" title="View-only is a display choice, not an access control" >}}
`render=view-only` locks the components on the canvas for that session. It does not change who may edit the design. Anyone with edit access can switch the mode back. Control who can edit with [design access]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/collaboration/index.md" >}}).
{{< /alert >}}


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Auto-pan on Drag"
url: /kanvas/reference/autopan/index.md
description: Reference for the Auto-pan on Drag setting - what triggers it, its default, where it is stored, the design size at which Kanvas turns it off for each render mode, and how it recovers.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Auto-pan on Drag** scrolls the canvas for you while you drag a component toward the edge of the view. Without it, moving a component to a part of the design that is off screen takes a drag, a manual pan, and another drag. With it, one continuous drag carries the component there.

Auto-pan is **off by default**. You turn it on as a personal setting, and Kanvas still switches it off while a design is too large for the current [render mode]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/render-modes/index.md" >}}).

## Behavior

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Off |
| Scope | Per user. The setting is stored in your Kanvas preferences on the server and follows you across browsers and devices. It is not stored in the design and is not shared with collaborators. |
| Trigger | Dragging a component to within 50 pixels of the edge of the visible canvas. |
| Pan speed | Fixed. It is not configurable. |
| Acts on | Component drags. |
| Applies in | Designer. The setting is listed with the Designer canvas settings in the Options dialog. |
| Takes effect | Immediately. Changing the setting needs no reload and no reopened design. |

{{< alert type="warning" title="Check where the component lands" >}}
Auto-pan ships off because, while it is on, panning during a drag can move the dragged component lower than you intended. Review the final position after a long drag, and turn the setting off if components drift. Undo (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd>) restores the previous position.
{{< /alert >}}

## When Kanvas turns it off

Every pan moves the whole canvas, and every layer that depends on the viewport redraws with it: the grid, badges, overlays and the drawing surface. The work grows with the number of components and relationships, so auto-pan on a large design makes dragging lag instead of helping it.

Kanvas therefore allows auto-pan only while **both** the number of components and the number of relationships drawn on the canvas are at or below a limit set by the render mode:

| Render mode | Auto-pan limit (components and relationships) |
| --- | ---: |
| Full | 100 |
| Medium | 500 |
| Wireframe | 1,000 |
| View-only | 1,000 |

The limit rises as the mode draws less, because fewer layers redraw on each pan.

Auto-pan runs only when your setting is on **and** the design is within the limit for the current mode. Kanvas re-checks this continuously:

- **The design grows past the limit.** Pasting a large group, importing a fragment, or receiving a collaborator's bulk change turns auto-pan off. Kanvas checks once per animation frame, so a burst of changes causes one decision, not many.
- **The design shrinks under the limit.** Deleting components turns auto-pan back on.
- **You change the render mode.** Moving from Full to Wireframe raises the limit from 100 to 1,000, so a design that blocked auto-pan in Full can allow it in Wireframe.
- **You change the setting.** The change applies at once.

Nothing on the canvas shows that auto-pan has been turned off by size. If it is on in your settings but does not scroll at the edge, count the components and relationships against the table for your current mode.

## Regain auto-pan on a large design

1. Switch to a lower-fidelity [render mode]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/performance.md" >}}). Wireframe and View-only allow 1,000.
2. Reduce what draws. Hiding layers in the [Layers panel]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/layout-and-layers/index.md" >}}) takes their components and relationships off the canvas, which lowers the counts Kanvas compares against the limit. Deleting components does the same.
3. Split the design. A design that regularly passes the limit of the mode you prefer is a candidate for several smaller designs.

## Known discrepancies

- The setting's description in the Options dialog says auto-pan is disabled "outside Full render mode". Kanvas does not behave that way: it allows auto-pan in Medium, Wireframe and View-only within the limits above.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Performance Limits"
url: /kanvas/reference/performance/index.md
description: Reference for what each render mode draws, the design sizes and zoom levels at which Kanvas gates features, how Adaptive mode decides to change modes, the enforced limits on a design, and what to adjust when a design feels slow.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kanvas draws a design on a canvas and redraws it on every pan, zoom and edit. The cost grows with the number of components and relationships and with how much detail each one carries. Kanvas controls that cost in four ways: the **render mode** you choose, **gates** that turn expensive features off past a design size or below a zoom level, **Adaptive mode**, which changes the render mode for you, and a small number of **enforced limits**.

For the reasoning behind render modes, see [Render Modes]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/render-modes/index.md" >}}).

## What each render mode draws

Switching render mode never changes the design. Components, relationships, configuration and layers stay as they are. Only what Kanvas draws changes. Full is the default.

| Drawn element | Full | Medium | Wireframe | View-only |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Component images | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Gradient fills | Yes | No | No | No |
| Relationship styling (color, curves, arrow style) | Yes | Yes | No. Thin, straight, light gray lines | Yes |
| TagSets | Yes | No | No | No |
| Expand and collapse badges | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Compound-component, label and external-link badges | Yes | No | No | No |
| Validation and dry-run error badges | Yes | No | No | No |
| Managed-by-Meshery and terminal-session badges (Operator) | Yes | No | No | No |
| Text-box content | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Animation when a component is added | Yes | No | No | No |
| Animated layouts | Yes, on designs within the limit below | No | No | No |
| Editing and selecting on the canvas | Yes | Yes | Yes | No. Components are locked and take no pointer input |

Layer visibility from the [Layers panel]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/layout-and-layers/index.md" >}}) applies in every mode. A layer you hide stays hidden.

Render mode applies to Designer and Operator alike, and to the whole canvas at once. It is session state: it is not saved in the design, not shared with collaborators and not remembered across sessions. Set it from the render mode switcher, which appears in the Options dialog and in the Designer toolbar, or from the `render` [URL parameter]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/url-parameters.md" >}}).

## Size and zoom gates

A gate turns a feature off while a condition holds and turns it back on when the condition clears. Kanvas re-checks gates as the design changes, as you change render mode, and as you zoom, so you never reload to recover a feature.

| Feature | Gate | Applies in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Auto-pan on Drag]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/autopan.md" >}}) | Needs your setting on, and at most 100 components and 100 relationships drawn in Full, 500 in Medium, 1,000 in Wireframe and View-only | Designer |
| Animated layout | Full mode only, and only while the design has no more than 50 components, no more than 50 relationships and no more than 100 edges drawn. Past that, a layout still applies its positions, without the animation | Designer |
| TagSets | Full mode only, and at most 30 drawn. Past 30, Kanvas skips the rest and shows the warning "Skipped rendering of N matchlabels relationships due to limit of 30" | Designer |
| Feasibility evaluation | Zoom above 0.5 divided by the display pixel ratio. That is 0.5 on a standard display and 0.25 on a display with a pixel ratio of 2 | Every mode |
| Component style toolbar | The same zoom threshold | Every mode |

TagSets are the only relationship type with a rendering limit. See [TagSets]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/tagsets/index.md" >}}).

## Adaptive mode

Adaptive mode lowers the render mode when the canvas becomes slow and raises it again when the canvas recovers.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Turn on | The Adaptive switch in the render mode switcher, or `adaptive=true` in the URL |
| Default | Off |
| Ladder | Full, Medium, Wireframe. View-only is never entered or left automatically |
| Ceiling | The highest mode Adaptive may use. It starts at Full. While Adaptive is on, the switcher shows the ceiling, labeled AUTO, not the mode currently in use |
| Signal | How long the canvas takes to produce the next frame after each pan or zoom, taken as the 95th percentile of the last 20 samples |
| Idle cost | None. Kanvas samples only when you pan or zoom |
| Step down | When the 95th percentile exceeds 80 ms. After a step down, Kanvas ignores samples for 3 seconds |
| Step up | When the 95th percentile stays under 30 ms for 10 consecutive samples, more than 5 seconds after the last change, and the next mode is not above the ceiling |
| Notification | "Switched to *mode* mode for better performance" on a step down. "Performance improved - switched to *mode* mode" on a step up |

Behavior to plan around:

- **Turning Adaptive on sets the canvas to the ceiling at once.** With the default ceiling, that is Full.
- **Recovery is one step.** After a step down, Adaptive recovers at most one step on its own. It steps down again if the canvas slows again, and it does not climb further until then. To return to a higher mode, turn Adaptive off and choose the mode.
- **A new ceiling applies the next time you turn Adaptive on.** Choosing a ceiling in the switcher while Adaptive is already on updates the label but does not change the running behavior. Turn Adaptive off and on to apply it.
- **Turning Adaptive off keeps the current mode.** The canvas stays in whichever mode Adaptive last chose, and manual selection resumes.
- **The thresholds are fixed.** You cannot set them per user or per design.

## Enforced limits

| Limit | Value | Where it is enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Components per design | Set by the organization's plan: 100, 200, 100 and 300 for Personal, Team Designer, Team Operator and Enterprise | Layer5 Cloud, when a design is saved or imported. See [Components per design]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/designs/index.md" >}}) |
| Image or text file added to a design | 512,000 bytes (about 500 KB) each, the same on every plan | The Kanvas canvas, when a file is dropped, pasted or uploaded. Images are embedded in the design, so each one adds to its size |
| TagSets drawn | 30 | The canvas, as described above |
| Canvas zoom | Minimum 0.1 (adjustable from 0.1 to 5), maximum 30 (adjustable from 0.1 to 30) | The Options dialog. Each person sets their own |

Kanvas enforces no cap on the number of relationships in a design or on how many images it holds. Large designs and embedded images still enlarge what Kanvas saves and synchronizes with collaborators, so loading, saving and live editing slow down as a design grows.

## What to change when a design is slow

Work from the cheapest change to the most disruptive.

| If | Then |
| --- | --- |
| Panning and zooming feel heavy | Switch to Medium, or turn on Adaptive. Switch to Wireframe for a layout pass on a very large design |
| Dragging a component to the edge does not scroll | Count components and relationships against the [auto-pan limit]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/autopan.md" >}}) for your mode |
| Only part of the design matters right now | Hide the layers you do not need in the Layers panel. Hidden components and relationships come off the canvas, and the design keeps them |
| TagSets are missing | Check the mode is Full, the TagSets layer is on, and the design has no more than 30 |
| The design saves slowly or collaboration lags | Remove unused embedded images, and prefer SVG or WebP images over PNG, JPEG and GIF files |
| The design keeps outgrowing the mode you prefer | Split it into several designs |
| Screenshots or demos need a steady picture | Turn Adaptive off and choose Full, so the mode cannot change mid-capture |

## Experimental WebGL renderer

Kanvas can draw the canvas with WebGL instead of the standard 2D canvas. It is an advanced option for diagnosing rendering, off by default, and available only from the Debug Mode panel, which appears when **Enable Debugger** is on in the Options dialog.

- **Scope.** The choice is stored in your browser, not your account, and applies the next time a canvas loads. Reload after changing it.
- **Trade-offs.** The WebGL path draws dashed and dotted relationship lines as solid lines, draws every arrowhead as a triangle, and does not hide labels at low zoom.
- **Fallback.** Above a zoom of 7.99 Kanvas draws with the standard canvas. After a browser loses its WebGL context, Kanvas uses the standard canvas for the rest of the browser session.
- **Browser support.** The panel reports when the browser does not support WebGL 2.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Help and Support"
url: /kanvas/reference/help-and-support/index.md
description: What the Kanvas Help Center offers, which support channel each plan includes, and the two preconditions the support form requires - a remote provider and a signed-in identity.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kanvas gives you two ways to get help without leaving the canvas: the **Help Center**, a single place for documentation, learning material and community channels, and the **support form**, which sends a request to the Layer5 team. This page lists what each one contains, which support channels each plan includes, and the conditions the support form needs to work.

## Help Center

The Help Center is a dialog with eight entries. Open it from the canvas context menu or from the help control in the whiteboard dock. It also opens from the **Get Help** action in the [troubleshooting]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/troubleshooting.md" >}}) panel.

| Entry | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| Documentation | These docs, opened in a new tab. |
| Video Tutorials | The Layer5 video library, opened in a new tab. |
| Quick Tips | An in-app tour of the core Kanvas workflow: placing and configuring components, connecting and grouping them, loading and combining designs, sharing, validating, deploying and undeploying, and collaborating. In Operator mode it covers filtering the resources under observation, health and details, quick operations, performance tests, the terminal and log streaming. |
| Academy | Structured learning paths in Layer5 Cloud, opened in a new tab. |
| Discussion Forum | The community forum at [discuss.layer5.io](https://discuss.layer5.io). |
| Slack | The Layer5 community Slack at [slack.layer5.io](https://slack.layer5.io). |
| Keyboard Shortcuts | A side panel listing shortcuts for Designer and Operator modes. The full list is in [Keyboard Shortcuts]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md" >}}). |
| Support | Opens the support form described below. |

The Help Center footer shows the installed Kanvas version and links to that version's release notes.

## Support channels by plan

Every plan includes community support. Standard and Premium support add direct contact with the Layer5 team. The table below is rendered from the product feature list and updates with it.

{{< feature-tiers categories="Support and Deployment" functions="Community Support|Standard Support|Premium Support" >}}

For the channels themselves, see [Layer5 Cloud support]({{< ref "cloud/reference/support.md" >}}).

## How a support request is delivered

A support request never leaves your browser for a third party. Kanvas submits the form to Meshery Server, which forwards it to your provider's support intake:

```text
Kanvas (browser)  ->  Meshery Server extension proxy  ->  Remote provider support webhook
```

For [Layer5 Cloud]({{< ref "cloud/_index.md" >}}) that intake is Layer5's support queue, the same one the Layer5 Cloud Help and Support form uses, so a request raised from Kanvas is triaged exactly like one raised from Layer5 Cloud. For a self-hosted Layer5 Cloud deployment it is whatever endpoint the operator has configured - see [Customizing Webhooks]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/customizing-webhooks.md" >}}).

## Requirements

### A remote provider

Because the submission travels through Meshery Server's extension proxy, the support form only works when Meshery is connected to a [remote provider](https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/providers). Under the **local** provider, Meshery Server has no support intake to forward to, and the extension proxy returns `501 Not Implemented`. This matches every other provider-bound Kanvas capability, including [sharing]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/collaborating/sharing-designs/index.md" >}}), the catalog and views.

If the form fails under the local provider, switch Meshery to a remote provider and submit again. If you cannot switch, reach the Layer5 team through the [community forum](https://discuss.layer5.io) or [Slack](https://slack.layer5.io).

### A signed-in identity

Every request carries the requester's name and email so the team can reply. Kanvas resolves your signed-in profile when you open the form instead of asking you to retype it:

- While the profile loads, the dialog shows a loading state and the form is unavailable.
- When the profile resolves, the form appears addressed with your identity.
- When the profile cannot be resolved, for example because the session expired, the form does not appear and nothing is submitted. A request with no way to reply has no value.

If the form does not appear, sign in to your provider again and reopen it. If it still does not appear, see [Troubleshooting Kanvas]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/troubleshooting.md" >}}).

## Type of inquiry

Each request carries a type that the support intake uses to route it.

| Type | Default |
|---|---|
| Support | Yes |
| Community | No |
| Account | No |
| Commercial | No |

If a submission fails, Kanvas keeps your subject, description and type so you can retry without retyping them.

## What You Will See

- **Three tool modes.** Default mode selects, moves, and configures; Pencil mode draws freeform notes without connecting components; Connector mode (<kbd>Command</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd>) draws annotation edges that explain relationships and flow. See [Understanding Tool Modes]({{< ref "kanvas/designer/understanding-tool-modes/index.md" >}}).
- **Shapes.** A warning shape dropped from the shapes palette, then switched to a different outline without rebuilding it. See [Working with Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/designer/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}).
- **Annotation edges.** The request flow traced with edges, then styled with a dashed line, arrowheads, and the marching ants animation. See [Whiteboarding]({{< ref "kanvas/designer/whiteboarding/index.md" >}}).
- **Styling is not configuration.** Fill, borders, text, edges, and animation change how the design looks, never how it is configured.
- **Evidence on the canvas.** A Grafana panel image and the runbook text placed beside the affected path, so the metric, the guidance, and the architecture share one frame.
- **The fix, made in the design.** A connection-pool setting raised in the component's configuration, then validated and deployed. See [Configuring Components]({{< ref "kanvas/designer/configuring-components/index.md" >}}), [Validating Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/tasks/designs/validating-designs/index.md" >}}), and [Deploying Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/tasks/designs/deploying-designs/index.md" >}}).
- **Annotations as a layer.** Hide the annotations and the infrastructure stays; show them again and the context is intact. See [Layout and Layers]({{< ref "kanvas/designer/layout-and-layers/index.md" >}}).
- **Real-time collaboration.** Every cursor and every edit stays visible to the whole team. See [Collaborative Editing]({{< ref "kanvas/tutorials/collaborative-editing.md" >}}).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Layer5 Cloud Documentation"
url: /cloud/index.md
description: What Layer5 Cloud does for Kanvas and Meshery, what it leaves to Meshery Server, and where to start.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Layer5 Cloud is the identity, tenancy, and collaboration service behind Kanvas and Meshery. It signs users in, organizes them into organizations, teams, and workspaces, decides what each of them may do, and stores the designs they create and share. Layer5 Cloud runs as a hosted service and as a [self-hosted]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/_index.md" >}}) deployment.

{{% pageinfo %}}

## Understanding the Layer5 Ecosystem

{{< ecosystem-box icon="cloud" title="Layer5 Cloud" >}}
is the identity provider and remote provider for Kanvas and Meshery. It owns accounts, organizations, teams, workspaces, roles, and the catalog, and it stores every design and design version. It is available as a hosted service or self-hosted.
{{< /ecosystem-box >}}

{{< ecosystem-box link="kanvas/_index.md" icon="images/logos/kanvas-icon-color.svg" image="true" class="hidden-highlight-box" title="Kanvas" >}}
is a visual designer and operator for Kubernetes and multi-cloud infrastructure. It runs as an extension inside Meshery and uses Layer5 Cloud to store, share, and publish designs.
{{< /ecosystem-box >}}

{{% /pageinfo %}}

## What Layer5 Cloud does

**Sign-in and identity.** Users create an account with an email address and password, with GitHub, or with Google. An organization that configures its own identity providers, including a generic OIDC provider, offers those instead. A signed-in user can link a GitHub or Google account to an existing profile, so either method signs in to the same profile. Email sign-ups verify their address before password sign-in works.

**Tenancy.** Organizations own teams and workspaces. A team belongs to the organization it is created in, a workspace can hold any number of teams, and a team can belong to several workspaces. At first sign-in, every new user receives a default organization, team, and workspace: they hold the Organization Admin role on the organization, the Team Admin role on the team, and own the workspace, so they can start working immediately.

**Authorization.** Roles, keys, and keychains decide what each user may do. A key is a single permission, a keychain groups keys, and a role carries keychains. Users hold roles within an organization, so the same person can have different permissions in different organizations. Built-in roles cover the provider, organization, team, and workspace levels, and organization admins invite users and assign their roles. See [Identity and Security]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/_index.md" >}}).

**Design storage and sharing for Kanvas.** Layer5 Cloud persists every Kanvas design and every version of it, records who each design is shared with, and keeps the event log. A design belongs to at most one workspace at a time. Real-time collaboration in Kanvas starts with a signaling service that Layer5 Cloud hosts; after participants connect, edits synchronize directly between their browsers.

**The catalog.** The [catalog]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/catalog/_index.md" >}}) publishes reusable designs. Anyone can browse it. A signed-in user with the right permission can clone a published or public design into their own workspace, download it, or open it in Kanvas on the [Meshery Playground](https://playground.meshery.io).

**Remote provider for Meshery Server.** Meshery Server connects to Layer5 Cloud as its remote provider. Users sign in to Meshery through Layer5 Cloud, Meshery Server registers itself as a connection owned by the signed-in user, and Layer5 Cloud returns a capabilities document that tells Meshery which features to enable for that user. Every new user holds the Kanvas role, which enables the Kanvas extension when their Meshery Server connects.

**Academy.** [Academy]({{< ref "cloud/academy/_index.md" >}}) delivers learning paths, challenges, and certifications, and gives content creators the tools to build and publish their own.

## What Layer5 Cloud does not do

- **It does not deploy to or manage your clusters.** Meshery Server, running in your environment, talks to your Kubernetes clusters through Meshery Operator and MeshSync, and performs every dry-run, deploy, and undeploy.
- **It does not run Kanvas.** Kanvas is an extension that runs inside Meshery. Kanvas sends its requests to Meshery Server, which forwards design, catalog, and sharing requests to Layer5 Cloud. Real-time collaboration signaling is the only direct path from the browser to Layer5 Cloud.

[How Layer5 Cloud works]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/architecture/index.md" >}}) explains these boundaries in depth, and [How Kanvas Works with Meshery and Layer5 Cloud]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/architecture/index.md" >}}) covers them from the Kanvas side.

## Choose your path

| Section | Go here to |
|---|---|
| [Getting Started]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/_index.md" >}}) | Create an account and learn what Layer5 Cloud sets up for you at first sign-in. |
| [Tutorials]({{< ref "cloud/tutorials/_index.md" >}}) | Work through end-to-end examples that build a working mental model. |
| [How-to Guides]({{< ref "cloud/guides/_index.md" >}}) | Complete a specific task: manage organizations and workspaces, connect integrations, or self-host. |
| [Concepts]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/_index.md" >}}) | Understand organizations, teams, workspaces, roles, the catalog, and how they relate. |
| [Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/_index.md" >}}) | Look up default permissions by role and the API. |
| [Academy]({{< ref "cloud/academy/_index.md" >}}) | Take learning paths and certifications, or create and publish your own content. |

To design infrastructure with what Layer5 Cloud stores, go to the [Kanvas documentation]({{< ref "kanvas/_index.md" >}}).

## What each plan includes

The following matrix shows which Layer5 Cloud capabilities each subscription plan includes. For default permissions by role, see the [Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/_index.md" >}}) section.
