| Organization Management | Managing organizations, their teams, and their users. |
| Events Management | Event management: statistics, audit, and summaries. |
| Security Management | Creating, downloading, and deleting API tokens, and managing credentials. Key and keychain management belongs to Provider Management. See the [Security Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md#permission-keys" >}}). |

Layer5 Cloud also ships keychains for workspaces, environments, the catalog, lifecycle actions, extensions, settings, performance, views, collaboration, infrastructure, curation, the Academy, and the two Kanvas action sets (Designer Actions and Operator Actions). For keychain behavior, see [Keychains]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}).

## What the matrices do not show

- **Canvas editing.** The permission list omits the per-edit Kanvas permissions, such as adding, deleting, and styling components. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}) for which Kanvas actions check a permission.
- **Provider Admin.** It holds every permission, including permissions that are not in the list.
- **Plan limits.** A role grants a permission, and the plan decides whether the capability exists for the organization. See [Feature Availability by Plan]({{< ref "cloud/reference/feature-availability.md" >}}).

## Custom roles

A custom role bundles keychains that the default roles do not combine. Only a Provider Admin can create, edit, or delete a custom role. On hosted Layer5 Cloud, Layer5 operates the Provider Admin role, so an organization cannot create custom roles itself. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator's Provider Admins can.

Roles and keychains are defined for the whole Layer5 Cloud deployment, not per organization. Only a Provider Admin can create, edit, or delete a keychain, change its keys, or assign a keychain to a role. Changing the keychains of a role changes that role for every organization that uses it. See [Roles]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Review and Sign Out Sessions"
url: /cloud/guides/security/sessions/index.md
description: See every active sign-in on your account and end the ones you do not recognize or no longer use.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every sign-in to Layer5 Cloud creates a session, on every browser, device, and Meshery Server you use. This guide reviews your sessions and ends the ones you do not want. For how long sessions last and what a session can reach, read the [Sessions concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/sessions.md" >}}).

## Before you start

- You need the **View Sessions** permission to open the Sessions tab. Every default user role holds it.
- Ending another session from the tab requires the **Delete Token** permission, which Organization Admin and Provider Admin hold by default. Other roles see the Logout control disabled. This is how the interface works today.
- You can end only your own sessions.

## Review your sessions

Open the Sessions tab under Security. Each row is one sign-in and shows its ID, name, purpose, and creation date. Search filters by name or purpose, and the newest sessions appear first.

The list shows no device or location. Use the creation date to judge which sessions you started and which you did not. A creation date you cannot account for means someone else signed in with your credentials.

## End a session

Choose Logout on the row and confirm. The session ends at once: the next request that carries its credentials fails. A confirmation reads `Token "<name>" deleted`, because a session is stored as a token.

The deleted session cannot be restored. Whoever used it must sign in again.

## If you suspect your account is compromised

1. End every session you do not recognize.
2. Change your password. Changing the password does not end other sessions, so complete step 1 first and check the list again afterward.
3. Review your [API tokens]({{< ref "cloud/guides/security/api-tokens.md" >}}) and revoke any you did not create. Tokens never expire and are not sessions, so signing out does not revoke them.
4. If you cannot sign in, ask an Organization Admin or Provider Admin to help recover the account.

Layer5 Cloud has no "sign out everywhere" action. End each session from the list.

## What ends a session without your action

A session also ends when its access token expires, 24 hours after sign-in by default. See the [Security Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md#session-and-token-lifetimes" >}}) for the lifetimes.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Set Up Your Organization"
url: /cloud/getting-started/setting-up-your-organization/index.md
description: Invite a teammate, create a team and a workspace, and move a design into that workspace to learn how organizations, teams, and workspaces control access.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An organization becomes useful when more than one person works in it. In this tutorial you invite a teammate by email, create a team, create a workspace, give the team that workspace, and move one of your designs into it. By the end you know which object controls what: the organization decides who is in, teams group people, and workspaces decide which shared resources those people reach.

## Before you begin

- You have a Layer5 Cloud account. If not, follow [Create Your Layer5 Account]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/getting-started-with-layer5-account.md" >}}).
- You work in **My Organization**, the organization Layer5 Cloud created for you, where you hold the Organization Admin role. Any organization where your role grants the permissions below works the same way.
- You own at least one design. If you do not, clone one first with [Start from a Catalog Design]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/creating-a-design-from-template.md" >}}).

Each step in this tutorial needs a specific permission. The table shows which built-in roles hold each one:

{{< keys-matrix caption="Permissions used in this tutorial" functions="Invite User to Organization|Create Team|Add User to Team|Create Workspace|Assign team to workspace|Assign Designs to Workspaces" >}}

## 1. Invite a teammate by email

Invite your teammate to the organization by email address. Your teammate does not need a Layer5 Cloud account first. An email invitation does all of the following at once:

- Creates a pending account for the address.
- Adds that account to the organization, and to any teams you choose.
- Assigns the organization and team roles you choose.
- Sends an invitation email that names you, the organization, and the teams. Its sign-up link pre-fills your teammate's name and address and carries your organization's identifier.

Layer5 Cloud refuses two kinds of invitation:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The address already belongs to a Layer5 Cloud account | Refused with HTTP 409 ("invite existing user"). |
| No email address given | Refused with HTTP 400 ("email is required"). |

To bring in someone who already has an account, share your organization's open invitation link instead. Layer5 Cloud accepts that link on every sign-in, not only the first. See [Using the open organization invitation link]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/org-management/_index.md#using-the-open-organization-invitation-link" >}}).

## 2. Create a team

Create a team for the people who will share the workspace you build next. A new team belongs to the organization you create it in.

Creating a team and adding people to it are separate actions. Once the team exists, add your teammate to it. When you invite more people later, you can choose this team in the invitation so they join it directly.

## 3. Create a workspace

Create a workspace in the same organization. A workspace groups shared resources such as environments, connections, credentials, and designs. Your **My Workspace** stays as it is; the new workspace is where you and your team collaborate.

## 4. Assign the team to the workspace

Assign your new team to the new workspace. Assignment is its own action, separate from creating either object. The relationship is many-to-many:

- A workspace has zero or more teams.
- A team can be assigned to several workspaces.

This is how you share access to a workspace's resources: through the teams assigned to it, not person by person.

## 5. Move a design into the workspace

Assign one of your designs to the new workspace. You can assign only designs you own.

Assigning a design moves it. A design belongs to at most one workspace, so assigning it to the new workspace removes it from the workspace it was in before, such as **My Workspace**.

## How the pieces fit together

| Object | What it controls | What you did with it |
|---|---|---|
| Organization | Who is a member at all. Teams and workspaces belong to one organization. | Invited a teammate into **My Organization**. |
| Team | A named group of organization members, each with a team role. | Created a team and added your teammate. |
| Workspace | A set of shared resources, reached by the teams assigned to it. | Created a workspace and assigned the team to it. |
| Design | A resource that lives in at most one workspace. | Moved a design you own into the workspace. |

Roles determine what each person may do at each level, as the permission table above shows for the actions in this tutorial.

## Check your result

Your organization is set up when all of the following are true:

- Your teammate's account appears in the organization.
- The new team lists your teammate.
- The new workspace lists the new team.
- The design you moved appears in the new workspace and no longer appears in its previous workspace.

## Go deeper

- [Organizations]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/organizations/_index.md" >}}): organizations as the unit of tenancy.
- [Teams]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/teams/_index.md" >}}): how teams group users.
- [Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/workspaces.md" >}}): what a workspace holds and how it is shared.
- [Organization management]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/org-management/_index.md" >}}): editing your organization and managing invitations.
- [Managing workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/guides/workspaces/managing-workspaces/index.md" >}}): editing, deleting, and organizing workspaces.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Security Reference"
url: /cloud/reference/security/index.md
description: Security permission keys and who holds them, session and token lifetimes, cookies, visibility rules, and the endpoints behind keys, keychains, tokens, and sessions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This page states how keys, keychains, tokens, and sessions behave, exactly, as of Layer5 Cloud v1.0.280. For the model, read the [Keys]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}), [Keychains]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}), [Sessions]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/sessions.md" >}}), and [Tokens]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/tokens.md" >}}) concepts. For tasks, use the [security guides]({{< ref "cloud/guides/security/_index.md" >}}). For base URL, authentication, and the organization header, see the [Cloud API]({{< ref "cloud/reference/api-reference/_index.md" >}}). All paths below sit under `/api` unless noted.

## Permission keys

Provider Admin holds every key. The table lists the default holders of the other roles. "Interface" means the control or tab is disabled or replaced by a permission error screen. "Server" means the Layer5 Cloud server refuses the request with HTTP 403.

| Key | Governs | Default holders besides Provider Admin | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| View Tokens | The Tokens tab | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Interface |
| Create Token | Creating an API token, and approving a desktop app or CLI sign-in | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Interface for the Tokens tab; server for approving a desktop app or CLI sign-in |
| Download Token | Downloading a token file | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Interface; the server returns only your own tokens |
| Delete Token | Revoking a token, and the Logout control on the Sessions tab | Organization Admin | Interface only; the server deletes only your own tokens |
| View Sessions | The Sessions tab | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Interface |
| Logout from a Session | Seeded for ending a session | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Not checked. The interface uses Delete Token for Logout. |
| View Keys | Seeded for the Keys tab | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Not checked. Every signed-in user sees the Keys tab. |
| Edit Key | Creating and changing a key | None | Interface and server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |
| Delete Key | Deleting a key | None | Interface and server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |
| View Keychains | The Keychains tab | User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Organization Admin | Interface |
| Create Keychain | Creating a keychain | None | Interface and server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |
| Edit Keychain | Renaming a keychain, adding or removing its keys | None | Interface and server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |
| Delete Keychain | Deleting a keychain | None | Interface and server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |
| Assign Keychains to Roles | Adding or removing a keychain on a role | None | Server. The server also requires the Provider Admin role. |

Roles that hold the keys come from the default keychains: View keys sit in User View, Delete Token in Security Management, Create Token and Download Token in Security Management and User Edit, and the key and keychain management keys, including Assign Keychains to Roles, in Provider Management. Where the server requires the Provider Admin role, it checks the role across the whole deployment, not the role held in one organization. See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) for the full role-by-keychain mapping.

## Visibility rules

| Resource | Who sees it | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keys | System-owned default keys, plus keys you created | Deployment-wide; not per organization |
| Keychains | System-owned default keychains, plus keychains you own | Deployment-wide; not per organization |
| API tokens | Your own, never the token value in the list | User account |
| Sessions | Your own | User account |

Default keys and keychains are owned by the system. Deleting a key or keychain is a soft delete, and a deleted key or keychain stops granting access immediately.

## Session and token lifetimes

The values are the defaults of the Layer5 Cloud deployment configuration. Operators of self-hosted deployments can change them.

| Credential | Lifetime | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser session (access token) | 24 hours | Not extended by activity. The user signs in again after it lapses. |
| Refresh token | 1000 hours | Single-use. Each refresh issues a new refresh token. Meshery Server uses it to renew without a new sign-in. |
| API token | No expiry | Ends only when deleted. |
| Sign-in flow | 12 hours | Time allowed to complete a sign-in. |
| Privileged-action window | 15 minutes in the packaged default | After the window, sensitive account changes ask the user to sign in again. A deployment can set a different value. |
| Anonymous Kanvas session | 24 hours | For use without signing in. It does not appear in the Sessions list. |

## Cookies

| Cookie | Purpose | Attributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider_token` | The browser session credential | HttpOnly, Secure over HTTPS, SameSite Lax |
| `has_session` | Tells the interface a session exists. Carries no secret and cannot authenticate a request. | Readable by page scripts, SameSite Lax, expires with the session |

The cookie domain is shared across the platform's hosts for organizations that use the platform sign-in provider. It is host-only for organizations that bring their own identity provider, and for custom domains outside the platform's domain.

## Endpoints

Success responses are JSON unless stated. Errors from the handlers below return a plain-text message. Refusals from the authorization layer return JSON. A missing or revoked credential returns `401` with `{"message": "user must be logged in to perform this operation"}`.

### Keys

| Method and path | Who may call | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /auth/keys` | Signed-in user | Lists keys you can see. Parameters: `page`, `pageSize`, `order`, `search` (matches the key name). Default order: most recently updated first. |
| `GET /auth/keys/{keyId}` | Signed-in user | Returns one key. A malformed id returns `400`. |
| `POST /auth/keys` | Provider Admin holding Edit Key | Creates or updates a key. |
| `DELETE /auth/keys/{keyId}` | Provider Admin holding Delete Key | Soft-deletes the key. Returns `204`. |
| `GET /identity/orgs/{orgId}/users/keys` | Signed-in user | Returns your effective keys in the organization. The interface uses it to enable controls. |

### Keychains

| Method and path | Who may call | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /auth/keychains` | Signed-in user | Lists keychains you can see. Parameters: `page`, `pageSize`, `order`, `search` (matches the keychain name). |
| `GET /auth/keychains/{keychainId}` | Signed-in user | Returns one keychain. |
| `GET /auth/keychains/{keychainId}/keys` | Signed-in user | Lists the keys in a keychain. `search` matches the key description. |
| `POST /auth/keychains` | Provider Admin holding Create Keychain | Creates a keychain owned by the caller. Only the `name` in the body is used. |
| `PUT /auth/keychains/{keychainId}` | Provider Admin holding Edit Keychain | Updates the keychain name. |
| `POST /auth/keychains/{keychainId}/{keyId}` | Provider Admin holding Edit Keychain | Adds a key. |
| `DELETE /auth/keychains/{keychainId}/{keyId}` | Provider Admin holding Edit Keychain | Removes a key. |
| `DELETE /auth/keychains/{keychainId}` | Provider Admin holding Delete Keychain | Soft-deletes the keychain and its key mappings. |
| `POST` and `DELETE /identity/orgs/{orgId}/roles/{roleId}/keychains/{keychainId}` | Provider Admin holding Assign Keychains to Roles | Adds or removes a keychain on a role. Roles are global, so the change applies in every organization. |

These key, keychain, and role writes refuse with `403` and a JSON error. A caller who lacks the route's key receives code `meshery_cloud-1108`. A caller who holds the key but is not a Provider Admin for the whole deployment receives code `meshery_cloud-3336`, "Only a Provider Admin can change roles, keychains or permission keys". Owning a keychain does not authorize a change to it. For a Provider Admin, a malformed keychain id on these routes returns `400` with a plain-text message.

### Tokens and sessions

Tokens and sessions share one store. `isOauth=false` selects API tokens and `isOauth=true` selects sessions.

| Method and path | Who may call | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /identity/tokens?name=&purpose=` | Signed-in user | Creates a token for the caller. `name` is required: an empty name returns `400` with `Token name missing.` `purpose` is optional. Writes a create event. |
| `GET /identity/tokens?isOauth=` | Signed-in user | Lists your tokens or sessions. Default order: newest first. `search` matches name and purpose. The response never contains token values. |
| `GET /identity/tokens/{id}` | Token owner | Returns the token for download. Returns `404` for an unknown or revoked token and `400` for a malformed id. Writes a download event. |
| `DELETE /identity/tokens?tokenId=` | Token owner | Revokes the token or session. A malformed id returns `400` with `invalid token id`. An unknown or already-deleted id returns `400` with `tokens does not exist`. Writes a delete event. |
| `GET /identity/tokens/infinite?userId=&provider=` | Provider Admin | Issues a non-expiring token for another account. The token is listed under that account. Others receive `403`. |
| `POST /refresh` (outside `/api`) | Holder of a refresh token | Exchanges a refresh token for a new session credential. Returns `400` with a JSON `error` if the token is missing, malformed, or already used. |
| `GET /logout` (outside `/api`) | Signed-in browser | Ends the browser's identity session. |

When Layer5 Cloud cannot read the revocation record, it refuses the request rather than accept a token it cannot check.

## Audit events

| Action | Event |
| --- | --- |
| Create a token | `<email> generated token <name>` (category token, action create) |
| Download a token | `Token <name> downloaded` (category token, action download). A failed download is also recorded, with an error severity. |
| Delete a token or log out a session | `<email> revoked token <name>` (category token, action delete) |

Key and keychain changes do not write audit events.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Build a Certification"
url: /cloud/academy/creating-content/building-certifications/index.md
description: A step-by-step guide to building a professional certification in the Academy.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In [Layer5 Academy](https://cloud.layer5.io/academy/), a **Certification** is a formal assessment designed to validate a learner's professional skills in a specific domain. Unlike a Learning Path, which guides a user through a curriculum, a Certification's primary goal is evaluation.

The successful completion of a Certification results in an official, shareable **Certificate of Completion** and a valuable badge, signifying a verified level of proficiency.

## When to use a certification

Choose a certification when the goal is to test, not teach. It assumes prior knowledge. Compare the content types in [Create Academy Content]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/_index.md#choose-a-content-type" >}}).

{{< alert type="info" title="Certification: Focus on Assessment, Not Instruction" >}}
A Certification is ideal when the main objective is to test, not teach. It assumes learners have prior knowledge and are ready to prove their expertise. If the objective is instead for the learner to solve a concrete, hands-on problem, build a [Challenge]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/building-challenges/index.md" >}}) rather than a Certification.
{{< /alert >}}

## How to Create Your Certification

Building a new certification involves setting up the correct directory structure and defining its properties through Markdown frontmatter.

### Get your identifiers

Register the certification in the Instructor Console and choose **Certification** as the content type. The console generates the certification `id` and a ready-to-paste front matter block. Use your organization's ID in the directory path. See [Create Academy Content]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/_index.md#register-content-in-the-console" >}}).

### 1. Set Up the Directory Structure

All content for a new certification must reside within the `content/certifications/<your-organization-uuid>` directory. To keep content organized, each certification has its own folder named with a descriptive, URL-friendly slug.

The final URL will follow this pattern: `https://cloud.layer5.io/academy/content/certifications/<your-organization-uuid>/<certification-folder-name>/`

Below is the standard file structure:

```
content/certifications/<your-organization-uuid>
└── layer5-certification-exam/   <-- The <certification-name> directory
    ├── _index.md                      <-- Defines the certification's metadata
    ├── exam-1.md                      <-- (Optional) A standard content page for introduction
    ├── optional-exam-2.md             <-- An optional supplementary exam
    └── exam-3.md                      <-- A mandatory exam, accessible after completing all previous required units.
```

**Key Files:**
- **`_index.md`**: The entry point for your certification containing all metadata (title, description, banner, etc.)
- **Exam Files (`*.md`)**: Individual Markdown files containing the exams. Order and optional status are controlled by frontmatter, not filename.

### 2. Define the Certification with Frontmatter

The `_index.md` file's frontmatter controls how the certification is presented to users..

Here's a complete example of the YAML frontmatter for a certification's `_index.md` file:

```yaml
---
type: "certification"
id: "<your-certification-uuid>"
title: "Layer5 Network Certification"
description: "Validate your expertise in Layer5 networking technologies through comprehensive assessment"
banner: "images/layer5-icon.svg"
weight: 1
tags: [layer5, cloud, infrastructure]
level: "beginner"
categories: [platform]
badge: 
    png: "https://images.credly.com/images/f28f1d88-428a-47f6-95b5-7da1dd6c1000/twitter_thumb_201604_KCNA_badge.png"
    svg: "https://images.credly.com/images/f28f1d88-428a-47f6-95b5-7da1dd6c1000/twitter_thumb_201604_KCNA_badge.png"
    title: "Layer5 Certified"
    description: "Earn the Certification badge to showcase your expertise in Layer5 cloud services."
---
```

#### Frontmatter Fields Reference

> In this table, fields marked with ✅  are required, while those marked with a hyphen are optional.

| Field | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `type` | ✅  | Must be set to `"certification"` to identify this content correctly. |
| `id` | ✅  | **Crucial.** A stable ID used to track learner progress. **Do not change.** |
| `title` | ✅  | The human-readable title that will be displayed to users. |
| `description` | ✅  | A comprehensive summary of the certification's scope and objectives. |
| `weight` | - | Controls the display order (lower numbers appear first). Items are sorted alphabetically by title if not specified.|
| `banner` | - | Path to a banner image located in the same folder (Page Bundle).  |
| `tags` | - | Keywords for content discovery. Multiple tags can be selected. |
| `level` | - | A string for the intended difficulty (`beginner`, `intermediate`, `advanced`). Default: `beginner`. |
| `categories` | - | A string that assigns the certification to a specific category. |
| `badge` | - | Defines the awarded digital badge. The png and svg fields accept either a full remote URL or a local file path for an image in the same folder (e.g., layer5-badge.svg).|

### 3. Add Content and Exams

A certification is primarily composed of exams. However, you can also include standard content pages to provide context.

  - **Exams:** The core assessable components. A certification can contain one or multiple exams.
  - **Informational Pages:** Standard Markdown pages that can serve as an introduction, a study guide, or a list of helpful resources.

{{< alert type="info" title="How to Create and Configure Exams" >}}
Every "Exam" file within a certification follows the unified Academy assessment standard.

For detailed instructions on how to write an exam file, define various question types, set scoring and passing percentages, and use advanced options, please refer to our comprehensive [Integrating Assessments in the Academy]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/integrating-assessments-in-the-academy.md" >}}) guide.
{{< /alert >}}

### 4. Manage question pools and test attempts

A **test** can include more questions than those presented to users in a single attempt, effectively turning it into a **test bank**, the collection of all possible questions available for that test. When users retry the test, a new set of questions is drawn from the test bank for each attempt.

This behavior is controlled by the `numberOfQuestions` property in the front matter.

* If `numberOfQuestions` is **not defined**, all questions in the test are used in every attempt.
* If it **is defined**, the test is automatically divided into multiple sets, each containing the specified number of questions.

To ensure even division, the **total number of questions** must be a **multiple** of `numberOfQuestions`.

By default, the **number of retries** is set to the number of generated sets. However, you can increase it, in which case the question sets will **cycle** through repeatedly across attempts.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Multi-Exam Certification Settings" >}}
For certifications containing multiple exams, each exam may have its own test bank, question count, and retry settings.  
These configurations are defined per test and may differ across exams within the same certification.
{{< /alert >}}




## Learner outcomes

| Outcome | When it is awarded | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Badge | The learner passes the certification's final test. | Named by the content's badge setting. A badge setting that points at a badge that no longer exists awards nothing, and the failure is logged. |
| Certificate of Completion | The same moment, when the certification defines a certificate. | Free learning and exams; certificate issuance is an optional paid feature. Each certificate gets its own ID, the recipient's name, the organization, and the issue date. It is served at a public certificate page, and the learner receives an email. A failed email does not undo the certificate. |
| Registration status | Becomes Completed. | Visible to instructors in the console. |

Certificates do not carry an expiry date. Attempt limits and time limits come from each exam's settings, covered in [Add Assessments]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/integrating-assessments-in-the-academy.md" >}}). You do not handle certificate payment; the platform does.

{{< feature-tiers categories="Academy" >}}

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
  <summary>Can my certification have only one exam?</summary>
  
Yes, it can. The simplest form of a certification consists of a single final exam. You can also include multiple independent exams if you wish to assess different skills.
</details>

<details>
  <summary>When should I choose to create a "Certification" instead of a "Learning Path"?</summary>
  
You should choose a Certification when your primary goal is to **test and assess** a learner's existing knowledge, rather than **teaching them** from scratch. A Learning Path focuses on instruction, while a Certification focuses on assessment.
</details>

<details>
  <summary>What does an "Optional" exam mean, and how does it affect a learner's progress?</summary>
  
An optional exam is supplementary material. Learners can take it, but they **do not** have to pass it to earn the final certificate. Its score **does not count** towards the certification's passing requirements. This is typically used for extra practice or to test non-core knowledge.
</details>

<details>
  <summary>How do I set an exam as "Optional"?</summary>
  
You need to add a specific field, `isOptional: true`, to the front matter of the exam's `.md` file. This field tells the system that the exam is not a mandatory requirement to pass the certification.
</details>

<details>
  <summary>Can I control the order of multiple exams within a certification?</summary>
  
Yes, you can. Each exam file's front matter has a `weight` field. Lower numbers result in an earlier display order. If you don't set a `weight`, the exams will be sorted alphabetically by file title by default.
</details>


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Build a Custom Keychain"
url: /cloud/guides/security/custom-keychains/index.md
description: Group keys into a keychain, change its keys, and delete it. A role must include the keychain before it grants anything.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A custom keychain bundles the keys that a custom role needs. This guide creates a keychain, changes its keys, and deletes it. It is written for Provider Admins and self-hosted operators, because only a Provider Admin can create, change, or delete a keychain, or include it in a role. For the model, read the [Keychains concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}).

## Before you start

- You need the Provider Admin role. The interface also checks the **Create Keychain**, **Edit Keychain**, and **Delete Keychain** permissions for the matching controls. Provider Admin holds all three. No other default role does.
- A keychain does nothing until a role includes it. Creating and editing roles is a Provider Admin action. On hosted Layer5 Cloud an organization cannot complete this path alone. On a self-hosted deployment, your Provider Admins can.
- Keychains are not organization-scoped. A role that includes your keychain grants its keys to every user who holds that role, in every organization.

## Create a keychain

Open the Keychains tab under Security and create a keychain. Give it a name and choose the keys it bundles. Layer5 Cloud creates the keychain and adds each key to it. If adding a key fails, the interface reports it as "Failed to add key to keychain". Open the keychain and confirm every key you chose is present.

You are recorded as the keychain's owner. The Keychains list shows system keychains and the keychains you own, so other administrators do not see it in their list. Any Provider Admin can still edit or delete it through the server, and ownership grants no right to change it.

## Change the keys in a keychain

**Needs:** the Provider Admin role. The interface also requires Edit Keychain.

Open the keychain's update dialog, rename it, or change the selected keys. The interface adds and removes only the difference. Removing a key stops that key flowing to every role that includes the keychain, immediately.

## Use the keychain

Add the keychain to a role. See the [Roles concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) for how roles bundle keychains and how users receive roles. Only a Provider Admin can assign a keychain to a role. The change applies to the role in every organization, because roles are global.

Test with a user who holds the role: sign in as that user in a specific organization and confirm the controls the keys govern are enabled.

## Delete a keychain

**Needs:** the Provider Admin role. The interface also requires Delete Keychain.

Delete the keychain from its row and confirm in the "Delete Keychain" dialog. Deleting removes the keychain's key mappings. The keychain stops granting anything at once, for every role that included it.

As with every keychain, only a Provider Admin can edit or delete a default keychain. Do not change a default keychain unless you intend to change permissions for every user who holds a default role.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Keychains tab shows a permission error | You lack View Keychains in the selected organization. | Ask an Organization Admin to check your role. |
| Create Keychain is disabled | You lack the Create Keychain key. | Use a Provider Admin account. |
| `403` with code `meshery_cloud-1108` or `meshery_cloud-3336` | You are not a Provider Admin for the whole deployment. Keychains and their assignment to roles apply across the whole provider. | Ask a Provider Admin to make the change. |
| A user still lacks a capability | The keychain is not on the user's role, or the user holds the role in a different organization. | Add the keychain to the role, and check the role is held in the organization in use. |


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Customize Webhooks"
url: /cloud/guides/self-hosted/customizing-webhooks/index.md
description: Send support requests, signup decisions, and Kanvas entitlement events from your self-hosted Layer5 Cloud to your own systems: the three webhooks, when each fires, the payloads, and how failures behave.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Layer5 Cloud calls an HTTP endpoint you choose when three things happen: a person asks for help, a Provider Admin decides a signup request, and a person gains Kanvas access. The calls let you route those events into your help desk, your chat, or your onboarding automation. On a self-hosted deployment you set the three endpoints; none is set by default, and an unset webhook does nothing useful.

## The three webhooks

| Chart value | Fires when | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env.webhookHelpAndSupport` | Someone submits the Help and Support form in Layer5 Cloud, or a support request raised in Kanvas reaches your deployment | `memberFormOne` |
| `env.webhookSignupRequest` | A Provider Admin approves or denies a signup request | `signupData` and `newUser` |
| `env.webhookKanvasEntitlement` | A new user registers, a user completes a first brokered social sign-in, or a role assignment gives a user Kanvas access | `signupData` and `newUser` |

## Set the endpoints

Add the three URLs to your Helm values and upgrade. The values are written into the server's ConfigMap, so the pods restart when you change them.

```yaml
env:
  webhookHelpAndSupport: "https://hooks.example.com/layer5/support"
  webhookSignupRequest: "https://hooks.example.com/layer5/signup"
  webhookKanvasEntitlement: "https://hooks.example.com/layer5/kanvas-access"
```

```bash
helm upgrade layer5-cloud layer5/layer5-cloud -n layer5-cloud --values values.yaml
```

Leave a webhook unset if you do not need it. The only way to add a fourth webhook is a change to Layer5 Cloud itself; the three names above are fixed.

## How a call is made

| Property | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Method and body | `POST` with a JSON body and `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`. |
| Authentication | None. There is no signature and no shared secret header. Restrict the receiver by network policy, or put an unguessable token in the URL path. |
| Success | A `200` or `202` response. Any other status counts as a failure. |
| Timeout | None. The server waits until the receiver answers. |
| Retries | None. Each event is sent once. |

Respond quickly and do the work afterward: the support and signup webhooks run inside the request of the person who triggered them, so a slow receiver makes that person wait.

## Payloads

### Help and support

```json
{
  "memberFormOne": {
    "firstname": "Ada",
    "lastname": "Admin",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "message": "I cannot connect my cluster.",
    "form": "support",
    "scope": "Layer5 Cloud",
    "subject": "Connection problem"
  }
}
```

Layer5 Cloud rejects a request that carries any field other than these seven, with a `400` error that names the problem. The same payload arrives whether the request came from the Layer5 Cloud form or from [Kanvas]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/help-and-support.md" >}}). Kanvas relays a request through the person's Meshery Server to the remote provider, so those users must be connected to your deployment for support to work. Under Meshery's local provider the request is refused as not implemented.

### Signup decisions

```json
{
  "signupData": {
    "id": "3f0c1d1e-8f6e-4a57-9d0e-2f1f0b4a9c11",
    "firstName": "Grace",
    "lastName": "Hopper",
    "email": "grace@example.com",
    "occupation": "Platform engineer",
    "organization": "Example Corp",
    "role": "Engineer",
    "formType": "meshmap",
    "status": "approved",
    "taskId": "task-123",
    "taskLink": "https://tasks.example.com/task-123",
    "createdAt": "2026-01-15T09:30:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-01-16T10:00:00Z"
  },
  "newUser": true
}
```

A decision requires an email, a first name, a last name, and a valid `taskLink` URL; otherwise Layer5 Cloud refuses it with a `400` error before any call is made. When the webhook fails, the decision request returns a `500` error (`unable to webhook`) and an alert event is recorded against the person.

### Kanvas entitlement

```json
{
  "signupData": {
    "firstName": "Grace",
    "lastName": "Hopper",
    "email": "grace@example.com",
    "formType": "meshmap"
  },
  "newUser": true
}
```

`newUser` is `true` for a first registration and a first brokered sign-in. For a role assignment it reflects whether the person is new to Kanvas. The `formType` value is the literal `meshmap`, the internal name of the Kanvas entitlement. A failure here never blocks the person: Layer5 Cloud records an event and continues.

## Failure behavior

| Webhook | When the receiver fails | What the person sees | What you see |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Help and support | The caller receives a `500` error. | An error on the form. | A logged error. |
| Signup decision | The decision request returns `500`. | The decision fails with an error. | A logged error and an alert event. |
| Kanvas entitlement | The call is dropped. | Nothing. | A logged error and an error event. |

Because nothing retries, build the receiver to be reliable, and reconcile missed events from the signup request list and the audit events.

## Test a webhook

Trigger each one through its real action: submit the Help and Support form, approve a test signup request, or register a test user. For a quick receiver check, point the URL at a request-capture service, perform the action, and confirm that the capture shows a `POST` with the payload above.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Instructor Console"
url: /cloud/academy/instructor-console-guide/index.md
description: Every view, metric, and action in the Academy Instructor Console: who can open it, how each number is calculated, and what instructors can manage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Instructor Console reports on your organization's Academy content and learners. It answers three questions: how many people are learning, how far they get, and which assessments stop them. The console is also where you register new content and manage who can access it.

## Availability and access

{{< feature-tiers categories="Academy" >}}

Opening the console requires the **View Academy Metrics** permission in the selected organization. Without it, the console shows a missing-permission message that names the permission.

| Role | Opens the console | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Academy Admin | Yes | Also holds team and workspace management, so it can assign content access to teams. |
| Organization Admin | Yes | |
| Provider Admin | Yes | Can view the combined "all organizations" scope. |
| Academy Learner | No | Holds content access only. |
| User, Team Admin, Workspace Admin, Billing Manager | No | Unless an operator has added the permission to the role. |

Role-to-permission assignments are seeded defaults and an operator can change them. See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).

### Organizations that are not configured

The console reports data only for an organization that has an Academy content module and version configured. Until your first content version is published, the console shows a "not configured" state that lists what you get after configuration: learner registration and progress tracking, content creation tools, test analytics, and reporting. Publishing is described in [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}).

## Views

The console has three views: **Overview**, **Learners**, and **Curricula**. "Curricula" is the console's term for a learning path, challenge, or certification.

### Overview

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Total Learners | Distinct learners who have registered for any of the organization's content to date. |
| Active Learners | Distinct learners who registered, progressed, or were graded on content this calendar month. Shown with its share of all learners. |
| Registrations | Every registration in the organization, including registrations against draft or retired content. Also shown as an average per learner. |
| Completion Rate | Registrations with status Completed divided by all registrations. |
| Quiz Pass Rate | Passed quiz attempts divided by all attempts. Retakes by one learner each count. A rate below 60% is highlighted. |

A rate with nothing to divide displays as `-`, not `0%`. No attempts and all attempts failed are different facts.

The Overview also charts:

- **Registrations by status**, using the five registration statuses below.
- **Final exams against practice quizzes.** Tests marked as final gate completion of the content. Every other test is practice. Comparing the two shows whether learners who practice successfully fail the exam that counts.
- **Test outcomes**, with the lowest pass rate, highest pass rate, and most attempted test. The two pass-rate rankings consider only tests with at least five attempts, so one failure on a new quiz does not crown it the hardest test. While no test has five attempts, the ranking uses all tests.
- **Content by type and level**, and the content ranked by registrations.

### Learners

A table with one row per registration: learner, content, registration time, and status. Rows load 20 at a time by default. Filter by content type (learning path, challenge, certification) and by status.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Registered | The learner enrolled and has not started. |
| In Progress | The learner started and has not finished. |
| Completed | The learner finished everything the content requires. |
| Failed | The learner did not pass the content. |
| Withdrawn | The learner left the content, or an instructor withdrew the registration. |

The Learners view does not export to a file.

### Curricula

Lists the **published** content of the organization. Draft and retired content is excluded, so the registrations count here is normally smaller than the Overview total. Each row shows the registrations, completion rate, and pass rate. Content that nobody has registered for is marked **Awaiting First Learner**. The view also shows the **content version** your learners are using.

If you published a release and the version does not change, publishing is a two-stage process: your content repository release, then the next Layer5 Cloud release for production. See [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}).

## Actions

| Action | Where | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Register new content | Content creation flow | Creates the content record and generates the configuration for your repository. See [Create Academy Content]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/_index.md" >}}). |
| Update content access | Curricula | Changes the team that can access the content, the access end date, the access status, the workspace, and the awarded badge. |
| Copy invite link | Curricula | Copies the link that registers a learner for the content. |
| Delete content | Curricula | Removes the content record after confirmation. |
| Withdraw a registration | Learners | Sets the registration to Withdrawn. Learners can also withdraw themselves. Any other learner needs an instructor with View Academy Metrics. |

## Active Learner definition

Active Learners counts people, not registrations, over the current calendar month, and it resets each month. A learner who enrolled months ago and submits a quiz this month is active this month. A learner who both registers and takes a quiz counts once. Because it counts distinct people over a monthly window, it is not comparable with the registration totals beside it.

## Limits and edge cases

| Situation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Quiz Pass Rate | Counts attempts, not learners. A learner who fails twice and then passes contributes two failures and one pass. |
| Registrations differ between views | Overview counts all registrations. Curricula counts registrations against published content only. |
| Provider "all organizations" scope | The console skips the not-configured check and aggregates across organizations. |
| Exporting | Not available in the console. |

## Related

- [Academy]({{< ref "cloud/academy/_index.md" >}}) for how content types relate.
- [Build a Challenge]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/building-challenges/index.md" >}}) and [Build a Certification]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/building-certifications/index.md" >}}) for authoring.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Manage Users"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md
description: Add, create, edit, and remove the people in an organization, change their roles, and understand what each action revokes and what it bills.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Users page is where administrators manage the people in an organization. It lists the organization's members and carries the actions that put people into the organization, change what they can do, and take them out. This guide covers each action, who can run it, and what it changes.

To bring in people who do not have an account yet, or to let a group join without administrator action, use [Invite Users]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/inviting-users/index.md" >}}). For what a user account is and how membership and roles combine, read the [Users concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/users/_index.md" >}}).

## Permissions

Each action needs a permission in your current organization. The server also checks your role for some actions, so holding the permission through another role is not always enough.

{{< keys-matrix caption="Organization membership permissions" functions="Add User to Organization|Invite User to Organization|Remove User from Organization|Promote or Demote User to Org Admin|Assign Roles to Organization members|Assign User Roles" >}}

The descriptions in the matrix are the permission catalog's own text. **Add User to Organization** adds an existing account to the organization, as described in [Add an existing user](#add-an-existing-user); it does not create an account.

| Action | Permission | Also required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open the Users page | View All Users | None |
| Create a user | Create User | None. Organization Admin and Provider Admin hold it by default. |
| Add an existing user | Add User to Organization | You are an Organization Admin or owner of the organization, a Provider Admin, or an Organization Admin or owner of its parent organization. |
| Remove a user | Remove User from Organization | You are an Organization Admin of the organization or a Provider Admin. |
| Edit a member's profile | Update User Profile | The member belongs to an organization you share. Only a Provider Admin can change their email address. |
| Change roles | Assign User Roles or Assign Roles to Organization members | You are an Organization Admin, a Provider Admin, or a holder of the permission. The target is a member of the organization. |
| Delete an account | Delete User | Provider Admin. See [Delete an account](#delete-an-account). |

Provider roles, such as Provider Admin, are deployment-wide. Only a Provider Admin can grant or clear them.

## Find members

The Users page shows the people with a live membership in the selected organization, 10 to a page by default and at most 100. A Provider Admin can switch the scope to every organization.

| Behavior | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Default list | Active accounts only. People who were created or invited but have not yet signed in (status Pending) and deactivated accounts are hidden until you apply a filter. |
| Default order | Most recent sign-in first. Order by sign-in time or creation time. |
| Search | Case-insensitive substring match on email, first name, and last name. |
| Filters | Role (include or exclude a role) and deleted or not deleted. |
| Columns | Name, email, status, organization roles, provider roles (Provider Admins and holders of Assign User Roles), created, last active, and counts of teams and organizations. |

Last active is the time of the person's most recent sign-in, not a live connection.

## Add an existing user

**Needs:** Add User to Organization, plus the role check in the table above.

Use this for someone who already has a Layer5 Cloud account. Search for the person, then choose the organization, and optionally the teams and organization roles they receive. The search covers every active, non-anonymous account on the deployment, not only your organization, and an empty search returns nothing.

Adding makes the person a member of the organization with **no role**. Roles and teams are separate steps that run after the membership is created. If a role or team step fails, the membership stays and the failure is reported. Adding someone who is already a member changes nothing.

Layer5 Cloud sets no seat limit on adding people. Billing counts members separately. See [Billing and seats](#billing-and-seats).

## Create a user

**Needs:** Create User.

Use this to create an account for a person who has not registered. You supply a first name, last name, and email address, all required.

Layer5 Cloud creates the account with the email address already verified and sends the person an **Account Setup** email. The link in that email is valid for 720 hours (30 days) and opens a page where the person sets a password. The account's status is Pending until they sign in.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Creating a user does not add them to an organization" >}}
The create form offers organization and role fields, but the account is created without them. The new user belongs to no organization and holds no roles until you add them. After creating the account, [add the user to the organization](#add-an-existing-user) and assign roles.
{{< /alert >}}

If the setup email cannot be sent, the request fails with `Failed to send "Account Setup" email`. The address must be a valid email; the identity provider rejects malformed addresses.

## Edit a profile

**Needs:** Update User Profile in an organization you share with the person.

Organization Admins can edit the profile of members of their organizations; Provider Admins can edit anyone. Edits to another person's profile are refused with `user is not authorized to administer this account` when you share no organization with them, and the message is the same whether the account exists or not.

The email address is restricted. A Provider Admin can change it; an Organization Admin who submits a different email is refused with `user is not authorized to change the e-mail address of this account`. Changing an email address marks the new address unverified and sends a verification message, and the person signs in with the new address once it is verified.

A person edits their own profile in [account settings]({{< ref "cloud/guides/account/managing-your-account.md" >}}). Granting badges is covered in [Assign User Badges]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/assigning-user-badges/index.md" >}}).

## Change a member's roles

**Needs:** Assign User Roles or Assign Roles to Organization members, and a role check as shown in the permissions table.

Roles control what a member can do inside the organization. To make someone an administrator, give them the **Organization Admin** role; to take administration away, remove it.

- **Roles you submit replace the roles the member holds.** The list is the complete set for that scope, so an empty list removes every role in the scope. Removing roles never ends the membership.
- **Provider roles cannot be granted inside an organization or a team.** A request that lists one is refused with HTTP 403 for every caller, a Provider Admin included, and no part of the request is applied. Provider roles are granted only through the provider role assignment.
- **Team scope accepts only Team Admin.** See [Manage Teams]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-teams/index.md" >}}).
- **A request is checked before anything is written.** If one row in a batch is refused, none of the rows are applied.
- **Layer5 Cloud does not stop you removing the last administrator.** An organization's owner keeps administrator access through ownership, but other administrators can be removed, including the last one. Confirm another administrator exists before you remove the role.

Roles, their permissions, and the defaults are listed in [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).

## Remove a user from an organization

**Needs:** Remove User from Organization, and Organization Admin of the organization or Provider Admin.

Removal takes a person out of the organization but leaves their account intact. Remove people one at a time from the row action, or select several and remove them together; bulk removal issues one removal per person, in order.

Removal acts on the organization currently selected in your session. Check the organization switcher before you remove anyone.

### What removal ends

Removing a member ends every access-bearing relationship they hold **inside that organization**, as a single operation:

* **Their organization membership**, together with the organization [roles]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) attached to it.
* **Their membership in that organization's [teams]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/teams/_index.md" >}})**, together with the team roles attached to those memberships.

Permissions reach a user through the roles carried on those memberships. A [keychain]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}) granted by a team role is revoked by the removal just as an organization role's keychain is, so a removed member holds no [keys]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}) in the organization by either route.

Removal does **not** affect:

* The person's Layer5 Cloud account, which continues to exist.
* Their membership in any other organization.
* Designs, environments, and other resources they created, which remain in the organization.
* The audit trail, which records who removed whom.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Shared teams lose the member everywhere" >}}
A team can be mapped to more than one organization. Removing a member from one organization ends their membership in every team mapped to it, including a team they use through another organization they still belong to. Add them back to that team afterward.
{{< /alert >}}

### Guards and outcomes

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The person is the organization's owner | Refused with `Organization owner cannot be removed`. Ownership cannot be transferred, so the owner stays a member for the life of the organization. Promote another member to Organization Admin if you need a second administrator. |
| An owner tries to remove themselves | Refused: owners cannot leave. Delete the organization instead. |
| An administrator removes themselves, and is not the owner | Allowed. |
| The person was never a member | `no organization membership to remove`. |
| The same removal is repeated | Succeeds and changes nothing. |
| One person in a bulk selection is refused | Only that row fails. The result names each refused person with the reason, for example `Failed to remove 1 of 3 user(s): name@example.com (reason)`, and the others are removed. |

Removal is not reversible from the Users page. To restore access, add the person again and reassign their roles and team memberships. Neither returns on its own. The confirmation reports only that the member was removed and does not list the team memberships that ended with it, so review the member's teams first if you need a record.

## Delete an account

Deleting an account removes a person from Layer5 Cloud entirely, in every organization. It is a Provider Admin capability. Organization Admins remove members from their own organization instead; they cannot delete accounts.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Account deletion from an organization's Users page does nothing" >}}
The Users page shows the delete action to holders of Delete User, but a request issued from a single organization's page reports success without deleting anything. Deletion takes effect only when a Provider Admin runs it with the all-organizations scope. Use removal to end someone's access to your organization.
{{< /alert >}}

Account deletion is refused when the account holds credentials designated to an organization that has no other owner or Organization Admin to receive them; promote another administrator or release the credentials first. A person deletes their own account from [account settings]({{< ref "cloud/guides/account/managing-your-account.md" >}}).

## Billing and seats

Removing a member stops them counting toward billing, and adding one starts it. A subscription's billable user count is the number of distinct members with a live organization membership and an active account, excluding members whose only role is Academy Learner, and never below the plan's minimum. A member added with no role is not counted. The count adjusts the subscription quantity; it does not block anyone from joining. See [how the billable user count works]({{< ref "cloud/guides/account/managing-subscriptions.md#how-the-billable-user-count-works" >}}).

## Events

Adding, creating, removing, editing, and role changes each write an audit event that names the person who acted and the person affected, for example `<actor> removed <person> from organization`.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Monitoring"
url: /cloud/guides/self-hosted/planning/monitoring/index.md
description: What a self-hosted Layer5 Cloud deployment exposes for monitoring: health endpoints, logs and error codes, startup signals, and OpenTelemetry traces.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Layer5 Cloud gives you four signals: two health endpoints, structured logs with stable error codes, a set of startup messages that tell you whether the deployment is fully working, and optional OpenTelemetry traces. It does not expose a Prometheus metrics endpoint, so build service-level indicators from ingress and Kubernetes metrics plus the signals below.

## Health endpoints

| Endpoint | Answers | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /healthz` | `200` with the text `Cloud is live` | The process is running. The chart uses it for the liveness probe. |
| `GET /readyz` | `200` when ready, `503` before | The server finished startup and is serving. The chart uses it for the readiness and startup probes. |

Both endpoints are unauthenticated. The startup probe allows 20 failed checks at 10-second intervals, so a slow start gets about 200 seconds before Kubernetes restarts the pod. Database migrations run before the server reports ready, so an upgrade that carries a large migration can approach that limit.

Kratos and Hydra expose their own health endpoints through their subcharts. The chart configures Hydra liveness on `/health/alive` and readiness on `/health/ready`.

## Logs

The server writes logs in syslog format. The chart sets the level to `4` (info). Set `env.loglevel` to `5` for debug and `6` for trace; use debug only while diagnosing, because it records more detail about requests and mail.

Errors carry a stable code of the form `meshery_cloud-NNNN`. Alert on the codes, not on message text. The codes that matter operationally:

| Code | Level | Meaning | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meshery_cloud-3301` | Error, then the process exits | The shared mail relay fails a startup screen. | [Troubleshoot Email Delivery]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/operating/smtp.md" >}}) |
| `meshery_cloud-3302` | Error | The mail relay is unreachable. No mail leaves until it clears. | Same |
| `meshery_cloud-3304` | Error | The mail relay's certificate does not verify. | Same |
| `meshery_cloud-3300` | Critical | An organization's own mail relay refused a message and fallback is off, so the message was dropped. | Same |
| `meshery_cloud-3303` | Critical | An organization's mail relay accepted a message and never confirmed it. | Same |

Failures that the server survives are logged and, where a person acted, recorded as events that Provider Admins can read: an entitlement webhook that did not return `200` or `202`, and a signup decision whose webhook failed. A failed support-request webhook is logged and returned to the person who sent the request, but not recorded as an event.

### Startup messages worth alerting on

The server exits when a database connection fails or a migration fails. It logs and keeps running for these, so a green pod does not prove they succeeded:

| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Failed to initialize Provider Admin And Provider Organization` | `INIT_CONFIG` was invalid or a step failed. The deployment runs without a provider administrator. |
| `IdP seed` warnings | The default Google or GitHub sign-in credentials were not stored. Sign-in on custom domains that use the defaults fails. |
| A credential encryption key error | `env.cloudCredentialEncryptionKey` is missing or malformed. Stored credentials cannot be read or written. |
| `Failed to initialize OpenTelemetry tracing` | The tracing configuration was rejected. The server runs without traces. |

## Traces

Set `env.otelConfig` to send OpenTelemetry traces to an OTLP gRPC collector:

```yaml
env:
  otelConfig: |
    service_name: layer5-cloud
    service_version: "1.0.278"
    environment: production
    endpoint: otel-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4317
    insecure: true
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service_name` | Yes | Name that identifies the service in traces. |
| `endpoint` | Yes | Collector address in `host:port` form, without a scheme. |
| `insecure` | No | `true` sends without TLS. Defaults to `false`. |
| `service_version` | No | Version reported with each trace. |
| `environment` | No | Deployment environment reported with each trace. |

Each request produces one trace with a span for the whole HTTP request, a span for each middleware that ran (domain resolution, authentication, authorization), and a span for the handler. Leave `otelConfig` empty to turn tracing off.

## What to monitor

| Concern | Signal |
| --- | --- |
| The server is up | `/healthz`, pod restarts |
| The server is serving | `/readyz`, ingress `5xx` rate and latency by route |
| Sign-in works | Ingress `5xx` on `/kratos` and `/hydra`, Kratos and Hydra pod health |
| Mail flows | Error codes `3301` to `3304`, and a periodic send through the [email test endpoint]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/operating/smtp.md#send-a-test-email" >}}) |
| Webhooks deliver | Recorded webhook failure events |
| The database is healthy | PostgreSQL connection count, storage, and replication, from your database's own metrics |
| Co-editing works | Ingress WebSocket connection counts on `/collaboration` |

Restrict access to logs: they carry user email addresses, and at debug level they include request detail. Provider initialization also logs the configuration it reads, including the initial administrator password, so treat startup logs as secret and remove `env.initConfig` after the first successful start.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Start from a Catalog Design"
url: /cloud/getting-started/creating-a-design-from-template/index.md
description: Browse the public catalog, try a design in the Meshery Playground, and clone it into your own workspace as a private copy.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The fastest way to a working design is to start from one someone has already published. The [catalog](https://cloud.layer5.io/catalog) is a public collection of designs for cloud native infrastructure. In this tutorial you browse it, try a design without changing anything, and then clone it. You finish with your own private copy in your workspace and a clear picture of what a clone is and what it is not.

## Before you begin

- Browsing the catalog needs no account. Cloning does: if you do not have one, follow [Create Your Layer5 Account]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/getting-started-with-layer5-account.md" >}}).
- Cloning needs the Clone Design permission. The table shows which built-in roles hold it:

{{< keys-matrix caption="Catalog permissions" functions="Clone Design|View Designs" >}}

## 1. Browse the catalog

Open the [catalog](https://cloud.layer5.io/catalog) and search by technology or type. Sort by **Most Cloned** or **Most Downloaded** to see what other people rely on most. Each design card shows a summary, and opening a design shows its full details. You can also download a design to work with it outside Layer5 Cloud.

## 2. Try a design in the Playground

Before you commit to a copy, open the design in the Playground. **Open in Playground** opens the design in a new browser tab in Kanvas on the [Meshery Playground](https://playground.meshery.io/), loaded straight from the catalog. Nothing is cloned and nothing lands in your workspace, so this is the safe way to explore a design.

## 3. Choose where the copy will go

A clone lands in the workspace you have selected, in the organization you have selected. Pick both before you clone, for example **My Workspace** in **My Organization**.

You must have one specific organization selected. Cloning in the all-organizations scope is refused.

## 4. Clone the design

Clone the design from its catalog entry. If your role lacks the Clone Design permission, the clone action is shown disabled.

Layer5 Cloud then creates your copy:

| Property of the clone | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | The original name followed by " (Copy)", for example "My App (Copy)" |
| Owner | You |
| Visibility | Private to you |
| Location | Your selected workspace in your selected organization |
| Content | The original's catalog data and file location, converted to the current design format |

Cloning also counts toward the original: Layer5 Cloud records a clone event on the original design, which feeds the catalog's **Most Cloned** sort and the catalog leaderboard. If this is the first design you own, your profile earns the first-design badge.

### When cloning is refused

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The design is not Published or Public | Refused with HTTP 403 ("unauthorized to clone design"). Only published or public designs can be cloned. |
| The all-organizations scope is selected | Refused with HTTP 400 ("Creating designs is not allowed for orgID all"). |
| No organization is selected | Refused with HTTP 400 ("orgID is not provided"). |
| Your role lacks Clone Design | The clone action is disabled. |

## What a clone is

A clone is a separate, private design that you own. It starts from the original's content and lives in your workspace, where you work on it like any other design you own. Opening a design in the Playground, by contrast, creates nothing in your account: it is a preview.

## Check your result

Your copy is ready when a design named after the original with " (Copy)" appended appears in the workspace you selected, owned by you and private.

## Next steps

- [Kanvas]({{< ref "kanvas/_index.md" >}}): design and edit infrastructure visually.
- [Catalog]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/catalog/_index.md" >}}): how the catalog works.
- [Set Up Your Organization]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/setting-up-your-organization.md" >}}): move your copy into a workspace your team shares.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Manage Subscriptions and Billing"
url: /cloud/guides/account/managing-subscriptions/index.md
description: See your organization's subscriptions, start or upgrade a paid plan, cancel at the end of a billing period, and understand how the billable user count and proration work.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A subscription connects an organization to a Layer5 plan and bills for it. This guide covers what you can see and do with subscriptions, who can do it, and how the amount you pay follows your membership. For what each plan includes, read [Feature Availability by Plan]({{< ref "cloud/reference/feature-availability.md" >}}). Current prices are on the [pricing page](https://layer5.io/pricing).

## Who can manage a subscription

A subscription belongs to an organization, not to a person. Layer5 Cloud checks the caller against the subscription's own organization, so administering one organization gives you no access to another organization's billing.

| Action | Organization Owner | Organization Admin | Provider Admin | Other members |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| See the organization's subscriptions | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Start a paid subscription | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Upgrade a subscription | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Cancel a subscription | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |

The Subscription and Plans tabs open for any user who holds **View Subcription** or **View Plans**. The default user role holds both. A member who is not an owner or Organization Admin can open the tab, but Layer5 Cloud refuses the data behind it, so the subscription table cannot load. For subscriptions that belong to another organization, Layer5 Cloud answers "subscription not found", the same answer it gives for an id that does not exist.

The Subscription and Plans tabs belong to the Layer5 Cloud interface. When the account page is shown inside a Meshery UI that uses Layer5 Cloud as its provider, only the Profile tab appears.

## Read your subscriptions

The Subscription tab lists each subscription with these columns:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Plan | The plan the subscription is on. |
| Cadence | Monthly or annual billing. |
| Status | The subscription's state, from the table below. |
| Users Billable | The number of billable users counted for the subscription. |
| Forecasted Amount | Users Billable multiplied by the plan's price per user, in US dollars. |
| Start Date, Created At, Updated At | When the subscription started, was created, and last changed. |

Three summary cards sit above the table: your current plan, the forecasted bill ("Based on current usage", or "No billable usage" when the amount is zero), and the next payment due.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| active | Paid and in good standing. |
| trialing | In a trial period. Layer5 Cloud's own checkout starts no trial. |
| incomplete | Created, but the first payment has not completed. |
| past_due | A payment failed. |
| unpaid | Payment attempts for the period have been exhausted. |
| canceled | Ended. |
| expired, inactive | No longer in effect. |
| incomplete_expired | The first payment never completed. The row is hidden from the list. |

Layer5 Cloud takes the status from the payment processor. Status changes arrive when the processor reports them, so the tab can trail a payment by a short time. Use the refresh control to reload.

## Start a paid subscription

The Plans tab lists the Personal plan ("Free Forever"), Team Designer, Team Operator, and Enterprise, each with monthly and annual prices and a currency selector.

- **Personal** is free and needs no subscription step.
- **Team Designer and Team Operator** start in the tab. Review the plan, apply a coupon if you have one, and enter your billing address and payment details. The payment form is hosted by the payment processor, and Layer5 Cloud does not store card details.
- **Enterprise** does not use self-service checkout. Its subscribe action opens a contact form, and the Layer5 team arranges the subscription.

Layer5 Cloud creates the subscription as incomplete, counts your billable users, and asks the payment processor to start billing. The status becomes active when the first payment succeeds. Checkout starts no free trial.

## Upgrade a subscription

Upgrade moves a subscription to a higher plan on the same ladder. Each ladder is separate:

- Monthly core plans, in order: Team Designer, Team Operator, Enterprise.
- Annual core plans, in the same order.
- Academy theory and lab bundles, each with its own monthly and annual ladder.

You cannot move down a ladder, and you cannot switch between monthly and annual billing on an existing subscription. To change cadence or move to a lower plan, contact [Support]({{< ref "cloud/reference/support.md" >}}).

Before you confirm, the upgrade shows an invoice preview with the prorated line items. Layer5 Cloud prorates the change: you pay for the new plan's price for the rest of the current period, less credit for the unused part of the old plan. The confirmation reads "Subscription upgraded to" followed by the plan name.

Upgrade is unavailable for subscriptions that are canceled, inactive, incomplete, or on the free plan.

## Cancel a subscription

Cancel asks you to confirm and then tells the payment processor to end the subscription **at the end of the current billing period**. The plan stays in force until the period ends. Because the plan runs to the end of the period, canceling issues no refund.

Cancel is unavailable for subscriptions that are already canceled or inactive, that never completed, or that are on the free plan.

## How the billable user count works

Plans bill per user. The count is the number of distinct people who are members of the organization, with these rules:

- The account must be active. A person who has been invited but has not accepted is not counted. A deleted account is not counted.
- A member whose only role is academy learner is not counted.
- A member added without any role is not counted.
- The count never falls below the plan's minimum number of users.
- Academy plans that bill per learner count active learners instead of organization members.

Layer5 Cloud recalculates the count when it creates a subscription, and then every 2 hours for subscriptions that are active, trialing, past due, incomplete, or unpaid. It sends the new count to the payment processor each time. No plan blocks you from adding users: the count changes what you pay, never what you can do.

### What a change in the count costs

- **The count rises mid-period.** The payment processor charges a prorated amount for the added users for the rest of the period. At renewal, the full amount reflects the new count.
- **The count falls mid-period.** The processor issues a prorated credit for the unused part. The credit stays on the organization's account balance, does not expire, and reduces future invoices. It is not refunded automatically.
- **Renewal date.** A change in the count never moves the renewal date. At renewal, the organization pays for the count as of that date.

Removing a user from the organization, or deleting their account, lowers the count at the next recalculation.

## What a plan enforces

Plans record several limits, but Layer5 Cloud enforces only the number of components in a design. See [Feature Availability by Plan]({{< ref "cloud/reference/feature-availability.md#limits-by-plan" >}}). Saving or importing a design that exceeds the component limit of the organization's active plan is refused, and an organization with no active subscription cannot add components to a design at all. Reduce the design or upgrade the plan.

## Failure modes

| What you see | Cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
