| The subscription table does not load | You are not an Organization Owner or Organization Admin of the selected organization | Ask an owner or Organization Admin to manage billing, or switch to the right organization. |
| "Payment Error" during checkout | The payment processor declined the payment | Correct the payment details and retry. |
| Status stays incomplete | The first payment has not completed | Complete the payment. An incomplete subscription that never completes becomes incomplete_expired. |
| Cancel and Upgrade are disabled | The status or plan rules above | Check the status column. |

## See also

- [Feature Availability by Plan]({{< ref "cloud/reference/feature-availability.md" >}}) lists what each plan includes.
- [Organizations]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/_index.md" >}}) explains organization owners and Organization Admins.
- [Manage Your Account]({{< ref "cloud/guides/account/managing-your-account.md" >}}) covers your own profile and sign-in.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Support"
url: /cloud/reference/support/index.md
description: The support channels for Layer5 Cloud, what each Layer5 plan includes, and what the in-product support form sends.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This page lists the ways to reach Layer5 about Layer5 Cloud and the support each plan includes.

## Contacting support {#contacting-support}

| Channel | Use it for | Available on |
|---|---|---|
| Email, [support@layer5.io](mailto:support@layer5.io) | Questions and problems with Layer5 Cloud | Every plan |
| [Community forum](https://discuss.layer5.io/) | Questions, shared experience, and help from other users and moderators | Every plan |
| [Slack](https://slack.layer5.io) | Real-time conversation with the community | Every plan |
| Support form in Layer5 Cloud | A written request routed to Layer5 | Every plan |
| [FAQs](https://layer5.io/company/faq) | Answers to common questions | Everyone |

### The support form

Layer5 Cloud has a Support page with cards for the documentation, the discussion forum, Slack, and the FAQs, and a contact form. The form takes these fields:

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| Subject | Required. At least 5 characters. |
| Issue Description | Required. At least 5 characters. |
| Type of inquiry | One of Account/Billing, Sales, Support, Partnership, Extension Points, or Community. |

Layer5 Cloud validates the request and delivers it to the support endpoint configured for the deployment. It rejects a request that carries fields it does not recognize with HTTP 400, and it answers HTTP 500 when delivery to the endpoint fails. The page shows a confirmation message after you submit, whatever the server answers, so confirm delivery by email if the request is urgent.

On a self-hosted deployment, your operator configures where the form delivers requests. See [Self-hosted deployment]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/_index.md" >}}).

## Support by plan

{{< feature-tiers functions="Community Support|Standard Support|Premium Support" >}}

- **Community Support** is help from the community forum.
- **Standard Support** adds troubleshooting help from Layer5 over the web.
- **Premium Support** adds a response-time agreement and 24/7 web and phone support. Terms are part of your order. Current plan details are at [layer5.io/pricing](https://layer5.io/pricing).

These are commercial entitlements. Layer5 Cloud does not check your plan when you submit the support form.

## Account recovery

If you forget your password, the sign-in page offers account recovery by email. Layer5 Cloud sends a recovery link and code to the address on the account. Both are valid for 30 days. Password sign-in is refused until the address on the account is verified, so verify your address before you rely on password sign-in. See [Getting started with a Layer5 account]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/getting-started-with-layer5-account.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Workspace and Environment Reference"
url: /cloud/reference/workspaces-and-environments/index.md
description: Defaults, limits, scope, permissions by operation, responses, and deletion effects for workspaces and environments.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This page states how workspaces and environments behave, exactly. For the model, read the [Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/workspaces.md" >}}) and [Environments]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/environments.md" >}}) concepts. For tasks, use the [workspace guides]({{< ref "cloud/guides/workspaces/_index.md" >}}). For every endpoint's schema, see the [REST API Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/api-reference/rest.md" >}}), and for base URL and authentication see the [Cloud API]({{< ref "cloud/reference/api-reference/_index.md" >}}). All paths below sit under `/api`.

## Fields, defaults, and limits

| Property | Workspace | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API. | Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API. |
| Description | Up to 255 characters. May be empty. | Up to 255 characters. May be empty. |
| Organization | Required on create. Fixed for the life of the workspace. | Required on create (`organizationId is required`). Fixed for the life of the environment. |
| Owner | The user who created it. | Not recorded on create. |
| Starting state | No teams, environments, designs, or views. | No connections, in no workspace. |
| Kind | Single kind. | Ordinary when created through the API. Platform-provisioned environments exist and are protected. |
| Update | Only the fields sent change. | Name and description are both replaced; an omitted field becomes empty. |
| Plan check | None. | None. The feature matrix lists environments under Enterprise. |
| Count limits | None. An organization must keep at least one workspace. | None. |

Layer5 Cloud creates **My Workspace** in any organization that has no workspace.

## Scope and visibility

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Who sees a workspace or environment in a list? | Every member of its organization. Team membership does not narrow the list. |
| How is the organization chosen? | A list request carries one organization identifier. The all-organizations value needs View All Organizations and otherwise returns HTTP 403. |
| What does a missing or foreign identifier return? | HTTP 404, `workspace not found` or `environment not found`. |
| Can a workspace or environment move to another organization? | No. |
| Which relationships can cross organizations? | None for teams and environments: both must share the workspace's organization (HTTP 403 otherwise). A design assigned to a workspace takes on that workspace's organization. |

## Permissions by operation

Layer5 Cloud checks each key in the organization that owns the workspace or environment. Operations marked UI only are hidden in the interface but not checked by the server.

| Operation | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /workspaces` | Create Workspace (organization from the request body) |
| `GET /workspaces`, `GET /workspaces/{id}` | UI only (View Workspace); organization scoping applies |
| `PUT /workspaces/{id}` | Edit Workspace |
| `DELETE /workspaces/{id}` | Delete Workspace |
| `POST`, `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/teams/{teamId}` | Assign team to workspace, Remove team from workspace |
| `POST`, `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/environments/{environmentId}` | Assign environment to workspace, Remove environment from workspace |
| `POST`, `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/designs/{designId}` | Assign Designs to Workspaces, Remove Designs from Workspaces |
| `POST`, `DELETE /workspaces/{id}/views/{viewId}` | Assign Views to Workspace, Unassign Views from Workspace |
| `GET /workspaces/{id}/views`, `GET /workspaces/{id}/events` | View Workspace |
| `GET /workspaces/{id}/teams`, `/environments`, `/designs` | None |
| `POST /environments` | Create Environment (organization from the request body) |
| `GET /environments`, `GET /environments/{id}` | UI only (View Environment); organization scoping applies |
| `PUT /environments/{id}` | Edit Environment |
| `DELETE /environments/{id}` | Delete Environment |
| `POST`, `DELETE /environments/{id}/connections/{connectionId}` | Assign connections to environment, Remove connections from environment |
| `GET /environments/{id}/connections` | View Environment |

Default holders by role:

{{< keys-matrix caption="Workspace and environment permissions" functions="View Workspace|Create Workspace|Edit Workspace|Delete Workspace|Assign team to workspace|Remove team from workspace|Assign environment to workspace|Remove environment from workspace|Assign Designs to Workspaces|Remove Designs from Workspaces|View Environment|Create Environment|Edit Environment|Delete Environment|Assign connections to environment|Remove connections from environment|View Connections" >}}

## List parameters

| Parameter | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orgId` | Workspace and environment lists | The organization to list. Required. |
| `search` | All lists | Case-insensitive match on name or description. |
| `order` | All lists | Order by `created_at` or `updated_at`. Environment connection lists also accept `name`. Default is newest first. |
| `page`, `pageSize` | All lists | Zero-based page and page size. |
| `filter` | Lists of a workspace's teams, environments, designs, views, and an environment's connections | `{"assigned": true}` (default) lists what is in; `{"assigned": false}` lists what is not yet in. For designs, the not-yet-in list holds only designs the caller owns. |
| `visibility` | Lists of a workspace's designs and views | Repeatable. Keeps only designs or views with that visibility. |

## Responses

| Operation | Condition | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create workspace | Organization missing or malformed | HTTP 400, `organizationId is required` or `invalid organizationId format` |
| Create workspace | Name or description over 255 characters | HTTP 500, `Unable to create workspace` |
| Update workspace | Empty or `null` body | HTTP 400, `Unable to update workspace` |
| Update or delete workspace | Not in the caller's organizations | HTTP 404, `workspace not found` |
| Delete workspace | Last live workspace in the organization | HTTP 500, `cannot delete workspace: at least one workspace must exist for the organization` |
| Assign team or environment | Team or environment in another organization | HTTP 403, `unable to add team to workspace` or `unable to add environment to workspace` |
| Assign environment | Platform-provisioned environment | HTTP 403, `this environment is provisioned by the platform and cannot be added to a workspace` |
| Remove environment from workspace | Never attached | HTTP 404, `no such environment assignment` |
| Create environment | Organization missing | HTTP 400, `organizationId is required` |
| Delete environment | Platform-provisioned | HTTP 403, `this environment is provisioned by the platform and cannot be deleted here` |
| Delete environment | No live environment | HTTP 404, `no environment with the requested id` |
| Assign connection | Platform-provisioned environment | HTTP 403, `this connection cannot be assigned to this environment` |
| Remove connection | Platform-provisioned environment | HTTP 403, `this connection cannot be detached from this environment` |
| Remove connection | Never assigned | HTTP 404, `no such connection assignment` |

Assigning a team or environment that is already assigned succeeds and returns the existing assignment. Every workspace create, update, delete, assign, and unassign writes an event to the workspace's activity log, and a failure writes an error event.

## What deletion ends

| Deleting a | Ends | Leaves in place |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | Team, environment, design, and view assignments | Teams, environments, connections, designs, views, and their owners |
| Environment | Connection assignments and workspace attachments | Connections, credentials, workspaces, and the connections' other environments |

Access that flowed through a deleted or detached link ends at once. See [Access to connections and credentials]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/environments.md#access-to-connections-and-credentials" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Add Assessments"
url: /cloud/academy/creating-content/integrating-assessments-in-the-academy/index.md
description: Add quizzes, tests, and exams to Academy content. Covers the file format, question types, scoring, attempt and time limits, and how a passing result completes a course, learning path, challenge, or certification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assessments gate progress and trigger completion in Academy content. A learner who passes an assessment unlocks the next level of the content, and a learner who passes the final assessment completes the content and receives its badge and, where defined, its certificate. Layer5 Cloud scores every submission on the server and records the result in the learner's grade history.

This page shows how to write an assessment file and explains how the server treats it. It assumes you have a content repository with a [learning path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}), [challenge]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/building-challenges/index.md" >}}), or [certification]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/building-certifications/index.md" >}}).

## Place assessments at each level

Each level of the content hierarchy takes its own kind of assessment. The kinds differ in name only. All three use the same file format.

| Level | Assessment | Typical file | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Learning path, challenge, or certification | Exam | `exam.md` | Validates the whole content item |
| Course | Test | `test.md` | Validates one course |
| Module | Quiz | `quiz.md` | Checks one module |

```
Learning path
├── Course 1
│   ├── Module A
│   │   └── quiz.md
│   ├── Module B
│   │   └── quiz.md
│   └── test.md
├── Course 2
│   ├── Module A
│   │   └── quiz.md
│   └── test.md
└── exam.md
```

Challenges and certifications place their exams directly under the content item. You may use any file names that keep the levels distinguishable, for example `test-for-course.md`.

Each mandatory section needs at least one assessment. A course with no test, or a learning path with no exam, has no event that can mark it complete or award its badge.

## Write an assessment file

An assessment is a Markdown file whose front matter holds the questions. Text after the front matter appears above the questions as orientation for the learner.

```yaml
---
title: "Kubernetes Basics Quiz"
id: "quiz-kubernetes-basics"
type: "test"
layout: "test"
passPercentage: 70
timeLimit: 15
maxAttempts: 3
final: false
isOptional: false
questions:
  - id: "q1"
    text: "Which object runs one or more containers as a unit?"
    type: "single-answer"
    marks: 2
    options:
      - id: "a"
        text: "Pod"
        isCorrect: true
      - id: "b"
        text: "Namespace"
  - id: "q2"
    text: "Which kubectl command lists all pods?"
    type: "short-answer"
    marks: 2
    correctAnswer: "kubectl get pods"
---
Answer every question. You can retake this quiz.
```

Front matter keys are camelCase. The theme still accepts older snake_case keys such as `pass_percentage` and `is_optional` for existing content, but new content should use camelCase.

### Assessment fields

| Field | Required | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | Yes | Must be `test`. |
| `layout` | No | Must be `test` when set. |
| `passPercentage` | Yes | Minimum percentage of total marks needed to pass, for example `70`. |
| `questions` | Yes | The list of questions. |
| `title` | No | Name shown to the learner. |
| `id` | No | Unique identifier. When omitted, the build generates one from the file path. Set a readable, globally unique value such as `quiz-containers` so grade history stays traceable. |
| `isOptional` | No | When `true`, the assessment does not block progress. See [Required and optional assessments](#required-and-optional-assessments). Default `false`. |
| `final` | No | When `true`, passing completes the parent section. See [Final assessments](#final-assessments). |
| `timeLimit` | No | Minutes allowed per attempt. `0` (the default) means no limit. |
| `maxAttempts` | No | Attempts allowed per learner and registration. `0` means unlimited. |
| `numberOfQuestions` | No | Number of questions served per attempt when the file holds a larger question bank. The bank size should be a multiple of this value. |

### Question fields

| Field | Required | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Yes | Identifier, unique within the assessment, for example `q1`. |
| `text` | Yes | The question prompt. |
| `type` | Yes | `single-answer`, `multiple-answers`, or `short-answer`. |
| `marks` | Yes | Points awarded for a correct answer. |
| `options` | For choice questions | List of options. Each has an `id`, `text`, and optional `isCorrect: true`. |
| `correctAnswer` | For `short-answer` | The expected text. |
| `instructions` | No | Replaces the default hint shown with the question. |

## Question types

| Type | Learner action | Scored correct when | Default hint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `single-answer` | Selects one option | Exactly one option is selected and it is correct | Select one answer |
| `multiple-answers` | Selects any number of options | Every correct option is selected and no incorrect option is selected | Select all that apply |
| `short-answer` | Types text | The text equals `correctAnswer` after trimming whitespace, ignoring case | Type your answer below |

Scoring is all or nothing per question. A `multiple-answers` question gives no partial credit. An unanswered question scores zero.

Short-answer matching is always case-insensitive. Layer5 Cloud has no case-sensitive mode, so write `correctAnswer` as the one canonical form you accept and avoid questions with several valid phrasings.

For a true or false question, use `single-answer` with two options:

```yaml
questions:
  - id: "q3"
    text: "A Kubernetes pod can contain multiple containers."
    type: "single-answer"
    marks: 1
    options:
      - id: "true"
        text: "True"
        isCorrect: true
      - id: "false"
        text: "False"
```

{{< alert type="warning" title="Use only the supported types" >}}
The scoring service evaluates `single-answer`, `multiple-answers`, and `short-answer`. A question with any other `type` is shown but never scores, so a learner cannot earn its marks.
{{< /alert >}}

## Required and optional assessments

Assessments are required by default. A learner must pass every required assessment in a section before the next level unlocks.

- Pass all module quizzes to unlock the course test.
- Pass all course tests to unlock the learning path exam.

Set `isOptional: true` to exclude an assessment from these prerequisite checks. Optional assessments never block progress, and a learner can skip them. If every module in a course is optional, learners go straight to the course test.

When a learner submits a test whose prerequisites are incomplete, the server rejects the submission with `Prerequisites not completed`.

## Final assessments

The final assessment of a section decides when that section is complete. The build selects it with these rules:

1. A section with a single exam treats it as final.
2. A section with several exams uses the one marked `final: true`. Mark at most one per section.
3. When no exam is marked, the last exam by file path is final.
4. A final exam cannot be optional, even when it is the only exam.

The build orders by file path and not by `weight`, because `weight` can be missing or duplicated across files. Name the file that must come last so that it sorts last, or mark it `final: true`.

A learner can take a final exam only after completing every mandatory sibling and child item.

## What passing does

| Result | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Pass any assessment | That assessment is marked completed in the learner's progress. |
| Pass a final assessment | The parent section is marked completed. |
| Pass the final assessment of a learning path, challenge, or certification | The registration becomes **Completed**, the content's badge is awarded when one is set, and a certificate is issued and emailed when the content defines one. |
| Pass a non-final assessment | Only that assessment completes. Passing a course test that is not final does not complete the course. |

Mark the assessment that closes each course or content item `final: true` when a section holds more than one exam, so completion does not depend on file ordering.

A learner can retake an assessment after passing it, subject to `maxAttempts`. The server never blocks a retake because of an earlier score.

## Attempts, time limits, and question banks

Layer5 Cloud applies these limits when a learner starts and submits an attempt.

| Behavior | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Attempt counting | Starting an attempt counts against `maxAttempts`, whether or not the learner submits it. |
| Attempt limit reached | Starting another attempt fails with `Maximum attempts reached for this test`. |
| Time limit | The attempt expires `timeLimit` minutes after it starts. A submission after expiry fails with `Test submission has expired`. |
| Resubmission | A submitted attempt cannot be submitted again. |
| Ownership | A learner can submit only their own attempt, and only against their own registration. |
| Payload size | A submission larger than 1 MiB is rejected. |

With `numberOfQuestions` set, the learner receives the next window of questions from the bank on each attempt. Attempt 1 gets questions 1 to N, attempt 2 gets N+1 to 2N, and so on. After the last window, the sequence restarts at question 1. When the bank size is not a multiple of N, the final window is shorter, so keep the bank an exact multiple.

The server never sends correct answers to the learner's browser.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Do not rename or move assessment files after launch" >}}
The server identifies an assessment by its published path. Renaming or moving the file makes the new path a different assessment. Earlier attempts and passes recorded against the old path no longer count, so attempt limits reset and prerequisites that depended on the old path stay unmet.
{{< /alert >}}

## Scoring

The build sums the `marks` of the questions into the assessment's total marks. The server computes:

```
percentage = learner's score / total marks * 100
```

The attempt passes when the percentage is greater than or equal to `passPercentage`. The saved result holds the score, the percentage, the pass or fail outcome, and which questions the learner got right. Instructors see pass rates in the [Instructor Console]({{< ref "cloud/academy/instructor-console-guide/index.md" >}}).

## Test your assessment

Local preview renders the assessment layout. It does not score. Submission, grading, attempt counting, and completion run on the server, so you must publish a version of your content to test them end to end. Use a dedicated test learner registration in a non-production organization so that pass and completion states do not appear in your real metrics.

## Answers to common questions

**Is the `id` required?** No. The build generates one from the file path when you omit it. Set one yourself for traceability.

**Why does every course and learning path need an assessment?** Completion is triggered by passing the final assessment. Without one, nothing marks the level complete or awards its badge.

**How are `multiple-answers` questions scored?** All or nothing. Selecting a wrong option or missing a correct one scores zero for the question.

**Can a learner retake an assessment after scoring 100%?** Yes, until `maxAttempts` is reached. When `maxAttempts` is `0`, retakes are unlimited.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Find and Use Catalog Designs"
url: /cloud/guides/exploring-the-catalog/index.md
description: Search the catalog, read a design's details, open it in the Playground, clone it into your workspace, and manage the catalog entries you own.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [catalog](https://cloud.layer5.io/catalog) holds published designs: reusable infrastructure patterns that anyone can inspect and any signed-in user with the right permission can clone. This guide covers finding a design, using it, and managing the entries you own. For how the catalog works, who can publish, and what the metrics mean, see [Catalog]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/catalog/_index.md" >}}).

![The catalog page showing published designs as a grid of cards with the Top Performers panel above them](images/catalog-view.gif)

## Before you start

- **Browsing needs no account.** Signed-out visitors can search, filter, and read every published design.
- **Cloning, downloading, editing, and deleting need you to sign in** and hold the matching permission. A role without the permission sees the action disabled. See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).
- **Cloning needs an organization.** The copy lands in your selected workspace, so you must have an organization selected. Cloud refuses a clone while the all-organizations view is active.

| Action | Permission | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browse, search, read details | None | Open to signed-out visitors. |
| Open in the Playground | None | Changes there are never written back to the catalog design. |
| Clone | Clone Design | Source must be published or public. |
| Download | Download a design | Core YAML only, without catalog metadata. |
| Edit catalog details | Publish Design | Type, technology, description, and caveats. |
| Unpublish | Unpublish Design | You must be the design's creator or hold Approve Catalog Request. |
| Delete | Delete a design | You must own the design. Provider administrators are the exception. |

## Browse the catalog

The catalog shows every published design from every organization. Two layouts show the same results:

- **Grid view** shows one card per design. The top-left banner is the design's class, such as Official. The top-right tag is its type, such as Deployment. A row of icons shows the usage counters (Opens, Downloads, Deploys, Clones, Shares). Hovering a card flips it to show the author, version, technologies, and last update.
- **Table view** is denser and suits sorting and comparing. The column control chooses which attributes show, such as Author, Created At, or Downloads.

![Table view of the catalog with sortable metric columns](images/design-view.gif)

The **Top Performers** panel above the results previews the leaderboard. You can hide it and show it again, and it opens the full leaderboard.

### Rank designs on the leaderboard

The leaderboard lists designs as a table sorted by Opens by default, ten rows per page. Sorting by any metric column re-ranks the list, and the sort order is kept in the page address, so you can share a ranking by copying the URL. You can also:

- Search by design name.
- Narrow by Type and Class. Each filter takes one value at a time, and All turns it off.
- Show or hide metric columns.
- Act on a row: clone it, download it, copy its link, share it with users or on social networks, or open it in the Playground.

Viewing the leaderboard needs the View Designs permission. Without it, the page shows a permission-denied message instead of the table.

## Find a design

The filter bar narrows the catalog. Filters combine, so each one you add shrinks the result set.

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Search | Matches design **names** only, as a case-insensitive substring. It does not search descriptions or technologies. |
| Sort by | Alphabetical (A-Z or Z-A), most or least recently updated, most opened, most shared, most cloned, most deployed, most downloaded. Results default to most recently updated. |
| Owner | Limits results to your organization, specific teams, or one author. |
| Class | Official, Verified, or Community. |
| Technology | The technology tags authors attached when they published, such as `Argo CD` or `AWS API Gateway`. |
| Type | The category authors chose when they published: Deployment, Traffic Management, Security, Workloads, Observability, Scaling, or Resiliency. |

The three classes tell you how much to trust a design:

- **Official** is produced and fully supported by Meshery maintainers.
- **Verified** is produced by partners and verified by Meshery maintainers.
- **Community** is produced and shared by Meshery users, with varying support.

## Read a design's details

Selecting a design opens its detail view.

![The detail view of a catalog design showing class, author, dates, version, visibility, and usage counters](images/design_model.png)

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Class, Created By, dates | The design's class, its original author, and when it was created and last updated. |
| Version | Increments each time the design is updated. |
| Visibility | **Published** for every design in the public catalog. |
| Caveats and Considerations | Stipulations and known behaviors to weigh before you use the design. |
| Similar Designs by Type | Other designs of the same type. |
| Metrics | Lifetime Opens, Downloads, Deploys, Clones, and Shares. |

## Open a design in the Playground

**Open in Playground** opens the design in the Kanvas designer at [playground.meshery.io](https://playground.meshery.io/extension/meshmap), in a new browser tab. The catalog page stays open behind it.

The Playground is a hosted Kanvas instance. It lets you pan, zoom, open components, and inspect relationships without installing Meshery or signing in. Changes you make there are not written back to the catalog design. To keep an editable copy, clone the design.

The link Layer5 Cloud builds carries the design's identifier as URL parameters, so the Playground opens that specific design. See [URL Parameters]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/url-parameters.md" >}}) to build such a link yourself.

## Clone a design

Cloning creates your own editable copy of a published or public design. Use it when a catalog design is a good starting point for your own.

A clone has these properties:

- It is **private**, owned by you, and placed in your selected workspace. It appears in [My Designs](https://cloud.layer5.io/catalog/content/my-designs).
- Its name is the original name with `(Copy)` appended.
- It keeps the original's catalog metadata and origin, but it is not published. Publishing it is a separate request.
- The source design's Clones counter rises by one.

You cannot clone a private design, including your own. Save a copy from Kanvas instead. A clone attempt on a private design fails with `unauthorized to clone design`.

## Download a design

**Download** saves the design as a Design (YAML) file, which suits offline backups and handing the file to someone else. The file holds the core definition only and omits catalog metadata such as the description, technology, and class.

To export in other formats, see [Exporting Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/export-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Edit a published entry

You can change how an entry you published is described. **Edit** opens a dialog with these fields:

- **Type**: the design's category.
- **Technology**: the technology tags.
- **Description**: the design's purpose and intended uses.
- **Caveats and Considerations**: stipulations and known behaviors.

![The edit dialog for a published design with type, technology, description, and caveats fields](images/design-edit.png)

Two properties of a published design are fixed. The **name** cannot change, and the **visibility** cannot be switched directly. To take a design out of the catalog, unpublish it.

## Unpublish a design

**Unpublish** withdraws a design from the catalog without deleting it. The design returns to **private** in the owner's account, so only the owner and anyone it is shared with can open it.

You can unpublish a design if you created it or if you hold Approve Catalog Request. The action also needs the Unpublish Design permission in the interface. Without either, Cloud answers `unauthorized to unpublish to catalog`.

## Delete a design

**Delete** destroys a catalog item you own: a design, a view, or a filter. The confirmation dialog is titled **Delete Catalog item?**.

Deleting is not unpublishing. Unpublishing keeps the design in your account. Deleting removes it permanently and unassigns it from every workspace it belonged to. There is no trash and no undo.

The permission is specific to the item type:

| Catalog item | Permission required |
| --- | --- |
| Design | Delete a design |
| WASM filter | Delete WASM Filter |
| View | Delete View |

The server requires you to own the item. A user who holds the permission but does not own the item is refused. Provider administrators are the exception. The **Delete** action stays disabled when your role lacks the permission.

My Designs also supports bulk delete in table view. Select rows and use the bulk **Delete** action. Each item is deleted independently, so a failure on one does not stop the others. Check the list afterward.

For the full walkthrough, including how deletion differs from removing a design from a workspace, see [Deleting a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/deleting-a-design/index.md" >}}).

## Troubleshooting

| You see | Cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthorized to clone design` | The design is private. | Ask the owner to share it, or have them publish it. |
| `orgID is not provided` | No organization is selected. | Select an organization, then clone again. |
| Clone is disabled | Your role lacks Clone Design. | Ask an organization administrator to review your role. |
| An action is disabled or a page shows a permission-denied message | Your role lacks the matching permission. | See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}). |
| A design you searched for by technology does not appear | Search matches names only. | Use the Technology filter instead. |

## Next steps

- [Start from a Catalog Design]({{< ref "cloud/getting-started/creating-a-design-from-template.md" >}}) walks through cloning a design and making it yours.
- [Publish Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/publishing-designs/index.md" >}}) covers sending your own design to the catalog.
- [Catalog]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/catalog/_index.md" >}}) explains classes, review, and metrics.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Invite Users"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/inviting-users/index.md
description: Bring people into an organization with invitation links or a direct invite, control who can accept and what they receive, and revoke access.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An invitation is a link that lets people join one organization, with the roles and teams you choose, under limits you set: who may accept, how many may accept, when it stops working, and what accepting does. The same mechanism powers your organization's open sign-up. This guide covers creating and managing invitations, what happens when someone accepts, and the separate direct invite for a single new person.

Layer5 Cloud has two ways to bring a person in:

| | Invitation | Direct invite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where | Invitations page | Users page, Invite New User |
| Target | Anyone with the link, a list of addresses, or a whole email domain | One new email address |
| Membership begins | When the person accepts | Immediately, before they act |
| Limits | Quota, expiry, address allowlist, enable and disable | None |
| Existing account | Can accept | Refused. Use [Add an existing user]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#add-an-existing-user" >}}). |
| Permission | Manage Invitations | Invite User to Organization |

## Permissions

**Needs:** the **Manage Invitations** permission in the organization. Provider Admin, Organization Admin, and Academy Admin hold it by default.

Creating, editing, and deleting an invitation, and changing which invitation is the open sign-up invitation, all require the permission. The same permission covers choosing the roles and teams an invitation grants, so anyone who can write an invitation, Academy Admins included, can specify its roles. A write without the permission is refused with HTTP 403.

Invitations are not tier-limited.

## Default organization state

Organizations are **closed** by default. A person cannot join by visiting a URL; they must open a valid invitation link or sign in through your organization's address when it has an [open sign-up invitation](#the-open-sign-up-invitation).

When no open sign-up invitation exists, people who register at your organization's page become platform users with no membership and no roles in your organization until an administrator adds them or they accept an invitation.

{{< alert type="info" title="Roles are not assigned automatically" >}}
A person who joins through an invitation receives only the roles and teams listed on it. An invitation with no roles adds the person with no role.
{{< /alert >}}

## Decide what the invitation allows

Choose the audience first, because it decides which fields you set.

- **Precise invitation:** list one or more full email addresses. Only those addresses can accept.
- **Domain-wide invitation:** list a domain pattern such as `@layer5.io`. Any address ending in that domain can accept.
- **Public invitation:** leave the address list empty. Anyone signed in with the link can accept. Use it for events and community programs.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Use domain wildcards and public links carefully" >}}
A pattern such as `@company.com` admits anyone with that domain, and a public link can be forwarded without limit. Verify domain ownership, grant only the access the audience needs, and set an expiry and a quota on public links.
{{< /alert >}}

Address matching is exact and case-sensitive. `User@Example.com` does not match an entry written `user@example.com`. List the address in the form people sign in with.

### Invitation properties explained

| Property | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `emails` | Exact addresses (`user@example.com`) and domain patterns (`@example.com`). If empty, any address can accept. |
| `roles` | Roles assigned on acceptance. If empty, the person joins with no role. Each role must be an existing organization role. Provider-wide roles, such as Provider Admin, cannot be granted by an invitation, and an invitation listing one, or a role that does not exist, is refused when it is created or edited. |
| `teams` | Teams the person joins on acceptance. If empty, the person joins no team. Each team must be an existing team of your organization; an invitation listing any other team is refused when it is created or edited. |
| `quota` | Maximum number of people who can accept. Not set, or 0, means unlimited. |
| `expiresAt` | Date and time after which the link stops accepting new people. Not set means it never expires. Does not affect people who already accepted. |
| `status` | `enabled` can be accepted. `disabled` cannot, and can be re-enabled later. |
| `name` | Human-readable name. Required in the form, up to 255 characters. |
| `description` | Internal note about the invitation's purpose, up to 5000 characters. |
| `acceptanceOutcome` | What accepting does. `direct_membership` (the default) makes the person a member of the inviting organization. `child_organization` creates a new organization for the person beneath it. See [Choosing what accepting an invitation does](#choosing-what-accepting-an-invitation-does). A `child_organization` invitation requires the **Create Organization** permission in the inviting organization. |
| `isDefault` | Marks this invitation as the organization's open sign-up invitation. Only one invitation per organization can hold the mark; setting it on one clears it from the others. An edit that omits this property leaves it unchanged. |

`emails`, `roles`, and `teams` can each be left empty or omitted.

## Create an invitation

**Needs:** Manage Invitations.

Create the invitation from the Invitations page, setting the audience, roles, teams, quota, expiry, status, name, and description. Enabled is the default status.

<img src="./images/create-invitation.png" alt="Create Invitation Dialog" style="width:30%; height:auto;" />

### Who receives an email

Creation sends one email to each **exact address** in the list. Domain patterns and public invitations send nothing, so share their link yourself.

- The email is sent at creation only. Editing an invitation does not send it again, and there is no resend. To notify someone again, send them the link.
- A failed send does not fail the creation. Sending stops at the first failure, so addresses after it are not emailed. Check that each person received it.
- The subject reads `<Inviter name> has invited you to <Organization name> Organization`. The body names the organization and the teams you pre-assigned, and carries an **Accept Invitation** button. It does not list roles.
- The sender is your organization's mail configuration when set, else the deployment default. See [Bring Your Own Mail Server]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/org-management/bring-your-own-mail-server.md" >}}).

<img src="./images/invitation-email.png" alt="Invitation Email" style="width:50%; height:auto;" />

## Share, track, and revoke

The Invitations page lists every invitation with its name, description, copyable link, owner, expiry, quota use, roles, teams, and status.

![Invitations Overview Table](./images/overview.png)

Filter by status, role, or team. The Quota column shows people accepted against the limit, such as `2 / 5`, or `2 / Unlimited`. To see the people who joined, open the [Users page]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md" >}}).

| To | Do this | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stop new acceptances temporarily | Set status to disabled | The link stops working for new people at once. Re-enable it later. |
| Stop new acceptances for good | Delete the invitation | The link fails. The delete has no confirmation step. |
| Change who can accept or what they receive | Edit the invitation | Applies to future acceptances only. |
| Remove someone who already accepted | [Remove the person]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#remove-a-user-from-an-organization" >}}) | Disabling or deleting an invitation never removes people who accepted. |

If another administrator deletes an invitation while your edit dialog is open, saving reports that the invitation was not found. Reload the table to see the current list. An expiry date stops new people only; it does not remove anyone.

## What happens when someone accepts

The link is `<your Layer5 Cloud address>/invitations/<id>/accept`. Anyone holding it can try to accept, and eligibility is decided at that moment.

1. **Invitation exists.** A deleted invitation cannot be accepted.
2. **Status is enabled.**
3. **Not expired.**
4. **Quota available.** A person who already accepted is also refused once the quota is full.
5. **Address allowed.** The signed-in person's email matches an entry, or the list is empty.
6. **Account verified.** For a direct membership invitation, an account whose email address is not yet verified is not placed. The invitation applies at the person's first verified sign-in.

The first failing check stops the acceptance and nothing is written. The person sees `The invitation cannot be applied to this user` with one of these reasons:

| Reason shown | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `invitation no longer exists` | Deleted. |
| `invitation is not enabled` | Disabled. |
| `invitation has expired` | Past its expiry. |
| `invitation has reached its quota` | Quota full. |
| `email is not on the invitation's allowlist` | Address does not match. |
| `account email address is not verified yet` | Verify the email, then sign in again. |

A `child_organization` invitation is not held for email verification; see below.

When the person is eligible, in order:

1. They are added to the organization, once.
2. Each listed role they lack is assigned.
3. Each listed team they are not in is joined.
4. They are recorded as accepted, which counts against the quota.

Assignments are additive. An existing member keeps what they have, gains any listed roles and teams they lack, and loses nothing.

Role and team failures do not block membership. If a role or team step fails, the person is already in the organization, but the page shows an **Error Accepting Invitation** message with the probable cause and remediation, and offers **Retry** and **Go to dashboard**. Retrying is safe: it does not duplicate the membership or the acceptance. A stored team that has left the organization is skipped and recorded on the acceptance event, and the acceptance still succeeds.

Each acceptance writes one event, `<email> accepted invitation "<name>"`. Creating, editing, and deleting invitations write no dedicated event.

### Accepting by situation

- **New person, no account:** opening the link while signed out saves the invitation in a 30-minute cookie and sends the person to registration for your organization. After sign-up and sign-in, the invitation is accepted, the organization is selected, and the person lands on the dashboard. If the cookie lapses, they reopen the link.
- **Existing account, not a member:** the same flow, but the person signs in instead of registering. The signed-out redirect goes to the registration page, so they navigate to sign-in from there. The cookie survives.
- **Existing member:** no duplicate membership. Missing listed roles and teams are added. The acceptance still counts against the quota, and a full quota refuses them even though they are already a member.
- **A revoked or invalid link:** the accept page loads and shows the refusal reason, rather than a not-found page.

### Choosing what accepting an invitation does

Every invitation has an `acceptanceOutcome` that decides where the accepting person ends up. In the create and edit dialogs it is the **When accepted** choice. **Direct membership** is the default. **Child organization** appears only if you have the **Create Organization** permission in the current organization. If you lack it and edit an invitation that already uses Child organization, the choice is shown selected but cannot be changed.

<img src="./images/acceptance-outcome.png" alt="When accepted picker in the Create New Invitation dialog" style="width:50%; height:auto;" />

| `acceptanceOutcome` | Result of accepting |
| :--- | :--- |
| `direct_membership` (default) | The person joins the inviting organization with the invitation's roles and teams. Role and team failures do not undo the membership. |
| `child_organization` | A new organization named **My Organization** is created as a child of the inviting organization. The person is its owner and Organization Admin, it gets the standard **My Team** and **My Workspace**, the invitation's roles are granted in it, and teams with the same names and descriptions as the invitation's teams are created in it with the person as a member. The person does not become a member of the inviting organization, and the inviting organization's own teams are unchanged. The acceptance is all or nothing: if any part fails, nothing is created and the quota is not used. |

For both outcomes:

- Every team on an invitation must belong to the inviting organization. An invitation listing another organization's team is refused when it is created or edited.
- Acceptance counts once per person. Accepting again creates no second child organization and uses no more quota.
- A person who creates a new account through your open sign-up invitation does not also receive a separate personal organization; the invitation decides where they land. If the invitation turns out not to apply, such as when its quota is used up, a personal organization is created as usual.

#### Branding of a child organization

A child organization created through a `child_organization` invitation starts with your organization's branding by default. The invitation's `childOrganizationBranding`, shown in the invitation dialogs as **Child organization branding**, can change that. It is ignored for `direct_membership`.

| `childOrganizationBranding` | The child organization starts with |
| :--- | :--- |
| `parent` (default) | A copy of your organization's branding: theme (logos and colors), sign-in page branding, links (including social profiles), and the sign-in page carousel setting. |
| `provider` | A copy of the platform provider's branding. |
| `none` | No branding of its own. |

The copy is taken once, when the child organization is created. Later changes to your branding are not carried over, and changes the child organization's admins make do not affect yours. Organizations created directly, not through an invitation, are unaffected.

#### Email verification

Someone who signs up with email and password through your open signup invitation must verify their email address before a `direct_membership` invitation adds them to your organization. Until then they are not a member, and they cannot sign in. They join on their first sign-in after verifying. A `child_organization` invitation does not wait: the new account's own child organization is created at sign-up, because it gives the person nothing of yours beyond a place beneath you. Either way the account becomes active once the address is verified.

## The open sign-up invitation

The open sign-up invitation is the one that admits people who sign in through your organization's own address, such as a custom domain. You designate it in either of two places:

- The **Open Org Invitation** selection when you edit the organization. Writing it needs Organization Admin in the organization or in its parent.
- The `isDefault` property on the invitation. Setting or clearing it needs Manage Invitations.

The edit-organization selection wins when it names an invitation that exists in the same organization. A selection that points at a deleted invitation, or at another organization's invitation, is ignored and the `isDefault` invitation is used. Releasing the mark on the invitation that the selection names, or deleting that invitation, clears the selection. With neither a selection nor a mark, nobody joins.

### How it is applied at sign-in

It is applied whenever someone signs in through your organization's address, on every sign-in method the address offers, including email and password and social sign-in. A person who has an account and has never been a member becomes one on that sign-in, with the roles and teams the invitation grants. When it is a `child_organization` invitation, the person instead receives their own child organization.

It applies only to people who are not already members:

- **Roles and teams are never re-applied.** If you remove a role or team from someone who joined this way, signing in again does not restore it.
- **Each person counts once.** Repeated sign-ins do not raise the acceptance count.

{{< alert type="warning" title="When open sign-up adds nobody" >}}
A person can sign in successfully and still not join. The open sign-up invitation applies only when all of these hold:

- Its status is `enabled`.
- Its expiry has not passed.
- Its quota is not reached.
- The person's email matches its `emails` list, or the list is empty.
- For a direct membership invitation, the person's email address is verified.

When one fails, a non-member signs in as a platform user with no membership and no roles in your organization, and sees no error. Existing members are unaffected. Check these properties first when people who sign in at your address are missing from the [Users page]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md" >}}).
{{< /alert >}}

## Invite one person directly

**Needs:** Invite User to Organization.

Use the direct invite to bring in one person who has no account. You supply an email address, optional first and last name, and optionally the organization roles and teams the person should have.

Unlike an invitation, the direct invite acts before the person does anything:

- Layer5 Cloud creates a Pending account, adds it to the organization and the listed teams, and sends an email with a sign-up link already filled in with the name, email, and organization.
- The email is always sent. There is no quota, expiry, or acceptance step, and no invitation record to disable.
- Roles are applied right after the email is sent, under the rules in [Change a member's roles]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#change-a-members-roles" >}}). A role you may not grant is skipped with an `unauthorized to assign` message.
- If the address already has an account, the invite is refused with `User with email '<email>' already exists`. Add that person as an existing user instead.

## Examples

| Goal | Audience | Grants | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Onboard one new employee | Their exact address | Their role and project team | Quota 1 |
| Open registration to a company | `@yourcompany.com` | A default role | Optional expiry |
| Run a community challenge | Empty (public) | A temporary role such as Academy Learner | Expiry at close of registration, quota at the participant cap |
| Give a partner temporary access | `@partner.com` | One shared project team only | Expiry at project end |

For learner programs, the seats available depend on your subscription plan. See [how the billable user count works]({{< ref "cloud/guides/account/managing-subscriptions.md#how-the-billable-user-count-works" >}}). Expiry stops new signups only. When a project ends, [remove the people]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#remove-a-user-from-an-organization" >}}) who joined through it.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Platform Development"
url: /cloud/academy/platform-development/index.md
description: Preview Academy content locally, develop the Academy theme against real content, and run an end-to-end build before you publish. Includes how the Academy repositories fit together.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Academy is assembled from separate repositories for content, theme, and build. This page shows how to preview content on your machine, how to change the theme and see the result on real content, and how to run a production-like build before you publish. Most authors need only the first workflow. Theme development and end-to-end builds are for contributors to the platform itself.

## How the repositories fit together

| Repository | Role | Who touches it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content repository, such as the `academy-example` starter or an organization's own repository | Your learning paths, challenges, and certifications, plus the workflow that announces a new version | Content authors |
| `academy-theme` | Layouts, colors, fonts, and the standard shortcodes. Content repositories import it as a Go module, so you never fork it to author content. | Platform contributors |
| `academy-build` | The Hugo configuration for the production build. It pins the version of the theme and of every content module. | Platform maintainers |

The path from a content change to a live Academy has three stages:

1. **Release.** Publishing a release in your content repository runs a local build as a sanity check. If the build is clean, the workflow calls the Layer5 Cloud publish API with your organization ID and the release version. The workflow validates and notifies. It does not build the site.
2. **Build.** Layer5 Cloud dispatches the central build for your organization at that version. The build collects the theme and every content module, applies the theme to the content, and produces one static site.
3. **Deploy.** The build pushes the finished site to Layer5 Cloud, which serves it to learners.

If the build fails, the previous version of your Academy stays live. Set up the repository and its publish secrets as described in [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}). Start from the [`academy-example`](https://github.com/layer5io/academy-example) template.

## Prerequisites

- Git and a recent Go toolchain. Content repositories use Go modules to import the theme.
- The tools that `make setup` installs, including Hugo.
- For end-to-end testing: write access to the build repository and a staging Layer5 Cloud environment. Layer5 platform maintainers hold these.

## Preview content locally

Run these commands from a content repository. The official `layer5-academy` repository is a feature-complete example of a large content repository.

```bash
go mod tidy
make setup
make site
```

`go mod tidy` verifies the module dependencies. `make setup` installs the tools and modules. `make site` starts the Hugo development server. Open `http://localhost:1313/academy` to read your content.

Local preview shows structure, content, and links. It does not show your organization's branding, and it cannot score assessments, count attempts, or record progress, because those run on the Layer5 Cloud server. See [Add Assessments]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/integrating-assessments-in-the-academy.md" >}}#test-your-assessment).

## Develop the theme against real content

Point a content repository at your local copy of the theme with a Go module `replace` directive.

1. Change the theme in your local clone of `academy-theme`.
2. In the content repository's `go.mod`, add:

   ```go
   replace github.com/layer5io/academy-theme => ../academy-theme
   ```

3. Run `go mod tidy`, then restart `make site`. The preview now renders with your local theme.

Remove the `replace` line and run `go mod tidy` again before you commit. A committed `replace` points other contributors, and the build, at a path that exists only on your machine.

Content repositories customize shortcodes only. They cannot override layouts or archetypes. To request a layout, archetype, or theme change, open an issue against the theme repository.

## Run an end-to-end build against staging

Use this workflow when a change must be verified inside the Layer5 Cloud interface before release. Run every command from the root of a local `academy-build` clone.

1. Install dependencies once:

   ```bash
   make setup
   ```

2. Point the build at local copies of any repository you changed, by adding `replace` directives to its `go.mod`:

   ```go
   replace github.com/layer5io/academy-theme => ../academy-theme
   replace github.com/layer5io/layer5-academy => ../layer5-academy
   ```

3. Build for staging:

   ```bash
   make stg-build
   ```

4. Sync the generated files to the staging Layer5 Cloud environment:

   ```bash
   make sync-with-cloud
   ```

5. Verify the result in staging. The change appears after about 10 minutes.

{{< alert type="warning" title="Local preview is not the final product" >}}
Layer5 Cloud wraps the Academy content in its own interface. CSS class conflicts and differences in how JavaScript runs inside the larger application can make the final page look or behave differently from the local preview. Verify every change in staging before you treat it as done.
{{< /alert >}}

## Inspect a production-like build

To check the final output without syncing to Layer5 Cloud, build locally from `academy-build`:

```bash
make prod-build
```

The build writes static files, including the HTML and JSON that Layer5 Cloud serves, to `public/`. Inspect them to diagnose build-time problems before you deploy.

## Working practices

- **Remove local `replace` directives** from `go.mod` and run `go mod tidy` before every commit.
- **Test in widening circles.** Preview locally, run a production-like build, then verify in staging.
- **Commit before you test in staging**, so you can trace and revert the exact change that you tested.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Workspaces"
url: /cloud/concepts/workspaces/index.md
description: A workspace groups teams, environments, designs, and views inside one organization, and decides which connections a team can reach.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A workspace is a named grouping inside an organization that brings together the teams who do a piece of work, the environments they deploy to, and the designs and views they work on. Workspaces exist so an administrator can draw a boundary around a project or a stage of a pipeline, such as staging or production, and decide in one place which teams reach which infrastructure connections.

A workspace does two separate jobs, and keeping them apart is the key to the model:

- **It organizes resources.** Designs and views live in a workspace, and the workspace decides which organization they are listed under.
- **It grants connection access.** Assigning a team to a workspace gives that team's members read-only access to the connections in the workspace's environments. That is the only access a team assignment grants.

Workspaces and environments appear together in the Spaces area of Layer5 Cloud, which also shows counts of your organization's environments, workspaces, and connections.

## What a workspace contains

A workspace belongs to exactly one organization for its whole life. Editing a workspace changes its name, description, or metadata, never its organization. To have a workspace in another organization, create one there.

A workspace holds zero or more of each of the following:

| Member | How many workspaces it can be in | What assigning it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team | Any number | Members of the team gain read-only access to the connections in this workspace's environments. The team must belong to the workspace's organization. |
| Environment | Any number | The environment's connections become reachable by the workspace's teams. The environment must belong to the workspace's organization. |
| Design | At most one | The design moves here. Assigning a design to a workspace removes it from the workspace it was in. |
| View | At most one | The view moves here, the same way a design does. |

Assigning a team or environment that is already in the workspace changes nothing. Creating a workspace assigns no team and no environment; you add them afterward.

### Designs live in one workspace at a time

Because a design sits in at most one workspace, assigning it to a workspace is a move, not a copy. The workspace a design sits in decides two things:

- The organization under which the design is listed.
- The organization in which the Share Design permission is checked when someone shares the design.

Moving a design requires the Assign Designs to Workspaces permission in the destination workspace's organization. Layer5 Cloud does not also require access to the workspace the design leaves. When you list the designs you can add to a workspace, the list shows only designs you own that are not already in it.

## Who sees a workspace and what a team assignment grants

Workspace visibility is organization-wide by design. Every member of an organization can list and open every workspace in that organization, whether or not one of their teams is assigned to it. Team assignment does not narrow what you see. The Workspaces, Environments, and connection areas of the Cloud UI appear only to people who hold the matching View Workspace, View Environment, and View Connections permissions.

Team assignment grants exactly one thing: **read-only access to the connections, and their credentials, in the workspace's environments.**

It does not grant access to designs. Placing a private design in a workspace and assigning a team to that workspace does not let the team read the design. To give people access to a design, share it with them; see [Share a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/collaborating/sharing-designs/index.md" >}}).

### The access chain for connections

A member of a team reaches a connection through a chain of four live links. Breaking any one of them ends the access.

| Link | Created by | Broken by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. User is a member of a team | Adding the user to the team | Removing the user from the team |
| 2. Team is assigned to a workspace | Assign team to workspace | Removing the team from the workspace, or deleting the workspace |
| 3. Environment is assigned to the workspace | Assign environment to workspace | Removing the environment from the workspace, or deleting either one |
| 4. Connection is assigned to the environment | Assign connections to environment | Removing the connection from the environment, or deleting the environment |

The result is read-only. Modifying or deleting a connection still requires owning it. Two other routes reach a connection independently of this chain: owning it, and holding the View All Organizations key. See [Environments]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/environments.md" >}}) for the full access rules.

## Lifecycle

- **Default workspace.** Every organization receives a workspace when it is created, so designs always have somewhere to live.
- **Names.** A name and description are each limited to 255 characters. Names are not unique: two workspaces in one organization can share a name.
- **Editing.** Only the fields you change are updated; the others keep their values.
- **The last workspace stays.** An organization always keeps at least one workspace. Deleting the last one is refused with `cannot delete workspace: at least one workspace must exist for the organization`. Two simultaneous deletes cannot both succeed and leave the organization empty.
- **Deleting a workspace** ends every team, environment, design, and view assignment it holds, in one step. The teams, environments, designs, views, and connections themselves remain. Designs and views that were in the workspace are left in no workspace until you assign them to another one. Team members lose any connection access that flowed through the deleted workspace.

## Recent activity

Each workspace records an activity log: creating, editing, and deleting the workspace, and assigning or removing teams, environments, designs, and views. Every entry carries the email address of the person who acted. Reading the log requires the View Workspace permission.

## Permissions

Every workspace action is checked in the organization that owns the workspace. Creating a workspace is checked in the organization you create it in.

{{< keys-matrix caption="Workspace permissions" functions="View Workspace|Create Workspace|Edit Workspace|Delete Workspace|Assign team to workspace|Remove team from workspace|Assign environment to workspace|Remove environment from workspace|Assign Designs to Workspaces|Remove Designs from Workspaces|Assign Views to Workspace|Unassign Views from Workspace" >}}

## Plan availability

{{< feature-tiers categories="Workspaces" functions="My Workspace|Shared Workspaces" >}}

The matrix shows how workspaces are packaged across plans. Layer5 Cloud enforces no plan check on workspace actions: creating, editing, deleting, and assigning work the same on every plan, governed only by the permissions above.

## Related

- [Manage Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/guides/workspaces/managing-workspaces/index.md" >}}) covers creating, editing, and deleting workspaces and assigning their members.
- [Environments]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/environments.md" >}}) explains the deploy targets a workspace exposes.
- [Teams]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/teams/_index.md" >}}) explains how teams group people.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Environments"
url: /cloud/concepts/environments/index.md
description: An environment is a named group of connections that forms a deploy target and the unit through which workspaces expose connections to teams.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An environment is a named group of connections, such as Kubernetes clusters, together with the credentials those connections use. Environments matter for two reasons:

- **An environment is a deploy target.** When you deploy a design, you choose the environment to deploy it to, and the design deploys to that environment's connections.
- **An environment is how a workspace exposes connections.** A workspace never holds connections directly. It holds environments, and teams assigned to the workspace reach the connections inside them.

Group connections the way you deploy: one environment per pipeline stage, region, or purpose, so that choosing a target means choosing one environment instead of a list of clusters.

## Scope and membership

An environment belongs to one organization for its whole life. Editing an environment never changes its organization.

| Relationship | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Connection in environments | A connection can be in any number of environments. Adding it to one does not remove it from another. |
| Environment in workspaces | An environment can be in any number of workspaces in its organization. |
| Who sees an environment | Every member of the organization can list and open every environment in it. Team membership does not narrow the list. |

Names and descriptions are limited to 255 characters. Names are not unique: two environments in one organization can share a name.

## Choosing an environment at deploy time

Deploying a design happens in Kanvas. The deploy action offers environments from your organization's whole list at the moment you deploy. The workspace the design sits in does not limit that choice, so a design in a staging workspace can still be deployed to a production environment. Choose the target deliberately. See [Deploy a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/deploying-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Access to connections and credentials

A user can read a connection, and the credential it uses, when any one of these holds:

| Route | What it grants | How it ends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You own the connection | Read, modify, and delete | - |
| You belong to a team assigned to a workspace that contains an environment that contains the connection | Read only | Removing you from the team, the team from the workspace, the environment from the workspace, or the connection from the environment, or deleting the workspace or environment |
| You hold the [View All Organizations key]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}) | Read access to every connection and credential in every organization | Losing the key |

Only ownership allows changes. Access through a workspace is always read-only, however many workspaces lead to the same connection.

This chain governs connections and credentials only. Designs and views are not opened by environment or workspace assignment; share a design to give someone access to it. See [Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/workspaces.md" >}}) for the full access chain.

## Platform-provisioned environments

Some environments are created by Layer5 Cloud itself to hold organization configuration, such as sign-in providers or the mail server. They appear in your organization's environment list, but they are not deploy targets you manage:

- They cannot be deleted. The attempt is refused with `this environment is provisioned by the platform and cannot be deleted here`.
- Connections cannot be assigned to them or detached from them through the normal environment controls.
- They cannot be added to a workspace. If one is already in a workspace, you can remove it.

Every environment you create is an ordinary environment.

## Deleting an environment

Deleting an environment ends its connection assignments and its workspace assignments in one step. The connections remain, and keep their membership in any other environment. Teams that reached a connection only through the deleted environment lose that access.

## Limits and behavior

- **Editing replaces both fields.** An environment edit sets both the name and the description. A field left out of the request becomes empty, so always send both.
- **Organization is fixed.** An edit never moves an environment to another organization.
- **Removing a connection that was never assigned** is refused with `no such connection assignment`.

## Permissions

Every environment action is checked in the organization that owns the environment. Creating an environment is checked in the organization you create it in.

{{< keys-matrix caption="Environment permissions" functions="View Environment|Create Environment|Edit Environment|Delete Environment|Assign connections to environment|Remove connections from environment|Assign environment to workspace|Remove environment from workspace" >}}

## Plan availability

The feature matrix lists environments under the Enterprise plan. Layer5 Cloud does not refuse environment actions by plan: creating, editing, deleting, and assigning environments are governed only by the permissions above.

## Related

- [Manage Environments]({{< ref "cloud/guides/workspaces/managing-environments/index.md" >}}) covers creating environments and assigning connections.
- [Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/workspaces.md" >}}) explains how environments reach teams.
- [Promote a Design from Staging to Production]({{< ref "cloud/tutorials/promoting-a-design.md" >}}) puts environments and workspaces to work together.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Keys"
url: /cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys/index.md
description: How keys work as the unit of permission in Layer5 Cloud: how a key reaches a user, where it takes effect, who can change it, and how to trace a missing permission.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A key is a named permission for exactly one action, such as Create Organization, Approve Catalog Request, or Download Token. Every authorization decision in Layer5 Cloud comes down to one question: does this user hold the key this action requires, in this organization? Understanding keys tells you why a user can or cannot do something, and whether the model fits the access rules you need.

## How a key reaches a user

Keys roll up in three layers. A [keychain]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}) groups related keys, a [role]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) groups keychains, and a user holds roles in an organization or a team. A user never receives a key directly: granting a key means placing it in a keychain that belongs to a role the user holds.

Keys, keychains, and roles are defined once for the whole Layer5 Cloud deployment. They are not copied or customized per organization. What varies per organization is which roles a user holds there. A user's effective keys in an organization are the union of the keys from every role they hold in that organization, so the same person can hold a key in one organization and lack it in another. Holding an additional role only adds keys; it never removes any. Provider Admin holds every key and passes every check in every organization. [Security Boundaries]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/_index.md#security-boundaries" >}}) explains why the organization is the authorization boundary.

A default installation ships more than 240 keys grouped into 30 default keychains. The system account owns every default key and keychain.

## Anatomy of a key

The Keys tab of the Security page lists each key with these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Key ID | A UUID that identifies the key. |
| Name | The action the key grants, for example Create Token. |
| Description | What the action does. |
| Category | The resource the key acts on, for example Token or Keychains. |
| Subcategory | The default keychain family the key belongs to, for example Security Management. |
| Owner | The account that owns the key. Default keys are owned by the system. |
| Created At, Deleted At | When the key was created and, if deleted, when. |

Most keys follow one of four shapes. A few grant an action that is not a simple change to a resource.

| Type | Grants | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Create | Creating a resource | Create Organization |
| View | Seeing a resource or a list | View Keys |
| Edit | Changing a resource | Edit Keychain |
| Delete | Removing a resource | Delete Token |
| Action | A workflow step | Approve Catalog Request |

## Where a key takes effect

A key has an effect only where something checks it. Two places do:

- **The server.** On a guarded action, the server resolves the organization of the request and tests whether the user holds the required key there. A missing key returns HTTP 403 with a JSON body. This check is what actually protects the action.
- **The interface.** The Layer5 Cloud UI reads your effective keys for the organization in context and disables or hides controls for actions you cannot perform.

Not every key is checked in both places. Some security keys are enforced only by the interface: the server does not test Delete Token, and tests Create Token only when you approve a desktop app or CLI sign-in. Changes to keys, keychains, and roles are checked on the server, which also requires the Provider Admin role for the whole deployment. The [Security reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md" >}}) lists which security keys the server enforces.

Because a key grants nothing unless a check names it, a custom key is only a record. Adding one to a keychain and a role changes no behavior anywhere.

## Who can see and change keys

Every signed-in user can open the [Keys](https://cloud.layer5.io/security/keys) tab. It lists the system's keys plus any keys you created, and searches by key name. Viewing keys requires no key on the server.

Creating or editing a key, including changing which keychains carry it, requires the Edit Key key. Deleting a key requires the Delete Key key. Both belong to the Provider Management keychain, which only Provider Admin holds by default, and the server also requires the caller to hold the Provider Admin role for the whole deployment. Only a Provider Admin can change which keys a keychain carries or which keychains a role includes. On hosted Layer5 Cloud, Layer5 operates the Provider Admin role, so organizations cannot change keys. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator's Provider Admins can.

Deleting a key is a soft delete. The key stops granting access immediately and disappears from every keychain that contained it. Because keys are deployment-wide, editing or deleting one changes access for every organization at once.

## Auditing key use

Keys do not carry a usage counter; the Keys tab has no "last used" column. What a key's use leaves behind is the event the action produced, and those events are what you audit. The Audit Logs page answers who did what, and when:

- **User ID** - the account that performed the action, which is the account whose key was exercised.
