- **Category** and **Action** - what was done, for example a workspace being created or a team being deleted. These correspond to the capability the key grants.
- **Acted Upon** - the resource the action affected.
- **Description** and **Created At** - the detail of the event and when it occurred.

Filter by actor to follow one user's activity, or by category and action to see everyone who exercised a capability over a period. The log you read belongs to the organization you currently have selected.

## Tracing a missing permission

When a user cannot perform an action, work from the key outward:

1. Identify the key the action requires. A 403 response or a disabled control both point to a missing key.
2. Find the default keychain and the roles that carry that key in the [Roles and Permissions reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).
3. Check which roles the user holds in the organization the request ran in, not in the organization they usually work in.
4. Grant a role that carries the key in that organization. Do not add the keychain to a shared role unless every holder of that role in every organization should gain it.

## Limits

- Keys do not rotate or expire. A key grants its action until it is deleted or removed from the user's roles.
- Keys have no per-key usage counter. Use the Audit Logs page instead.
- On hosted Layer5 Cloud, only Provider Admins edit or delete keys.
- A key and its keychains are deployment-wide. Organizations tailor access by assigning roles, not by changing keys.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Manage Teams"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/managing-teams/index.md
description: Create a team, add and remove members, assign Team Admins, attach a team to a workspace, and delete a team.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This guide covers the administrator tasks for teams. For what a team is and how it grants access, read the [Teams concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/teams/_index.md" >}}).

{{< keys-matrix caption="Team permissions" functions="Create Team|Edit Team|Delete Team|View All Teams|Add User to Team|Remove User from Team|Leave Team|Assign team to workspace" >}}

## Create a team

**Needs:** the Create Team permission in your current organization.

A team takes a name and a description. The name is required on the Teams page; Layer5 Cloud does not check it for uniqueness or length beyond 255 characters. You can pick initial members from the organization's users in the same step.

The creator becomes the team's owner, a member, and a Team Admin. Members chosen at creation are added as plain members with no role.

The team is created in the organization you have selected. Confirm the organization switcher shows the organization you intend before you create it.

## Add members

**Needs:** Team Admin or owner of the team, or Provider Admin.

1. Make sure each person is already a member of the organization. Add them first if not.
2. Add them to the team.

Added people receive an email unless they have turned off organization and team user-management notifications. Adding an existing member is harmless and changes nothing.

Adding someone to the team does not give them a role in it. A member with no role holds only what they receive through their organization roles and the team's workspace assignments.

## Make a member a Team Admin

**Needs:** Team Admin of the team, Organization Admin or a holder of Assign User Roles, or Provider Admin.

Team Admin is the only role offered for team scope. Assigning it sets the person's role list in that team: the roles you submit replace the roles they held there, and an empty list removes every team role while keeping the membership. The person must belong to the organization. Granting the role to someone not yet on the team also adds them to it.

Team Admin permissions apply across the whole organization, not just this team. See [How a team grants access]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/teams/_index.md#how-a-team-grants-access" >}}).

## Remove a member or leave a team

| You are | You can |
| --- | --- |
| Team Admin removing someone else | Remove them |
| A member without Team Admin | Leave the team (remove yourself) |
| A Team Admin | Not remove yourself; another Team Admin or a Provider Admin removes you |
| The owner | Not leave; delete the team instead |
| Provider Admin | Remove anyone except the owner removing themselves |

Removal ends the person's membership and all their roles in the team. It leaves their organization membership and other teams unchanged. A removed owner remains the owner of record.

## Give a team access to a workspace

**Needs:** Assign team to workspace in the workspace's organization (Organization Admin, Workspace Admin, Academy Admin, Provider Admin).

Assign the team to the workspace. The team and the workspace must belong to the same organization. Unassigning needs Remove team from workspace. See [Workspaces]({{< ref "cloud/guides/workspaces/_index.md" >}}).

## Delete a team

**Needs:** Organization Admin or Owner, Provider Admin, or the person who is both owner and Team Admin of the team. Team Admin alone and owner alone are refused.

Deleting is irreversible and removes only the team record: members keep their user accounts, and resources remain. Before you delete, do these so no access remains:

1. Remove every member from the team.
2. Unassign the team from each workspace it has access to.

## Limits and failure modes

- Deleting the team does not remove its members' team roles or workspace assignments on its own; do the steps above.
- Updates that fail partway can leave a team without its creator as member. If the creator is not listed, add them to the team.
- A team cannot be moved to another owner. Plan to keep at least one other Team Admin so someone can administer the team if the owner leaves the organization.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Troubleshoot Email Delivery"
url: /cloud/guides/self-hosted/operating/smtp/index.md
description: Diagnose why a self-hosted Layer5 Cloud is not sending mail: the shared mail server's requirements, what the server checks at startup, how to test delivery, how mail is routed, and what each error code means.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Layer5 Cloud sends two kinds of mail. **Application mail** (invitations, notifications, welcome mail) leaves the Layer5 Cloud server, through an organization's own mail server when one is turned on, and otherwise through the **shared mail server** you configure in the chart's `smtp` values. **Identity mail** (email verification and account recovery) is produced by Kratos and reaches the same server only when you select the HTTP courier. See [Plan a Deployment]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/planning/_index.md#mail" >}}). This guide helps you find which of those paths is failing and why.

{{< alert title="Read this before upgrading to v1.0.253 or later" type="warning" >}}
The shared mail server you configure with `SMTP_HOST` and `SMTP_PORT` is screened the same way an organization's own mail server is, and **the server refuses to start when it fails that screen**. If `SMTP_HOST` points at an in-cluster relay, at a non-submission port such as mailpit on `1025`, or at a plaintext MTA, this deployment stops on upgrade and says so at startup. See [Constraints on the shared mail server](#constraints-on-the-shared-mail-server).
{{< /alert >}}

## Debug Log Levels

To enable email debugging, set `env.loglevel` in your Helm values to `5` (debug) or `6` (trace) and upgrade. The chart default is `4` (info). Return it to `4` when you finish, because debug logs record more detail.

```yaml
env:
  loglevel: 5
```

## Testing Email Configuration

### 1. Email Configuration Test Endpoint (Provider Admin Only) {#1-email-configuration-test-endpoint}

Check that the four `SMTP_*` values are configured, without sending an email.
**Both verbs of this endpoint require authentication and the provider admin
role**, so the `GET` must carry a credential. It validates configuration only -
it does not dial the SMTP server.

```bash
curl -X GET "https://your-domain.com/api/system/email/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
```

**Expected Response (Success):**

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Email configuration is valid",
  "timestamp": "1695312000"
}
```

The response carries the verdict only. It does not report `smtp_host`,
`smtp_port` or `smtp_username`: those are the deployment's own relay settings,
and `SMTP_USERNAME` is an email address. Read the configured values from your
deployment configuration instead.

**Expected Response (Error):** `500 Internal Server Error`, as plain text
rather than JSON. The body is the error's short description alone - the full
error, which names the relay, stays in the log:

```text
SMTP configuration error for field 'SMTP_HOST'
```

**Expected Response (Unauthenticated):** `401 Unauthorized`

```json
{
  "message": "user must be logged in to perform this operation"
}
```

**Expected Response (Authenticated, not a provider admin):** `403 Forbidden`

```json
{
  "message": "user you@example.com must be Provider Admin to perform this operation"
}
```

### 2. Send a test email {#send-a-test-email}

Send an actual test email to verify delivery end to end. The endpoint requires authentication and the Provider Admin role:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://cloud.layer5.io/api/system/email/test" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "to": "test@example.com",
    "subject": "Layer5 Cloud Email Test"
  }'
```

**Request Body:**

```json
{
  "to": "test@example.com",
  "subject": "Layer5 Cloud Email Test (optional)"
}
```

**Expected Response (Success):**

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Test email sent successfully",
  "timestamp": "1695312000",
  "sentTo": "test@example.com"
}
```

**Expected Response (Unauthenticated / not a provider admin):** the same `401`
and `403` JSON bodies as the `GET` above - both verbs carry the same
provider-admin gate.

**Expected Response (Error - Invalid Email):** `400 Bad Request`, as plain text:

```text
Invalid email address format
```

**Expected Response (Error - Email Configuration):** `500 Internal Server
Error`, as plain text. The configuration is checked before anything is sent, so
this is the same verdict the `GET` gives:

```text
SMTP configuration error for field 'SMTP_HOST'
```

**Expected Response (Error - the send itself failed):** `500 Internal Server
Error`, as plain text, carrying the short description only. The relay's own
reply, the resolved endpoint and the SMTP username stay in the log:

```text
Failed to send email with subject 'Layer5 Cloud Email Test' to recipients: test@example.com
```

### 3. Required Environment Variables

Either set all four values or leave all four empty. A deployment that leaves
them empty is a supported state - it simply sends no mail - but a deployment
that sets some of them and not others does not start.

| Variable | Chart value | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SMTP_HOST` | `smtp.smtphost` | Must resolve to a publicly routable address |
| `SMTP_PORT` | `smtp.smtpport` | One of `25`, `465`, `587`, `2525` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME` | `smtp.smtpusername` | A full address: it becomes the `From:` header |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `smtp.smtppassword` | The mailbox password or app password |

`SMTP_PORT` also decides how the session is encrypted, because the four keys
carry no mode of their own: **`465` means implicit TLS**, and every other
permitted port takes STARTTLS. Read
[Constraints on the shared mail server](#constraints-on-the-shared-mail-server)
before you change either value.

## Constraints on the Shared Mail Server

Since **v1.0.253**, mail is routed per Organization: an Organization that has
[brought its own mail server]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/org-management/bring-your-own-mail-server.md" >}})
sends through that server, and everyone else sends through the shared mail
server your deployment configures. Both now go through **one** send primitive,
so the shared mail server is screened exactly as a tenant's is.

That screening is new. The previous send path applied none of it, so a
deployment that has been sending mail happily can be refused after an upgrade.
A self-hosted install that points `SMTP_HOST` at an internal, plaintext, or non-submission relay can be refused.

### What is refused

| Constraint | What is refused | How to fix it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Submission port allowlist** | any port other than `25`, `465`, `587` or `2525` - for example mailpit on `1025` | move the relay onto a submission port, or put a submission-port listener in front of it |
| **Internal-address screen** | an `SMTP_HOST` that resolves to loopback, RFC 1918 private, IPv6 unique-local, RFC 6598 carrier-shared or link-local space - for example an in-cluster `mailhog.default.svc` | point `SMTP_HOST` at a publicly routable relay. There is deliberately no allowlist or opt-out setting |
| **STARTTLS is required** | a relay that answers but does not advertise the extension - a plaintext internal MTA | enable STARTTLS on the relay. It is refused rather than downgraded, because a downgrade would put the mailbox password on the wire in the clear |
| **`SMTP_PORT` parses as a number** | a stray character or space in the value, such as `"587 "` | correct the value in your Secret or environment file |
| **`SMTP_USERNAME` parses as an RFC 5322 address** | a bare mailbox name such as `no-reply` with no domain - it becomes the `From:` header | use the full mailbox address |

**Every address `SMTP_HOST` resolves to is screened, not just the one a
connection happens to use.** A host publishing both a public and a private
record is refused.

Port `465` is the exception to STARTTLS: it speaks TLS from the first byte, and
the deployment selects that mode automatically from the port. You do not
configure the encryption mode separately.

### What happens at startup

The server validates the shared mail server once, at startup, rather than
waiting for somebody's password reset to fail silently. Only the first row below
stops the deployment:

| At startup | Verdict | What you see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The configuration fails one of the constraints above | **the server exits** | `meshery_cloud-3301` at Error, then exit code 1 |
| The relay could not be reached at all - DNS did not answer, or the connection did not complete | the server starts | `meshery_cloud-3302` at Error |
| The relay answered but its certificate did not verify - expired, wrong host name, or an untrusted issuer | the server starts | `meshery_cloud-3304` at Error, naming the relay host |
| None of the four `SMTP_*` values is set | the server starts | a warning naming the first unset key |
| The relay answered and the screens passed | the server starts | `INFO The shared mail relay answered on smtp.example.com:587 over starttls` |

The two non-fatal failures are still failures: **no mail leaves over the shared
mail server until they clear.** Treat `3302` and `3304` at startup as a page,
not a note. They are separate codes because the remedy is different - `3302` is
the network, `3304` is the relay's certificate.

A refusal is fatal on purpose. The alternative is a deployment that comes up
green and drops every message silently, which is the failure this check exists
to convert into a refusal to start.

The startup check **does not authenticate and sends no message**. A rotated
password is not a reason a deployment will not start, and an authentication
failure is not one of the verdicts this check acts on.

{{< alert title="The configuration test endpoint does not dial" type="info" >}}
`GET /api/system/email/test` now applies everything above that can be decided
without a connection - the presence of all four keys, the port allowlist, the
shape of the host, and the two parse rules. It still opens no connection, so
whether the relay offers STARTTLS is the startup check's answer to give, not
this endpoint's.
{{< /alert >}}

## Flow Emails (Kratos Integration)

Identity mail reaches Layer5 Cloud only when Kratos uses the HTTP courier, which posts each message to `/api/identity/flow/emails`. Layer5 Cloud then renders it with the signup organization's branding and sends it like other application mail. Under the HTTP courier there is no SMTP fallback. When Layer5 Cloud answers anything but a success, Kratos retries the message (five times by default) and then abandons it, with no visible error to the user, so an unreachable or misconfigured Layer5 Cloud silently stops verification and recovery mail. With the default SMTP courier, Kratos sends the mail itself through `kratos.kratos.config.courier.smtp.connection_uri`, and none of the shared-relay rules on this page apply to it.

**Only two Kratos template types are dispatched:** `verification_code_valid`
and `recovery_code_valid`. Every environment runs the `code` strategy for
recovery and verification, so those are the only two Kratos emits - and the
unknown-recipient notices (`recovery_code_invalid`, `verification_code_invalid`)
are deliberately not sent. Any other type is acknowledged with a `200` and
logged as unsupported rather than mailed; a `200` for one of those means the
request was accepted and no message was sent.

```log
DEBUG Flow email attempt.  subject_template:  email-templates/valid/email-recover-subject.body.gotmpl , body_template:  email-templates/valid/email-recover.body.gotmpl , organization_id:  0e6b7ba0-... , recipient:  user@example.com
DEBUG Flow email delivery failed.  error_type:  *errors.Error , template_type:  recovery_code_valid , organization_id:  0e6b7ba0-... , recipient:  user@example.com
INFO Flow email sent.  template_type:  recovery_code_valid , recipient:  user@example.com
```

## Which Mail Server a Message Left Through

Every message this deployment sends is routed by the reader's Organization. An
Organization that has configured its own mail server, verified its from domain
and turned it on sends through that server; every other message takes the shared
mail server configured by `SMTP_HOST`.

That routing produces its own log lines, and a self-hosted operator will meet
them without having configured anything themselves:

- **The Organization's mail server was used and the message was accepted.** No
  operator action; the verdict is recorded against that Organization's delivery
  health, which its administrators read on the Email tab.

- **The Organization's mail server refused the message and fallback is on.** The
  message is re-sent over the shared mail server, arriving from this
  deployment's address with the Organization's name and a `(via ...)` suffix.
  Logged as `meshery_cloud-3299`.

- **The Organization's mail server refused the message and fallback is off.**
  The message is **dropped**, logged as `meshery_cloud-3300` at Critical. This
  is that Organization's own setting working as documented, not a fault in this
  deployment - but a dropped verification or recovery message locks a user out
  of their account, so it is worth alerting on.

- **The Organization's mail server took the whole message and never answered.**
  Delivery is unknown, so the message is deliberately **not** re-sent over the
  shared mail server - re-sending it could deliver it twice. Logged as
  `meshery_cloud-3303` at Critical.

- **The Organization's stored configuration could not be read** - a database
  read failed, or a stored password would not decrypt, usually after
  `CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` was rotated. The message takes the shared
  mail server whatever that Organization's fallback setting says, because the
  fault is this deployment's rather than a delivery policy the tenant chose.
  Logged as `meshery_cloud-3298`.

The full behavior an Organization administrator sees is documented in
[Bring Your Own Mail Server]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/org-management/bring-your-own-mail-server.md" >}}).

## Common Issues and Solutions

### 1. SMTP Configuration Errors

**Issue:** `SMTP configuration error: SMTP_HOST is empty`

**Solution:**

- Verify all SMTP environment variables are set
- Check that environment variables are properly loaded in your deployment
- Use the test endpoint to validate configuration

### 2. Authentication Failures

**Issue:** `SMTP authentication was refused by the mail server`

**Solution:**

- Verify SMTP username and password are correct
- For Gmail, use App Passwords instead of regular passwords
- Check if 2FA is enabled and properly configured

The identity that was refused and the endpoint it was presented to are in the
log's long description (`authenticating as <username> at <host:port>`), never in
the response - an SMTP username is an email address.

### 3. Template Errors

**Issue:** `Email template missing or inaccessible`

**Solution:** the templates ship inside the Layer5 Cloud image. If you built a custom image or mounted a volume over its configuration directory, restore the bundled templates, and confirm that the image tag matches the release you run.

### 4. Recipient Validation Errors

**Issue:** `Email recipient validation failed`

**Solution:**

- Verify email addresses are valid and properly formatted
- Check for empty recipient lists
- Validate email addresses contain `@` symbol
- Check for a carriage return or line feed in an address. An address carrying
  one is **refused**, not sanitized: recipient addresses are written as SMTP
  protocol verbs and into the header block, so a line break in one would start a
  header of its own. This applies to `Cc` addresses as well as `To`

Subjects are the deliberate asymmetry: a line break in a subject is stripped
rather than refused, because a subject is display text and dropping a
notification over a design name containing a newline would turn a cosmetic
problem into a lost message.

### 5. Network Connectivity Issues

**Issue:** `meshery_cloud-3302` at startup, or `dial tcp: lookup smtp.example.com: no such host`

**Solution:**

- Check network connectivity to SMTP server
- Verify egress from this cluster to the relay's submission port is allowed
- Test DNS resolution for SMTP host

No mail leaves over the shared mail server while this is outstanding, even
though the deployment started.

### 6. The Server Will Not Start After an Upgrade

**Issue:** `meshery_cloud-3301` at Error, then exit code 1.

**Solution:** the shared mail server fails one of the
[constraints](#what-is-refused). The logged cause names which screen refused it:

| Cause code | The screen that refused | What to change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| meshery_cloud-3297 | a key is unset, `SMTP_PORT` is not a number, or `SMTP_USERNAME` is not an RFC 5322 address | correct the named key |
| meshery_cloud-3262 | the host is empty, or carries whitespace or a line break | correct `SMTP_HOST` |
| meshery_cloud-3263 | the port is not a submission port, or the host resolved into internal address space | correct `SMTP_PORT`, or point `SMTP_HOST` at a publicly routable relay |
| meshery_cloud-3265 | the relay answered and does not offer STARTTLS. Only reachable on a port other than `465`, which never negotiates STARTTLS | enable STARTTLS on the relay, or move it to `465` for implicit TLS |

### 7. The Server's Certificate Is Not Trusted

**Issue:** `meshery_cloud-3304` at Error; the deployment starts.

**Solution:** the relay answered, and its certificate did not verify against the
trusted roots - it has expired, was issued for a different host name, or is
self-signed or from an issuer this server does not trust. Fix the certificate;
this is not a network fault and not something egress rules will clear. Every
send fails identically until it verifies.

## Development Mode

In development environment (`ENVIRONMENT=development`), the rendered email
content is logged **in addition to** being sent, so the body can be read without
opening the recipient's mailbox:

```log
INFO Development mode - Email details recipients=user@example.com subject="Test Email" body="<html>...</html>"
```

The message still goes out over the shared mail server, which still has to
satisfy the [constraints](#what-is-refused) above. Pointing a development
deployment at a local catch-all mailbox on port `1025` does not work.

## Error Codes Reference

| Error Code | Description | Common Causes |
|------------|-------------|---------------|
| meshery_cloud-1092 | Failed to send email | Network issues, SMTP server down |
| meshery_cloud-1144 | SMTP authentication was refused by the mail server | Invalid credentials. The refused identity and the endpoint reach the log only |
| meshery_cloud-1145 | SMTP send mail error | Server rejection, quota exceeded |
| meshery_cloud-1146 | SMTP configuration error | Missing environment variables |
| meshery_cloud-1147 | Email template missing | Template files not found |
| meshery_cloud-1148 | Email recipient validation failed | Invalid email addresses, an empty recipient list, or an address containing a carriage return or line feed |

### Mail routing and the shared mail server

These codes arrived with per-Organization mail routing in **v1.0.253**.
The four marked **send path** describe a message that belonged to an
Organization with its own mail server; the rest describe the shared mail server
this deployment configures.

| Error Code | At startup | Meaning |
|------------|------------|---------|
| meshery_cloud-3297 | cause of 3301 | The shared mail server is not usable as configured: a key is unset, `SMTP_PORT` is not a port number, or `SMTP_USERNAME` is not an address. The log names the key, never its value. The same faults are reported under this code by `/api/system/email/test` and by a send |
| meshery_cloud-3298 | send path | An Organization's mail server configuration could not be read, so the message went over the shared mail server |
| meshery_cloud-3299 | send path | A delivery over an Organization's own mail server failed. The endpoint is in the log only |
| meshery_cloud-3300 | send path | Nothing was sent: an Organization's mail server refused the message and its fallback is turned off |
| meshery_cloud-3301 | **exits** | The shared mail server fails one of the [constraints](#what-is-refused) - port, address, or no STARTTLS. The cause names which screen refused it |
| meshery_cloud-3302 | starts | DNS or the connection did not complete. Genuine unreachability only; no mail leaves over the shared mail server until it clears |
| meshery_cloud-3303 | send path | An Organization's mail server took the whole message and never acknowledged it. Recorded as uncertain and **not** re-sent, because re-sending could deliver it twice |
| meshery_cloud-3304 | starts | The shared mail server's certificate failed verification - expiry, host name or issuer. Check the certificate, not the network |

## Monitoring

Alert on the error codes in the tables above, in particular `meshery_cloud-3301`, `3302`, `3304`, `3300`, and `3303`. See [Monitoring]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/planning/monitoring.md" >}}).

## Troubleshooting Checklist

- [ ] Set `env.loglevel` to `5` for debug logging while you diagnose
- [ ] Verify all SMTP environment variables are configured
- [ ] Confirm `SMTP_PORT` is one of `25`, `465`, `587`, `2525`, and that `SMTP_USERNAME` is a full address
- [ ] Confirm `SMTP_HOST` resolves only to publicly routable addresses, and that the relay offers STARTTLS (or is on `465`)
- [ ] Read the startup log for `meshery_cloud-3301`, `-3302` or `-3304` before looking anywhere else
- [ ] Test the configuration with the Provider Admin-only `/api/system/email/test` endpoint, authenticating the request
- [ ] If only identity mail is missing, check which Kratos courier you use and, for the HTTP courier, that Kratos can reach `/api/identity/flow/emails`
- [ ] Check network connectivity to SMTP server
- [ ] Confirm the image still carries its bundled email templates
- [ ] Verify recipient email addresses are valid
- [ ] Check SMTP server logs for additional error details
- [ ] Monitor email service provider quotas and limits


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Use the Content Template Creator"
url: /cloud/academy/creating-content/using-content-template-creator/index.md
description: Register Academy content with the Content Template Creator, copy the front matter and identifiers it generates into your repository, and control who can enroll through the content's invitation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Content Template Creator is the five-step flow in the Instructor Console that registers a learning path, challenge, or certification and hands you the front matter to start writing it. One run does three things:

1. Creates the content's record in Layer5 Cloud, with status **not ready**, **public** visibility, and a generated slug.
2. Creates the invitation that governs who can enroll.
3. Generates the front matter, the content ID, and the organization ID that tie your repository files to that record.

The record is what learners enroll in, what progress and grades attach to, and what the Instructor Console reports on. The front matter is how your repository declares the same content, so the two must carry the same ID.

## Prerequisites

- The **View Academy Metrics** permission, held by Academy Admin, Organization Admin, and Provider Admin. See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).
- A workspace and a team to assign. You can type a new workspace name instead of picking an existing one. The team must already exist.
- Optional: a badge to award on completion. The Recognition step can create one.

## Run the creator

The field list, with the behavior of each field, is in [Create Academy Content]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/_index.md" >}}#register-content-in-the-console). Three details matter when you run it.

- **Team accepts one value.** The team you pick is added to the invitation, and learners join it when they enroll.
- **Access status** sets the invitation to enabled or disabled. It defaults to enabled. A disabled invitation blocks enrollment. See [How the invitation controls enrollment](#how-the-invitation-controls-enrollment).
- **Content Access End Date** sets the invitation's expiry. Leave it empty for no expiry.

![Screenshot of the Academy content creation flow in the Instructor Console](images/template-creator.png)

The creator writes the record when you advance from Recognition to Generate Template. You can go back to earlier steps and the entries you made stay in place, but advancing to the last step again creates another record with a new content ID and a new invitation. Use the ID on the final screen of your last run, and treat any earlier record as unused.

## The generated front matter

The last step shows the front matter with a copy button, followed by the content ID and your organization ID. For a certification titled "Meshery Contributors Certification", the output has this shape:

```yaml
---
type: "certification"
title: "Meshery Contributors Certification"
description: "A certification for developers who contribute to Meshery"
weight: 1
banner: "images/meshery-contributors-banner.svg"
id: "7c0f6a3e-2b1d-4c58-9d0e-5a1b2c3d4e5f"
tags: ["meshery", "kubernetes", "golang"]
categories: "open-source, cloud-native"
level: "beginner"
# competencies:
#   - title: "Domain Name"
#     percentage: 25
#     items:
#       - "Competency item 1"
# prerequisite_knowledge:
#   - title: "Prerequisite Title"
#     url: "https://example.com/resource"
#     description: "Brief description of the prerequisite"
---
A certification for developers who contribute to Meshery.
<!-- Add your Academy content here -->
```

| Key | Source | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | Content type | `learning-path`, `challenge`, or `certification`. |
| `title`, `description` | Basic Information | Also appear on the catalog card. |
| `weight` | Fixed at `1` | Change it to order the content among its siblings. |
| `banner` | Content Details | Present only when you entered a banner. The path is relative to the folder that holds the content's index file. |
| `id` | Generated | The content ID. It links your files to the record. |
| `tags`, `categories` | Content Details | Present only when you entered values. |
| `level` | The content record | Always reads `beginner` at creation, whatever difficulty you picked. Set it to `beginner`, `intermediate`, or `advanced` yourself. |
| `competencies`, `prerequisite_knowledge` | Commented samples | Uncomment and fill them in to describe what an exam covers and what learners should know first. |

Paste the output into the content's index file in your repository, inside the directory named for your organization ID. Then write the content as described in [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}).

{{< alert type="warning" title="Never change the content ID after learners enroll" >}}
Registrations, progress, grades, and certificates are recorded against the content ID. Changing the `id` in your repository orphans the existing learners' progress.
{{< /alert >}}

## How the invitation controls enrollment

Every content record created in an organization other than the provider organization has an invitation attached. Enrolling in the content accepts that invitation for the learner, and acceptance is where access is decided.

| Invitation setting | Value the creator sets | Effect on a learner who enrolls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `Academy Invitation for <slug>`, using the generated slug | Identifies the invitation in the organization's invitation list. |
| Role | Academy Learner | Assigned in the organization if the learner does not hold it. |
| Team | The team you picked | The learner is added to it if not already a member. |
| Status | Your Access status | A disabled invitation blocks enrollment. |
| Expiry | Your Content Access End Date | Checked at enrollment. Once it passes, new learners cannot enroll. Learners who already enrolled keep their role and team membership. |
| Email list | Empty | Anyone who is signed in can accept. Add exact addresses or `@domain` entries to restrict it. |
| Quota | Empty | Unlimited. A quota blocks enrollment once that many people have accepted. |

Acceptance is idempotent. A learner who accepts twice gains no duplicate membership or role, and the invitation counts them once.

When an enrollment hits a disabled, expired, full, or email-restricted invitation, the request fails with a server error. The registration is recorded before the invitation is evaluated, so the learner appears in the Learners view without having joined the organization or team. Fix the invitation, then have the learner enroll again.

You can change the team, access status, and end date later from the Curricula view of the [Instructor Console]({{< ref "cloud/academy/instructor-console-guide/index.md" >}}). Editing the invitation itself, to set a quota or restrict the email list, follows the [invitation guide]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/inviting-users/index.md" >}}). To bring in a co-instructor, create an invitation with the Academy Admin role instead of Academy Learner.

## Content owned by the provider organization

Content created while the console is scoped to all organizations belongs to the provider organization. It has no attached invitation, so enrollment accepts nothing and grants no team or role.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Assign and Manage Roles"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/managing-roles/index.md
description: Assign organization, team, and provider roles to people, remove them, and create or edit custom roles. Covers who can do each, what the server enforces, and how to confirm a change took effect.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Roles decide what a person can do in an organization. This guide covers the two jobs an administrator does with them: giving people roles (and taking roles away), and defining the roles themselves. The first is an everyday organization task. The second changes a definition shared by every organization on the deployment, so it belongs to the Provider Admin.

For how roles, keychains, and keys fit together, read the [Roles concept]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}). For the keys each built-in role holds, see [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}).

## Availability

Built-in roles are available on every plan. Custom roles are listed for the plans below, and the Provider Admin requirement applies on all of them.

{{< feature-tiers functions="Built-in Roles|Custom Roles|User-defined Roles" >}}

## Choose the scope

Every assignment has a scope, and the scope decides who may make it and which roles it accepts.

| Scope | Roles you can assign | Who assigns | The person must |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | Provider Admin, Kanvas, Curator | Provider Admin | Have an account |
| Organization | Every role except the provider roles and Anonymous User, custom roles included | Organization Admin of the organization, a holder of Assign User Roles, or Provider Admin | Be a live member of the organization, unless you are a Provider Admin |
| Team | Team Admin only | Team Admin of that team, Organization Admin or holder of Assign User Roles for a team mapped to the organization, or Provider Admin | Be a live member of the organization, unless you are a Provider Admin |

A person's permissions in an organization are the union of the roles they hold in the organization and in every team mapped into it. A Team Admin role held on one team therefore adds its keys across the organization, not only inside the team. Grant it with that reach in mind.

## What each administrator can do

| Action | Organization Admin or Assign User Roles holder | Team Admin | Provider Admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assign or remove organization roles | Yes, for members of their organization | No | Yes, in any organization |
| Assign or remove Team Admin | Yes, for teams mapped to their organization | Yes, for their own team | Yes, for any team |
| Assign or remove provider roles | No | No | Yes |
| Create or edit a custom role | No | No | Yes |
| Add or remove a keychain on a role | No | No | Yes |
| Delete a role | Not available | Not available | Not available |

Organization Admin and Provider Admin hold Assign User Roles by default. The server decides each of these by the caller's role in the scope, so holding the matching key through a custom role is not enough for the Provider Admin rows.

## Assign or change organization roles

Use this to make someone an administrator, give them workspace or academy responsibilities, or move them between roles. Open the member on the Users page and edit their roles.

1. Confirm the organization in your session is the one you mean to change. Role writes act on the selected organization.
2. Choose the complete set of roles the member should hold. The list you submit replaces the roles they hold in that scope.
3. Save. Layer5 Cloud checks every row of the request before it writes any of them.

Rules that apply to every organization role change:

| Rule | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Replace, not append | Roles you leave out are removed. An empty list removes every role in the scope and keeps the membership. |
| Membership required | The person must already be a member of the organization. A Provider Admin is exempt. An unauthorized or non-member row is skipped and reported in the result, not applied. |
| Provider roles refused | A request that names Provider Admin, Kanvas, Curator, or Anonymous User in an organization or team row is refused with HTTP 403 for every caller, a Provider Admin included, and nothing in the request is applied. |
| Unknown role | A role name that does not exist is refused with HTTP 400 and nothing is applied. |
| Role the member already holds | Accepted without change. |
| All or nothing for refusals | One refused row stops the whole request before any write. |
| Not transactional across failures | If a write fails after screening, rows written earlier in the same request stay written. Check the result. |

The role list the interface offers for organization scope is limited to Organization Admins and Provider Admins. A holder of Assign User Roles who is neither is offered an empty list, although the server accepts the assignment.

### Notify the member

A role change can email the person. The email is sent only when you ask for it in the request. A failed send is reported in the result and does not undo the role change. The welcome email option is honored only for Provider Admins.

## Assign Team Admin

Team Admin is the only role a team accepts. Assigning it sets the person's role list in that team, with the same replace behavior as organization roles. Granting it to a person who is in the organization but not yet on the team also adds them to the team, so this action can pull an organization member into a team. See [Manage Teams]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-teams/index.md" >}}) for team membership and the rest of the team lifecycle.

Each team row in a request writes only to its own team, so one request can set different roles on different teams for the same person.

## Assign provider roles

Provider roles are deployment-wide. Only a Provider Admin writes them, and they never appear in an organization or team assignment.

| Role | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Provider Admin | Administers the whole deployment and passes every permission check |
| Kanvas | Makes the Kanvas extension available when a Meshery Server connects; every new user receives it at sign-up |
| Curator | Manages catalog content |

A request from anyone else that includes provider roles skips those rows and reports `<email> unauthorized to assign provider roles`. This message also appears in the result of ordinary organization role changes made by a non-Provider-Admin, because the provider portion of the request is skipped for them. It is expected and does not indicate that the organization change failed.

Layer5 Cloud does not guard the last Provider Admin. A Provider Admin can remove the Provider Admin role from every Provider Admin, themselves included. Confirm another Provider Admin exists first.

## Remove roles

To remove roles, assign the set the person should keep. Removing every role in a scope leaves the member in the organization or team with no role in that scope; their membership and their other scopes are unchanged. To end a person's access to an organization altogether, remove them from it instead: see [Manage Users]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#remove-a-user-from-an-organization" >}}).

Layer5 Cloud does not stop you removing the last Organization Admin or the last Team Admin. An organization's owner keeps administrator access through ownership, so the owner cannot lock themselves out. Anyone else can. Confirm a second administrator holds the role before you remove it from the first.

## Confirm the change

A role write answers with HTTP 200 and a JSON array of strings. An empty array means every row was applied. Each string is a row that was skipped or a step that failed, for example `<email> unauthorized to assign org roles` or `role assigned:role change notification failed`.

The Users page reports success whenever the answer is 200, so it does not display the strings. After a role change, check the member's roles in the Users table, and for automation read the array. The audit trail records each change as `<actor> assigned roles: [<names>] to <person>` or `<actor> removed roles for <person>`.

## Create a custom role

**Needs:** Provider Admin.

A custom role is a name, a description, and a set of keychains. It holds keychains, not individual keys, so build it from the [keychains]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}) that already group the permissions you want.

| Field | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Name | At most 50 characters. The server checks no other rule: an empty name is not rejected up front, and a duplicate name is accepted. |
| Description | Free text. |
| Keychains | Chosen from the deployment's keychains. |

Creating a role is two steps: the role is saved, then each keychain is attached. The interface reports "Role created" as soon as the first step succeeds, and it does not report a failure in the second. Open the role afterward and confirm the keychains listed are the ones you chose.

Consider these before you create one:

- **Roles are global.** A custom role appears in the role list of every organization on the deployment, not only the one you were working in.
- **Use unique names.** Layer5 Cloud resolves a role by its name when you assign it, and it does not enforce uniqueness. Two roles with the same name make assignment ambiguous.
- **A custom role is assigned at organization scope.** Teams accept only Team Admin, and the provider roles are fixed.
- **On hosted Layer5 Cloud, an organization cannot create a custom role.** The Provider Admin of a self-hosted deployment creates them for that deployment.

## Edit a role or its keychains

**Needs:** Provider Admin.

You can rename a role, change its description, and add or remove keychains. Every change applies to every person who holds the role in every organization at once, built-in roles included.

- The interface refuses to edit Provider Admin, Kanvas, and Curator. The server does not distinguish them from other roles, so do not rely on the interface for protection when you automate.
- Renaming a role changes the name that assignment looks up. Existing holders keep the role, and later assignments must use the new name.
- To change what people in one organization can do without changing a shared role, change which roles they hold in that organization.

Only a Provider Admin can attach or detach keychains. Organization Admins and Team Admins cannot, whatever keys their roles hold.

## Delete a role

Layer5 Cloud has no way to delete a role. The delete control on the Roles page is disabled. To retire a role, remove it from every member who holds it and stop assigning it. A retired role cannot be granted again once it is soft-deleted in the database, but no operation in the product soft-deletes one today.

## Failure reference

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 403 `You do not hold the permission this action requires in this organization` | The route needs a key you do not hold in the organization of your session | Switch organization or ask an administrator who holds it |
| HTTP 403 with a provider role named | A provider role was submitted in an organization or team row | Remove the provider role from the row; assign provider roles separately as a Provider Admin |
| HTTP 403 for a non-Team-Admin role in a team row | Teams accept only Team Admin | Assign the other role at organization scope |
| HTTP 400 for an unknown role | The role name does not exist, or it was renamed | List roles and use the current name |
| 200 with `unauthorized to assign org roles` or `team roles` | You lack authority for that member or team, or the member is not in the organization | Add the member to the organization first, or ask an administrator with authority |
| 200 with `error: ... assign provider roles` after an organization change | A write failed and earlier rows may already be written | Re-read the member's roles and resubmit the full set |
| Custom role created without its keychains | An attach step failed and the interface did not report it | Edit the role and attach the keychains again |

## Related

- [Manage Users]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md" >}}) - add, remove, and edit members.
- [Manage Teams]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-teams/index.md" >}}) - team membership and Team Admin.
- [Roles]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) - the model behind scope and keys.
- [Keychains]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains.md" >}}) - what a custom role is built from.
- [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) - keys held by each built-in role.
- [Security Reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md" >}}) - key holders and responses for role routes.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Extend the Academy"
url: /cloud/academy/creating-content/extending-the-academy/index.md
description: Go beyond plain Markdown in your Academy content with inline HTML and CSS, organization-specific Hugo shortcodes, embedded Kanvas designs, and branded award emails.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Academy content is Markdown in your organization's Git repository, built with Hugo into your organization's Academy. Markdown covers most lessons. When a lesson needs a custom layout, a reusable component, or a live design, you extend the content in your own repository without touching the shared theme.

This page covers what you can extend and the limits of each extension. It assumes a working content repository. If you do not have one yet, start with [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}).

## Availability

Publishing your own Academy content is an Enterprise-tier capability. Your organization also needs an Academy configuration from Layer5 before it can publish. Without one, the Instructor Console shows its "not configured" state and the extensions below have nowhere to deploy. See [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) for who can use the console.

## What you can extend

| Extension | Where it lives | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline HTML and CSS | Your Markdown pages | The page that contains it |
| Custom shortcode | `layouts/shortcodes/<organization-id>/` in your repository | Every page in your organization's content |
| Embedded Kanvas design | A shortcode in your page | The page that contains it |
| Branded award emails | Organization settings in Layer5 Cloud | Every badge and certificate email your organization sends |

You cannot replace the theme's layouts, archetypes, or site-wide styles from a content repository. You can customize shortcodes only. Request theme changes through the theme's issue tracker.

## Keep your files in your organization's directory

Each organization's files live under a directory named for its organization ID, which the Template Creator shows on its final step. The Academy build keeps organizations apart by that directory name, so content or shortcodes placed outside it are not part of your Academy. Use the same ID for the content directory and for the shortcode directory.

## Mix HTML and CSS with Markdown

Markdown pages accept raw HTML. Use it for layout that Markdown cannot express, such as columns, callout boxes, or styled tables.

```markdown
## Why this matters

Standard **Markdown** works above and below the block.

<div class="lesson-note" style="padding: 1rem; border-left: 4px solid #00b39f;">
  <strong>Note:</strong> Use inline HTML for one-off layout.
</div>
```

Leave a blank line between a raw HTML block and the Markdown that follows it. Without the blank line, Hugo does not parse the next Markdown element and it renders as literal text. Markdown inside an HTML element is parsed only when blank lines separate it from the tags, so write short content inside HTML elements in HTML.

Style with inline `style` attributes, with CSS classes you define in a shortcode's `<style>` block, or with the theme's existing classes. Inline styles apply to one element. CSS in a shortcode applies wherever the shortcode renders.

## Create a custom shortcode

A shortcode is a reusable template that takes parameters and returns HTML. Define it once and call it from any page in your organization's content.

1. Create the template at `layouts/shortcodes/<organization-id>/callout.html` in your content repository.

   ```html
   <style>
   .org-callout {
     padding: 1rem;
     margin: 1rem 0;
     border-left: 4px solid #00b39f;
   }
   </style>
   <div class="org-callout">
     <strong>{{ .Get "title" | default "Note" }}:</strong> {{ .Inner }}
   </div>
   ```

2. Call it from a page by its file name, without the extension. The tags below are escaped for display. Write them as `{{</* callout title="Heads up" */>}}` and `{{</* /callout */>}}`.

   ```markdown
   {{</* callout title="Heads up" */>}}
   Back up the design before you scale it down.
   {{</* /callout */>}}
   ```

Hugo reads `{{ .Get "title" }}` as a named parameter and `{{ .Inner }}` as the content between the opening and closing tags. A shortcode written without a closing tag cannot use `.Inner`. The Academy supports the full Hugo shortcode feature set. See the [Hugo shortcode documentation](https://gohugo.io/content-management/shortcodes/).

{{< alert type="info" title="Name collisions" >}}
Choose names that do not match a shortcode the theme already provides. Use a prefix that is specific to your organization.
{{< /alert >}}

## Embed a Kanvas design

The Academy renders live Kanvas designs inside a lesson with the `meshery-design-embed` shortcode, so learners inspect a real topology instead of a screenshot. See the publishing diagram in [Create a Learning Path]({{< ref "cloud/academy/creating-content/creating-your-learning-path/index.md" >}}#publish) for a working embed.

## Award emails

When a learner earns a badge or a certificate, Layer5 Cloud sends an email on behalf of your organization. Both messages draw their branding from your organization's settings, including your logo, colors, and contact links. See [White-label Layer5 Cloud]({{< ref "cloud/guides/self-hosted/white-labeling/_index.md" >}}) for how to set them.

| | Badge email | Certificate email |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sent when | A badge is awarded | The learner passes the final assessment of content that defines a certificate |
| Subject | Names the organization that awarded the badge | Congratulations on receiving your certificate title certificate from organization name |
| Recipient | The learner | The learner, addressed by first and last name |
| Learner can turn it off | Yes, through the badge assignment and updates notification preference | No |
| Links | Learner's public profile | The certificate's public page on your organization's Academy |

The certificate link points to your organization's custom domain when one is set. Otherwise it points to the deployment's base address. If the branding settings cannot be read when the email is sent, the email still goes out with default branding. A failure to send the certificate email is logged and does not undo the completion or the certificate.

Anonymous users never receive a badge email.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Keychains"
url: /cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keychains/index.md
description: How keychains group keys into reusable bundles for roles in Layer5 Cloud, who owns and can change a keychain, and what a change to a keychain affects.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A keychain is a named bundle of keys. It sits between the single permission and the role a person holds:

- A [key]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}) allows one action, such as Create Token.
- A keychain groups related keys, such as everything needed to manage teams.
- A [role]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) groups keychains, and users hold roles in an organization or team.

A user's effective keys in an organization are the union of the keys in every keychain of every role the user holds there. A keychain grants nothing by itself. It takes effect only through a role that includes it.

## Why keychains exist

Keychains make permissions reusable. Many roles need the same set of keys: every default user role, for example, needs to view tokens, sessions, keys, and keychains. Instead of attaching those keys to each role one by one, Layer5 Cloud puts them in one keychain and includes that keychain in each role. The same keychain can belong to many roles, and a role can include many keychains.

Reuse also means one change propagates. Adding a key to a keychain grants it to every role that includes the keychain, and removing a key withdraws it from all of them at once.

## Keychains are defined for the whole deployment

Keys, keychains, and roles are records of the whole Layer5 Cloud deployment, not copies inside each organization. What is scoped to an organization is the role assignment. As a result, a change to a keychain, or to the keychains a role includes, applies to every user who holds an affected role in every organization. [Roles]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md#changing-a-role-changes-it-everywhere" >}}) explains this from the role side.

## Default keychains

Layer5 Cloud ships 30 default keychains, each grouping the keys for one area. The system account owns them. Representative examples:

| Keychain | What it groups |
|---|---|
| User View | Viewing keys every user needs, including View Tokens, View Sessions, View Keys, and View Keychains |
| User Management | Managing users and their roles |
| Team Management | Managing teams and team membership |
| Organization Management | Managing organizations, their teams, and their users |
| Security Management | Token administration, including Create Token, Delete Token, and Download Token |
| Provider Management | Deployment administration, including Edit Key, Delete Key, Create Keychain, Edit Keychain, Delete Keychain, and Assign Keychains to Roles |

The remaining default keychains cover workspaces, environments, the catalog, lifecycle actions, extensions, settings, performance, views, collaboration, infrastructure, curation, the Academy, events, and the Kanvas action sets. The [Roles and Permissions reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) lists them and shows which roles hold which keys.

Only a Provider Admin can change a default keychain, as with every other keychain. See [Who can change a keychain](#who-can-change-a-keychain).

## Custom keychains

A Provider Admin can create keychains beyond the defaults. The Provider Admin who creates a keychain is recorded as its owner, and a custom keychain appears only in its owner's keychain list. Other administrators, including other Provider Admins, do not see it in their list, although any Provider Admin can still change or delete it on the server. Ownership only decides that list: it grants no right to change the keychain. A custom keychain does not belong to an organization.

## Who can change a keychain

Keychains and their assignment to roles apply across the whole provider, not to one organization. Only a Provider Admin can create, edit, or delete a keychain, add or remove its keys, or include it in a role or remove it from one. This is the rule as of Layer5 Cloud **v1.0.280**.

Layer5 Cloud enforces keychain operations in two places. The interface enables or disables each control based on the keys you hold. The server checks the matching key and then confirms that the caller holds the Provider Admin role for the whole deployment. Holding the Provider Admin role inside one organization does not satisfy that check.

| Operation | Who can do it | Where it is enforced |
|---|---|---|
| View the keychain list and a keychain's keys | Anyone holding View Keychains, which every default user role holds through User View. The list shows system-owned keychains and the viewer's own. | Interface: the Keychains tab requires View Keychains. Server: returns only system-owned keychains and the caller's own. |
| Create a keychain | Provider Admin. The interface also requires Create Keychain. | Server and interface |
| Rename a keychain, add keys, remove keys | Provider Admin. The interface also requires Edit Keychain. | Server and interface |
| Delete a keychain | Provider Admin. The interface also requires Delete Keychain. | Server and interface |
| Include a keychain in a role, or remove it | Provider Admin | Server |

When the server refuses a change to a keychain, it answers HTTP 403 with a JSON error. A caller who lacks the route's key receives code `meshery_cloud-1108`. A caller who holds the key without being a Provider Admin for the whole deployment receives code `meshery_cloud-3336`, "Only a Provider Admin can change roles, keychains or permission keys".

{{< alert title="Note" >}}
Create Keychain, Edit Keychain, Delete Keychain, and Assign Keychains to Roles belong to the Provider Management keychain, so by default only Provider Admins see these controls enabled. Everyone else can still view keychains.
{{< /alert >}}

## A keychain takes effect only through a role

Creating a keychain changes no one's permissions. The keychain grants its keys only when a role includes it, and including it in a role changes that role for every holder in every organization.

Creating and editing roles is a Provider Admin action on the server. On hosted Layer5 Cloud, Layer5 operates the Provider Admin role, so an organization cannot build its own custom role from custom keychains. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator's Provider Admins can create custom keychains and the custom roles that use them. To give people a role, see [Roles]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) and [Users]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/users/_index.md" >}}).

## What changes take effect, and when

- **Deleting a keychain** removes its key mappings, so the keychain stops granting anything immediately, in every role that included it.
- **Removing a key from a keychain** stops that key flowing to every role that includes the keychain.
- **Adding a key to a keychain** grants it to every holder of every role that includes the keychain.

Authorization is evaluated on every request, so users gain or lose access on their next action, without signing in again.

## Change keychains deliberately

Default roles carry the default keychains, and every new user receives a default role. A change to a default keychain therefore changes permissions for users across the deployment, regardless of organization. Leave default keychains as shipped unless that is the intended outcome. On a self-hosted deployment, to grant a different combination of keys, a Provider Admin creates a new keychain and includes it in a new role, and then the role is assigned to the users who need it. Keychains and roles are shared by every organization, so per-organization differences come from which roles a user holds in that organization.

The [custom keychains guide]({{< ref "cloud/guides/security/custom-keychains.md" >}}) covers creating, editing, and deleting a keychain and including it in a role. To browse keychains in your account, open [Keychains](https://cloud.layer5.io/security/keychains) in Layer5 Cloud.

## Related

- [Keys]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}) - the individual permissions and how they are enforced.
- [Roles]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/roles/_index.md" >}}) - how roles bundle keychains and who assigns them.
- [Roles and Permissions]({{< ref "cloud/reference/default-permissions.md" >}}) - the default roles, keychains, and keys.
- [Security reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md" >}}) - security permissions, token and session lifetimes, and endpoints.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Review Access Requests"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/access-requests/index.md
description: Review, approve, and deny signup requests for product access, and learn what an approval or a denial changes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An access request is a person asking for access to a Layer5 product capability, such as Kanvas. Layer5 Cloud collects these as **signup requests** in a queue. A Provider Admin reviews the queue, then approves or denies each request. Approval grants the requester Kanvas access and, for someone without an account, creates one.

This guide covers who can review requests, what the queue shows, and exactly what approval and denial do. It describes the queue that ships today. Layer5 Cloud has no general request flow for access to a specific design, workspace, or environment, and a denial does not restrict any resource. See [What this does not cover](#what-this-does-not-cover).

## Who can review requests

Reviewing requests is a **Provider Admin** capability. Provider Admin is a deployment-wide role, so Organization Admins cannot review or decide requests.

| Task | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| Open the User Requests page | The View All Access Requests permission, held by Provider Admin |
| Approve a request | Accept Access Request, held by Provider Admin |
| Deny a request | Deny Access Request, held by Provider Admin |
| Approve or deny from a notification link | Signed in as a Provider Admin |

Anyone who is signed in can file a request. Filing needs no role.

## How requests arrive

A signed-in person files a request from the Playground card on their dashboard. The request is stored with the person's name and email, a form type, a status, and a task link. A request filed this way carries placeholder values that appear as-is in the queue: form type `Cloud`, organization `Cloud org`, occupation `Cloud user`, a placeholder task link, and a role taken from the person's first role or `cloud user`.

A new account receives the Kanvas (`meshmap`) role at its first sign-in, so the queue matters mainly for existing accounts that do not hold it.

A request needs an email, a first name, a last name, and a valid task link. A request that omits one is refused with a message naming the missing field. Creating a request sends no email or notification.

## Review the queue

The User Requests page lists requests with these columns: ID, name, last name, email, occupation, organization, role, form type, status, task ID, task, and created time. Processed rows are shaded.

| Control | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Default view | Pending requests only. |
| Status filter | Pending, Approved, or Denied. |
| Form type filter | Meshmap, Docker Extension, Playground, or Event. Requests filed from the dashboard card are stored with form type `Cloud` and are not reachable through this filter. Find them with search or by clearing the form type filter. |
| Search | Case-insensitive substring over first name, last name, email, organization, and task link. |
| Order | By created time or updated time. |

## Approve a request

Approval acts only on a request whose status is **pending**. Layer5 Cloud then:

1. Looks for an existing account with the request's email address.
2. **If an account exists,** adds the `meshmap` role to it. Roles the account already holds stay in place. The person receives a role-change email.
3. **If no account exists,** creates one with the request's name and email, marks the email verified, and sets the account up so the person can sign in.
4. Saves the status as approved.
5. Sends the request to the deployment's signup-request webhook, which notifies the requester and updates the request's tracking task.
6. Records an event: `<admin email> approved signup request for <email>`.

Approval has no confirmation step. If the webhook call fails, the status stays saved and you see the failure, so the request does not return to pending.

A request with form type `epsma-book` skips steps 1 to 3: approval only records the status and sends the notification.

## Deny a request

Denial asks for confirmation. It sets the status to denied, sends the same webhook notification, and records an event: `<admin email> denied signup request for <email>`.

Denial removes nothing. It does not remove a role or an account, and it does not restrict any resource. It closes the request.

## Approve or deny from a link

Notification links open the decision directly. The link requires a Provider Admin session: if you are signed out, you are sent to sign in and returned to the page. A person who is not a Provider Admin receives `Forbidden`. If the request is no longer pending, you are sent to the User Requests page with a notice that it was previously processed, and nothing changes.

Opening one of these links changes the request. Treat them like a button, and do not open them to preview.

## Outcomes and errors

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The request is not pending | `signup request for <email> previously processed`. Nothing changes. |
| The request id is unknown | `unable to get signup request`. |
| The caller is not a Provider Admin | `Forbidden`. |
| Approval cannot create the account | `cannot create account at the moment`, with the cause from the identity provider. |
| The webhook call fails | An error is shown and an alert event is recorded. The status is already saved. |

Statuses are `pending`, `approved`, and `denied`. A processed request cannot be decided again.

## What this does not cover

- **Resource access requests.** A request for access to a specific design, workspace, environment, or other resource, approved by its owner, does not exist. The queue covers product signup requests only.
- **Restricting access.** Layer5 Cloud has no action that restricts a person's access to a requested resource. To limit what someone can do, change their [roles]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#change-a-members-roles" >}}) or [remove them from the organization]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/managing-users/index.md#remove-a-user-from-an-organization" >}}).
- **Catalog publishing.** Requests to publish a design to the catalog use a separate approval queue.
- **Joining an organization.** To let people join your organization, use [invitations]({{< ref "cloud/guides/organizations/inviting-users/index.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Sessions"
url: /cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/sessions/index.md
description: How long a Layer5 Cloud sign-in lasts, what ends it, how the browser stores it, and how sessions differ from API tokens.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A session is the credential Layer5 Cloud issues each time someone signs in. It is what keeps a browser tab, a second device, or a connected Meshery Server signed in, and it is what you end when you want one of those sign-ins to stop working. Sessions expire on their own; API tokens do not.

## One session per sign-in

Every sign-in creates its own session. Each browser, device, and Meshery Server that signs in through Layer5 Cloud holds a separate session with its own expiry, and any number of them can be active at once. Ending one session leaves the others untouched.

A session acts as the user who signed in. What it can do in an organization is whatever the roles that user holds there allow, checked on every request. See [Keys]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/keys.md" >}}) for how roles grant permissions.

Users see their own sessions on the [Sessions](https://cloud.layer5.io/security/sessions) tab of the Security page, which lists each session's ID, name, purpose, and creation date. The tab requires the View Sessions key, which every default user role holds. The list shows no device, browser, or location for a session.

## How long a session lasts

These are the Layer5 Cloud deployment defaults. Operators of a self-hosted deployment can change them.

| Credential | Default lifetime | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Access token | 24 hours | The browser session ends when it lapses. Activity in the interface does not extend it, so a browser user signs in again after 24 hours. |
| Refresh token | 1000 hours (about 41 days) | Clients such as Meshery Server use it to obtain a new access token. Each refresh token works once; every refresh issues a new one. A failed refresh returns an error. |
| Privileged-action window | Set by the deployment; 15 minutes in the packaged default | Sensitive actions, such as profile changes, ask you to authenticate again once this window has passed since sign-in. |

Anonymous Kanvas use, without signing in, lasts 24 hours and does not appear on the Sessions tab.

## What ends a session

A session ends in one of three ways:

- **Expiry.** The access token lapses at its lifetime, as described above.
- **Logout from the Sessions tab.** The session's token is revoked immediately; the next request that presents it fails. The action records the same audit event as deleting a token.
- **Signing out of the app.** Signing out ends the browser's identity session and revokes its stored grant.

Changing your password does not end your other sessions. Layer5 Cloud has no sign-out-everywhere action and no idle timeout setting. To end your other sessions, log each one out from the Sessions tab. [Review and sign out sessions]({{< ref "cloud/guides/security/sessions.md" >}}) covers the task.

{{< alert type="info" title="Who can use Logout" >}}
The Logout action on the Sessions tab requires the Delete Token key, which only Organization Admins and Provider Admins hold by default. Users, Team Admins, and Workspace Admins see Logout disabled, even though their roles hold the Logout from a Session key. Layer5 Cloud lets each user log out only their own sessions; no role can end another user's session from this tab.
{{< /alert >}}

## How the browser stores a session

The browser keeps the session in a cookie that page scripts cannot read (HttpOnly), that is sent only over HTTPS, and that uses SameSite Lax, so other sites cannot send it along with their own requests except on ordinary top-level navigation. A second, companion cookie tells the interface that a session exists. It carries no secret and lapses with the session.

The cookie's scope depends on how the organization signs users in:

- **Platform sign-in provider.** The cookie is shared across the platform's hosts, so one sign-in covers them.
- **Organization's own identity provider, or a custom domain outside the platform's domain.** The cookie is host-only and is never sent to any other host.

See [Organizations]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/organizations/_index.md" >}}) for how custom domains and identity providers decide where a user signs in.

## Sessions and API tokens

Sessions and API tokens both authenticate as you, and Layer5 Cloud revokes them through the same mechanism. They differ in how they start and how long they live.

| | Session | API token |
|---|---|---|
| Created by | Signing in from a browser, device, or Meshery Server | Creating it on the Tokens tab with a name and purpose |
| Lifetime | 24-hour access token, renewable by clients for up to about 41 days | No expiry |
| Ended by | Expiry, Logout on the Sessions tab, or signing out | Deleting it on the Tokens tab |
| Used for | Interactive use and connected Meshery Servers | Scripts and API clients sending a Bearer token |

The Tokens tab never lists sessions, and the Sessions tab never lists API tokens. See [Tokens]({{< ref "cloud/concepts/identity-and-security/tokens.md" >}}) for how API tokens behave.

## What Layer5 Cloud does not offer

- No organization-level session policy. Lifetimes are set for the whole deployment.
- No idle timeout setting in the product interface.
- No device, browser, or location detail on a session.
- No action that ends every session at once.

The [security reference]({{< ref "cloud/reference/security.md" >}}) lists the session keys, default lifetimes, and cookie attributes in one place.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Recognize Members with Badges"
url: /cloud/guides/organizations/assigning-user-badges/index.md
description: Create recognitions for your organization, award them to members, and let members share them from their public profile.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A **recognition** is a badge that an organization defines and awards to its members. Recognitions mark milestones such as completing training, contributing to a project, or reaching a team goal. An awarded badge appears on the recipient's public profile, where the recipient can share it.

Two kinds of badges exist, and they come from different places:

- **Organization recognitions** are created and awarded by an organization's administrators. This guide covers them.
- **Layer5 community badges** belong to the Layer5 community recognition program. Browse them in the [Badge Gallery](https://badges.layer5.io) and read how they are earned in the [Recognition section of the Layer5 Community Handbook](https://layer5.io/community/handbook/recognition).

## Who can do what

| Task | What it needs |
| --- | --- |
| Create, edit, or delete a recognition | The **Manage Recognitions** permission in the organization that owns the recognition. Organization Admin, Provider Admin, and Academy Admin hold it by default. The **Manage Recognitions** control on the Organizations page is enabled for holders of **Edit Organization**. |
| Award a recognition to a member | The permission to update that member's profile, held in an organization you share with the member. |
| View a badge | Anyone who can open the recipient's public profile. |

Two limits apply to every award:

- **You cannot award a badge to yourself.** Layer5 Cloud refuses the request with a 403 error, including for a Provider Admin. A badge is a public claim about what its holder completed, so someone else must grant it.
- **The recipient is notified**, and an event records who awarded which badge to whom.

## Create a recognition

Open **Manage Recognitions** from the Organizations page to see every recognition and to create, edit, or delete the ones your organization owns.

Each recognition follows these rules:

- **The name must contain at least one letter or number.**
- **The label must be unique.** A label that another organization has already reserved is refused with a 409 conflict. Choose a different name.
- **Ownership is fixed.** A recognition belongs to the organization where it was created. You can edit or delete it only while that organization is selected. A recognition owned by another organization stays visible in the list, but its edit and delete controls are disabled, with the message that it belongs to another organization.

The recognition list itself is not private. The recognition catalog read is unauthenticated and not scoped to an organization, so any recognition's name and label can be read by anyone. Do not put sensitive text in a recognition's name or description.

## Award a recognition

Administrators award a recognition to one member at a time, or set a member's full badge list from the member's profile editor. Both paths apply the same rules: the recipient is never the person awarding, and the awarder needs permission to update the recipient's profile.

Some badges are awarded automatically. Completing an Academy quiz awards the badge tied to that quiz. Layer5 Cloud awards no other badge automatically.
